title: Android access by feature
text:
# Android access by feature

Read automationStatus.deviceAccess.requirements for this package's actual setup, nativeDataStatus for provider grants/columns, and tools/list for implemented commands. A manifest declaration, Lua policy, network connection or permission notification is not a grant. Release/debug packages have independent grants.

- Home/public files need shared-storage access. Other file paths use Android app-UID access.
- Contacts/calendar operations need their declared read/write grants and supported resource fields. Synced-account rules apply.
- SMS history, receive and send have corresponding grants; SIM inventory can need phone-state access. No default SMS role. Calls, history and USSD need their own phone grants and platform eligibility.
- Clipboard reads can be foreground-restricted.
- Notifications/media-session access needs the notification listener; posting and Do Not Disturb access are separate.
- Cross-app UI needs Accessibility. Actual-display capture additionally needs Android11+; secure windows remain protected. Device Administration enables lockDevice.
- Ordinary sensors can work without runtime access; restricted sensors report their own requirement/reason. Health Connect daily steps needs that provider's read consent.
- Location needs appropriate precision/providers, and background access where used. Geocoding can send queries/coordinates to its provider. GNSS observation is not a location fix.
- Camera/microphone need grants, foreground eligibility and exclusive hardware ownership. PCM can continue behind another app under its microphone foreground service. Bounded recording, recognition and video have their documented foreground restrictions.
- TTS needs an installed engine; network-required voices/system recognition can contact a provider. Strict onDevice recognition never falls back.
- Bluetooth needs the applicable scan/connect/location access and enabled radio. Wi-Fi scans need location/services and remain throttled.
- NFC needs enabled hardware, foreground unlocked Dikciz and a compatible presented tag. USB host needs owner approval for the attached peripheral.
- Settings writes need Modify system settings and the allowlist. APK install needs source approval and Android confirmation where required.
- root:false shell runs as the app, not adb shell. Root defaults true and needs approved su. There is no silent fallback or Shizuku backend.

Use requirementId from discovery with requestDeviceAccess or autoRequestPermissions:true on an ordinary command. Inspect permissionRequest; tell the owner to review the phone, check grants again and explicitly retry. Full device access setup opens its own resumable task.

File APIs protect remote-auth.json, .bak/.new and canonical aliases, plus ancestor move/delete. An independent app-UID/root shell is not sandboxed by file-command restrictions. Enabled scripts/widgets have owner command authority; the returned-action policy does not sandbox context.request.

Native commands share all ordinary bindings. Network shellStream push is transport-only; shell sessions, event journal and PCM use shared cursor reads with bounded process memory. Durable jobs persist results and never replay interrupted work. Activity restart preserves the process; APK update/process death loses memory histories.

[Permissions](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions), [Security](dikciz://docs/guides/security), [Hardware](dikciz://docs/guides/hardware). Full feature map: https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/blob/main/docs/android-access.md
aliases: Android privileges root permissions accessibility notification listener device administration

title: Typed actions: apps, media and messages
text:
# Typed actions: apps, media and messages

Read [dispatch basics](dikciz://docs/guides/actions-state). Every record has type. Lua policy.actions uses the same name except setMediaVolume uses mediaVolume.

- launchApp requires component, a flattened Android component. Check activityLaunches. Accepted launch is not foreground verification.
- appAction requires component and action: launch, appInfo, uninstall or forceStop. Typed actions refuse addShortcut. Force stop needs approved root.
- postNotification requires title and text within configured title/text limits. Android posting access applies.
- sendSms requires dialable recipient (max20chars) and body within configured text limits. Legacy submission only; Android can show confirmation or rate-limit it. Android can persist a non-default app's sent SMS. Prefer ordinary smsSend/smsStatus for SIM choice, durable idempotency and receipts.
- explicitIntent requires intentType activity/broadcast and component; optional action. This typed form has no data URI. Use the ordinary intent command for its broader schema.
- mediaControl requires packageName and command: play, pause, playPause, skipNext, skipPrevious or seekTo. Only seekTo requires/allows positionMilliseconds (integer0..86400000). Notification-listener access is required.
- setMediaVolume requires levelPercent (integer0..100). Policy capability is mediaVolume, not setMediaVolume. Results/logs may use mediaVolume as the capability name.
- notificationControl requires an unexpired plain actionToken from notificationsList. Use ordinary notificationManage for inline reply, dismiss or snooze.
- lockDevice has no extra fields. Owner-enabled Device Administration is required.

Volume example:
~~~json
{"type":"setMediaVolume","levelPercent":35}
~~~

Lua returns that record under actions and its policy allows "actions":["mediaVolume"]. The percentage maps to discrete Android media-volume indices; it is not sound pressure. Read deviceState.mediaVolume/mediaVolumeMaximum before/after. Per-player audioPlayback.volumePercent is a separate gain setting. Fixed volume or rejected read-back is an explicit outcome.

None of these actions silently grants Android access. Message submission is not delivery, notification invocation is not remote application success, and a dispatch array is not transactional. Only perform external effects the owner requested.

[UI actions](dikciz://docs/guides/actions-ui), [Tracked SMS](dikciz://docs/recipes/contact-sms), [Audio](dikciz://docs/guides/audio).
aliases: device control intent launch application volume flashlight vibration speech

title: Typed actions: state and events
text:
# Typed actions: state and events

Actions differ from ordinary commands. HTML uses dikciz.dispatch({actions}); MCP uses dikciz_automation_dispatch; HTTP/WebSocket use automationDispatch. Network dispatch requires an existing HTML sourceWidgetAddress. Arrays contain 1..8 actions and execute in order without rollback. Inspect each outcome. Lua returns {status="...",actions={...}} and needs enabled subscription/event capability plus policy.actions for each returned action.

Every record has type. Required fields:
- selectPage: pageId.
- patchWidget: widgetAddress and values.
- patchState: values object. Replaces current script state in Lua, source widget state in HTML/network dispatch.
- patchDom: widgetAddress, selector (max512 chars) and values.
- emitEvent: event (valid custom name) and payload object; optional coalescingKey.

Policy names match these types. Saved state replacement is not a merge. Preserve prior keys when needed. JSON null is a saved value, not key deletion; Lua nil omits a key.

For HTML, JSON patchWidget values support title, html, css, javascript, state, itemStates and eventSubscriptions, at most6 fields. The parser accepts text for compatible text targets. Layout is not a patch field. eventSubscriptions replaces the full array, at most128 entries, using the saved-configuration validator. widgetGet returns the current list. Lua returned patchWidget accepts at most5 fields and no itemStates or eventSubscriptions. Use context.request with automationDispatch and an actual HTML source address for the JSON contract, or edit the saved widget record.

patchDom values: text, html, value, className and string-valued attributes (max16). DOM changes are transient. Saved source changes can recreate the WebView. Long press opens whole-widget controls; native Delete removes the entire WebView and owned files.

Enabled Lua context.request and HTML command calls have owner authority subject to Android access. The returned-action policy is not a command sandbox. Keep event handlers' journal reads nonblocking.

[Device actions](dikciz://docs/guides/actions-device), [UI actions](dikciz://docs/guides/actions-ui), [Events](dikciz://docs/guides/events). Full reference: https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/blob/main/docs/typed-actions.md
aliases: automation dispatch state event trigger battery network time conditions

title: Typed actions: Accessibility
text:
# Typed actions: Accessibility

Read [dispatch basics](dikciz://docs/guides/actions-state). Owner-enabled Dikciz Accessibility is required. Every record has type; Lua policy action names match these types.

- accessibilityAction: snapshotId, nodeId and action; optional text. Supported actions: click, longClick, focus, clearFocus, scrollForward, scrollBackward, setText and select. setText requires text. Derive nodeId from a fresh accessibilitySnapshot.
- accessibilityGesture: snapshotId, gesture and durationMilliseconds. tap requires x/y; swipe requires startX/startY/endX/endY. Coordinates are integer0..10000; duration integer1..10000ms. Use observed node bounds, not guessed positions.
- accessibilityGlobalAction: action is back, home, recents, notifications, quickSettings, lockScreen or takeScreenshot. Android version and system support apply; global actions do not take a snapshotId.

Node/gesture snapshots expire after five seconds and window changes invalidate them. A refused snapshot is not permission to act on replacement content. Read the resulting screen after an accepted action.

Lua receives context.accessibility only with an accessibilityWindow event. Its service-lifecycle event has no window tree. HTML can request the ordinary snapshot and dispatch the same action fields. A returned Lua action uses its table parser; HTML/network dispatch uses the JSON parser; both feed the common native runtime.

displayScreenshot is the separate ordinary command returning actual image bytes through every binding. Accessibility takeScreenshot asks Android to take a screenshot; it does not replace that image-returning API. Launcher screenshot captures its own window. Secure windows and system limits still apply.

[UI](dikciz://docs/guides/ui), [Permissions](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions). Full guide: https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/blob/main/docs/automation-control.md#cross-app-android-ui
aliases: tap click swipe scroll accessibility input text key screen interaction

title: Public Android SDK
text:
# Public Android SDK

Prefer dedicated native commands when they cover the task. The SDK bridge adds exact public Android overloads through the same executor on every binding. The pinned catalogue is API 36; discovery is not a permission grant or proof every API runs on this phone.

1. Call dikciz_android_api_discover. Omit className for classes, or set an exact name for members and inherited overloads. query is a literal filter. Follow hasMore with offset plus returned item count.
2. Inspect bridgePermitted, runtimeAvailable, parameters, nullability and permission annotations. Copy the exact member ID. Never guess an overload.
3. Use dikciz_android_api_read for approved reads. Other calls require dikciz_android_api_invoke and a unique idempotencyKey. The arguments array is required, including [].

Example read arguments:

```json
{"className":"android.os.BatteryManager","member":"getIntProperty(int)","target":"service:batterymanager","arguments":[4]}
```

Targets: context, activity, service:NAME or an earlier objectRef. Static methods and constructors omit target. IDs: method(type,...), new(type,...), field:NAME; writable fields use set:NAME. The BatteryManager example reads Android BATTERY_PROPERTY_CAPACITY.

Values accept exact primitives, null, enum names and arrays. Tags: {"objectRef":"ID"}, {"className":"PUBLIC_SDK_CLASS"}, {"long":"SIGNED_DECIMAL"}, {"bytesBase64":"BASE64"}, {"arrayType":"COMPONENT_TYPE","values":[]}. No nested calls or arbitrary object maps. Nullability and integer bounds are validated.

Read-only agents cannot see write tools or mutating/unaudited SDK members. The executor also blocks forged writes and autoRequestPermissions:true with read_only_violation. androidApiRead independently enforces the approved member policy before resolving arguments, targets or permissions. Unknown members default to write, regardless of their names.

Invocation timeout defaults to 30000ms; timeoutMilliseconds accepts 1..300000. thread is auto, main or background. Auto follows SDK thread annotations. A timeout means completion is unknown. Reuse the identical write key to observe its original result without repeating it. Keys are process-owned; use jobStart for durable submission/results. SDK completed means the method returned, not that an asynchronous Android effect finished.

Object handles survive activity recreation but not process death. androidApiObjects pages indexed arrays/lists/maps/text; text offsets are UTF-16 units. Previews mark omitted contents explicitly. At most 256 handles are retained. Unregister SDK listeners and stop hardware sessions, then release handles with androidApiRelease. close:true calls AutoCloseable.close when supported; release alone does not undo effects.

androidApiCallback creates an SDK interface proxy or public non-final callback subclass. Select constructor/arguments when needed. returns maps exact overload IDs to explicit constant non-void results. Poll callback records with androidApiObjects objectRef/afterSequence. There are 256 retained events per callback; inspect droppedEvents and gap. The same records emit custom event android_api_callback. Callbacks never execute model-supplied commands automatically.

Android permissions, foreground rules, optional SDK modules, roles and hardware remain authoritative. Known missing grants use existing opt-in owner review. Reflection, raw files/databases/providers, private app internals and dynamic loading require dedicated protected adapters. bridgePermitted:false states that boundary explicitly. No silent grants or simulated success.
aliases: Android API framework system service reflection methods signatures network statistics data usage traffic bytes

title: APK sets and cancellation
text:
# APK sets and cancellation

Upload files through ordinary protected file APIs. apkInstallSet takes apks [{path,sha256?}], base first then splits. At most32 unique APKs,512MiB each,1GiB total. SHA-256 verifies while staging. Android authoritatively validates split names/package/version/signatures/compatibility. Unknown-source access and owner confirmation remain required.

Poll apkInstallStatus with sessionId. Staged/queued does not mean installed. Inspect actual terminal callback and package state.

apkInstallCancel with a Dikciz-owned sessionId abandons a still-cancellable staging/pending session. cancellationAccepted false means terminal or too late. A raced actual install success remains installed. Cancellation never uninstalls an app.

Standalone apkInstall shares the same staging/callback path. No silent approval bypass.

title: Apps and running tasks
text:
# Apps and running tasks

Use app catalogue discovery or open the app drawer and inspect its semantic nodes. appCatalogue reports usageAvailable, usageReason and usageWindowDays:7. When Android Usage access is granted, each app includes foregroundMilliseconds; otherwise it is null. Clients may rank by that value. The read never opens a permission prompt. `launchApp` accepts an app node's `semanticId`. App actions and explicit intents have their own schemas. Confirm package identity with `packageInfo` when names are ambiguous.

App launch results distinguish an attempted launch from verified foreground state. Check the returned outcome and a fresh Accessibility snapshot or display screenshot. A backgrounded Home screen does not prove a launch worked. Apps can reject intents, be disabled, crash immediately, or be unavailable in the current Android profile.

The native recent-app strip tracks resumable tasks. Pressing Home should leave a task available to resume, but Android task history, app flags and manufacturer restrictions still determine which tasks exist. Resume the reported task rather than inventing a component. Inspect current controls and the resulting foreground app.

An ordinary Dikciz process cannot silently force-stop every app or inspect another app's private data. Optional root shell execution has a separate access boundary. A reachable socket is not evidence that Accessibility, overlay or usage access is enabled.

[Launch recipe](dikciz://docs/recipes/launch-app). [Permission review](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions).

Use `appIcon` or `dikciz_app_icon` with a launchable `component` from `appCatalogue`. Optional `sizePixels` defaults to 64 and accepts 16 through 128. The shared result includes PNG base64 in `pngBase64`, width, height and MIME type. HTML can use `dikciz.command("appIcon", {component})` and a `data:image/png;base64,` image URL. Cache only the icons needed by the visible list. Android supplies icons from installed package resources.
aliases: installed apps packages icons drawer launch open application foreground recent tasks

title: Audio playback
text:
# Audio playback

Use audioDevices for output IDs. Upload a local audio file, or use the path from speechSynthesize/microphoneRecord. audioPlayback action=play requires path. Optional volumePercent=0..100 (default 100), loop=false, outputDeviceId and maximumDurationMilliseconds=1..86400000 (default 3600000). URLs are not accepted.

Play returns sessionId and asynchronous preparing state. Poll action=status with sessionId. Verify playing/completed/failed, not just accepted preparation. Failed state has error and optional Android decoder details. A concurrent play fails hardware_busy; stop the current session explicitly.

pause/resume require sessionId. seek requires sessionId and positionMilliseconds within duration; poll seeking=false. volume requires sessionId and volumePercent. stop and status allow no ID to target/inspect the current session. Supplying a stale ID fails instead of affecting a newer session.

Focus denial is explicit. Keep Dikciz foreground for start/resume on restricted Android versions. Focus loss pauses with pauseReason=audio_focus_lost and never auto-resumes. Output selection is a preference, not proof of physical routing or audible output.

Completion, stop, failure and the wall-clock lifetime release player/focus. Lifetime includes pauses and preparation. Sessions end on process death. This is not a background playback service or cellular call-audio injection.

Full guide: https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/blob/main/docs/audio-playback.md

## Recording

microphoneSession action=start returns sessionId and recording state. Open Dikciz and grant Android microphone permission before starting. Configuration fields: maximumDurationMilliseconds=1..86400000 (default 60000), maximumBytes=4096..1073741824 (default 67108864), inputDeviceId, sampleRateHz accepts 8000, 16000, 22050, 44100 or 48000 (default 44100), bitRate=8000..320000 (default 128000), channels=1..2 (default 1).

status optionally selects sessionId; stop/cancel require it. Stop or a duration/file limit finalizes M4A and returns completed with path/bytes/mimeType. Cancel discards output. Foreground loss, silencing and recorder/finalization errors fail and discard output; cleanupFailed exposes failed deletion. Poll final state before claiming a saved recording.

Shares ownership with microphoneRecord and speechRecognize. No overlapping captures, process persistence, background service or cellular call audio.
aliases: play sound music audio speaker volume playback session

title: Encrypted backups
text:
# Encrypted backups

Use backupCreate with passphrase of 12 or more characters. includeApiKeys defaults false. All archives are encrypted. Public home assets, scripts, widget state, provider profiles and chat history are included; control authentication, listener ports, logs and Android grants are excluded.

Use backupsList, then backupPreview with path and passphrase. Read counts and the returned sha256. Restore only the owner-selected preview: backupRestore requires previewId, exact sha256 and confirm=true. It replaces current home and chat. activateAutomation defaults false. Stop active and queued assistant turns before restore.

Do not replay interrupted tool calls after restore. Keys omitted from a backup need re-entry. Preview expires after 15 minutes and private staging is excluded from file APIs. Limits: 4096 files, 32 MiB public data, 128 profiles, 1000 conversations, 10000 messages, 64 MiB archive.

Commands use owner access. Create, preview and restore are unavailable in read-only mode. The full guide is available through documentation search: backups.

title: Bluetooth
text:
# Bluetooth

Discover schemas before use. Android scan/connect access and enabled hardware are required. These commands never silently enable the radio.

bluetoothDevices lists bonded peers with pagination. bluetoothScan mode=ble|classic collects actual peers for durationMilliseconds (default 5000, maximum 120000), maximumDevices (default 50, maximum 200). Classic refuses to interrupt existing discovery.

bluetoothPair(address) returns paired only if already bonded. A new bond request returns submitted; check bluetoothDevices after Android confirmation.

bluetoothExchange requires address and serviceUuid, secure defaults true. Optional dataBase64 writes at most 65536 bytes; readBytes defaults 4096, maximum 65536, zero disables input. One read is not a complete application message. Deadline closes the socket. Partial output may precede failure.

bluetoothGatt requires address and action: discover, read, write, readDescriptor, writeDescriptor or observe. Discovery is paginated with offset/limit. Other actions require serviceUuid and characteristicUuid; descriptor actions also descriptorUuid. Use discovered serviceInstanceId/characteristicInstanceId to resolve duplicate UUIDs. Writes require dataBase64, maximum 512 bytes. writeType=default|noResponse|signed. Observe accepts maximumEvents (default 1, maximum 100); a subscribed window can expire with no events. Optional mtu=23..517.

Both transactions default timeoutMilliseconds=30000, maximum 120000. They close owned connections afterward. Verify the peripheral's application result before retrying writes. No-response writes do not prove application success.

Full guide: https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/blob/main/docs/bluetooth-control.md
aliases: Bluetooth nearby discovery scan pair bond RFCOMM BLE GATT characteristic

title: Chat budgets and compaction
text:
# Chat budgets and compaction

Each conversation configures contextTokens (default131072), maxOutputTokens (4096), safetyMarginTokens (1024), compaction (drop-oldest or summarize), summaryModel (optional same-provider ID), summaryOutputTokens (2048), reasoning, thinkingTokens, outputTokenField, maximumRounds (32), timeoutMilliseconds (300000) and optional systemPrompt.

The provider connection stores host/protocol/key once. configure patches per-conversation settings without duplicating the provider or affecting other conversations. settings reads effective settings and saved overrides. Selecting a known model fills contextTokens and clamps the current reply reserve to its known output ceiling and remaining input space. Explicit token fields in the same request win. Unknown models keep current budgets. Discovery alone never changes settings. Changing providers retains read-only access and resets other overrides. Existing provider defaults and encrypted keys survive upgrade.

Available input = min(contextTokens - maxOutputTokens, known maximum input when supplied) - safetyMarginTokens. The actual output cap is sent to the provider as well as reserved. OpenAI defaults to max_completion_tokens; outputTokenField:max_tokens selects that field exclusively for compatible hosts. Anthropic uses max_tokens.

The input estimator conservatively counts UTF-8 bytes, framing, tool schemas and image allowances. It is not an exact provider tokenizer or billing counter. Known limits use validated provider metadata first, then a bundled exact-ID catalog. Unknown limits remain null. settings includes modelLimits with contextTokens, maxOutputTokens, maxInputTokens and limitsSource (provider, catalog, provider+catalog or unknown). Model discovery is persisted per connection and invalidated on connection edits. Manual budgets and safety margins remain editable.

drop-oldest omits complete old exchanges from outbound context. summarize replaces a completed old prefix with a stored summary/checkpoint, preserving full original transcripts in SQLite. Its request reserves summaryOutputTokens separately. Current user input and its live tool results remain together. An input that cannot fit fails explicitly; it is never silently chopped. Failed summaries preserve original history. A summaryModel must support the configured context limit. Switching provider/model drops incompatible saved reasoning on replay.

reasoning:auto leaves provider defaults. OpenAI explicit efforts are sent as reasoning_effort; actual model support varies. Anthropic supports none (disabled), or low/medium/high/xhigh/max adaptive effort where supported. Explicit Anthropic thinkingTokens requires reasoning:auto, at least1024 and less than maxOutputTokens. Reasoning counts toward provider output budgets. summary requests use default reasoning and no explicit thinking budget.

Stop cancels generation. Timeout/max-round exhaustion is visible in failed messages. Completed tool effects are not rolled back. After process death active/executing messages become interrupted; uncertain tool effects are never replayed automatically. Poll read/status and inspect actual results before continuing.

Anthropic thinking signatures, omitted-text blocks and redacted blocks are preserved for tool continuations and later turns. Opaque thinking stays opaque. Screenshot images use each provider's supported content format.

Later turns retain failed, cancelled and interrupted owner requests and completed tool outcomes under either context policy. Unrecorded tool outcomes receive a matching tool_outcome_unknown result for context, never automatic execution. Inspect actual state before retrying a side effect. Pending later requests are excluded from the current context.

Empty tool arguments become `{}`. Malformed nonempty arguments are rejected without execution. Replay preserves rejected text and recorded outcomes in valid JSON, including old conversations after restart. It never reruns past actions.
aliases: context window output reserve maximum tokens summarization compaction conversation history

title: Chat event rules
text:
# Chat event rules

Call dikciz_chat action subscribe with conversationId and rules. This replaces all rules for that conversation. Each rule has optional unique id, subscription and instructions. Rules use the existing canonical automation event subscription validator and filters.

```json
{"action":"subscribe","conversationId":"CONVERSATION_ID","rules":[{"id":"owner-check","subscription":{"event":"example.check","minimumIntervalMilliseconds":60000},"instructions":"Report relevant phone state for this event."}]}
```

Publish that custom event through the existing emitEvent action. Native events use the same names, package/sensor/location filters and grants as Lua/HTML subscriptions. Read guides/events and guides/actions-state for discovery and publication.

Rules run while chat is hidden and persist across restart. They can create paid provider requests. Default minimum interval is 60000 milliseconds, minimum allowed 1000. At most 32 rules per conversation. One event turn can wait while another runs; further events are coalesced. Own notification events are excluded to avoid a reply-notification loop. Rule instructions are the configured task; event payload is untrusted data.

Hidden events/replies increment unread state. Notifications open the conversation if Android allows notifications. Read the transcript for real outcomes; an event being queued does not prove tool completion. Clear with rules:[] to disable listeners. Stop cancels turns, not subscriptions. The agent may create its own rules with this same tool when the owner requests automation.

Foreground service lifetime depends on active work/rules. Android force-stop, revoked grants and system restrictions can interrupt it. Active or executing work becomes interrupted after process death and is not automatically replayed. Review effects before retrying.

Active work updates one quiet notification with its current phase and a Stop action. Tap it to reopen the exact running conversation. Stop cancels that conversation's active/queued turns, preserves completed effects and leaves subscriptions enabled. Old turn notifications cannot stop newer work. Notification permission/channel settings control visibility; chat-panel Stop remains available. Progress omits prompts, arguments and screen contents.

Home posts a separate quiet Open chat shortcut while idle. An owner tap opens half-screen chat over the current app; Explain this screen then captures that underlying app. The shortcut needs notification permission and its Chat shortcut channel, not another running service or overlay permission for the tap. Opening it does not send a message.
aliases: autonomous assistant event subscription automation trigger background agent

title: Assistant tool contracts and access
text:
# Assistant tool contracts and access

The embedded assistant has five compact wrappers. Their provider schemas define parameter types:

- `phone_tools`: required string `query`, optional decimal string `offset`. Empty query lists tools; nonempty queries rank tasks and identifiers with aliases and typo correction. Follow `hasMore`/`nextOffset` only when needed.
- `phone_search`: required string `query`, optional string `collection` (default `docs`) and decimal strings `limit`/`offset`. Returns ranked excerpts, exact IDs and URIs. Collection `tools` returns current permitted schemas.
- `phone_call`: required string `name` and string `arguments_json`. Discover the exact native name first. The string contains a strict JSON object matching the native `inputSchema`, including all required fields, types, enums and nested objects. Send `"{}"` for a no-argument tool.
- `phone_resources`: optional string `cursor` from the preceding resource page. No arguments means `{}`.
- `phone_resource`: required string `uri`, copied from search or resource discovery.

Discovery does not execute an operation. Reuse installed contracts while the build and access context remain unchanged. Rediscover after an APK or access change, or a contract rejection. Search for the relevant procedure instead of walking the entire resource catalog. Rejected native calls include `toolContract` when that tool is currently exposed. Follow its actual `inputSchema`; the original error and permission recovery remain available. Unexposed or unknown tools return discovery guidance. Correction does not automatically execute or retry anything. Check uncertain side effects before retrying.

Each model request has current launcher access context. `conversationReadOnly` is the saved setting; `turnReadOnly` is the executor restriction for this turn. `reason` distinguishes `conversation_setting`, `screen_explanation`, `turn_started_read_only` and `writable_conversation`. `writeAccessResumesNextTurn` means the saved conversation permits writes but this turn retains a temporary restriction. A screen task does not change saved settings. Treat current context as authoritative over old assistant claims; do not tell an owner to enable writes when their conversation already allows them. Android grants are separate and must be checked through actual tool results.

Each call rechecks trusted saved access. A configure patch containing only settings:{"readOnly":true} can restrict an active turn immediately; other configuration changes require stopping it first. Model arguments cannot relax access.
aliases: tool calling required parameters arguments schema validation errors read only access

title: On-device chat
text:
# On-device chat

MCP dikciz_chat, HTTP/WebSocket chatControl and native bindings share validation, permissions and results. The launcher cheese opens half-screen chat with streaming Markdown, model selection, settings and conversation management. Expand or hide it; scroll up to pause following and Latest to resume.

Actions:

- profiles; profileSave with profile; models with profileId.
- create with profileId and optional title/settings; list with limit/offset.
- read with conversationId and message limit/offset; rename with conversationId/title.
- settings with conversationId; configure with conversationId and settings and/or profileId; delete an idle conversation.
- send with conversationId/text/requestKey; stop with conversationId.
- task with conversationId/requestKey/task and optional text. widget requires a description and writable access; it preserves the selected page target. explainScreen uses an optional question, hides chat, captures the display before contacting the provider and forces read-only tools for that turn. Chat requests reopening afterward. Missing capture access fails without a provider request; busy assistants reject a new capture. Native buttons use these same actions.
- status; show/fullscreen with optional conversationId; hide.
- subscribe with conversationId/rules. Read guides/chat-events.

Add provider offers OpenAI, Anthropic and Custom templates. Standard templates fill their API URL/protocol; Custom accepts your compatible host. Changing templates clears the typed key. profileSave takes name, protocol, baseUrl and optional apiKey; model may be omitted. Protocol openai uses Chat Completions, anthropic uses Messages. Keys are write-only and Keystore-encrypted. Explicit empty apiKey clears it; a changed host/protocol clears a retained key unless replaced. Use HTTPS for public providers. Redirects are disabled.

Discover models once, then configure each conversation independently, for example settings:{model:"MODEL_ID",contextTokens:131072,maxOutputTokens:8192,reasoning:"medium"}. Known model selection fills context and clamps the reply reserve; explicit token fields win. Unknown models retain manual budgets. settings returns effective values, overrides and modelLimits. Discovery never rewrites saved budgets. Changing provider retains readOnly and resets other overrides. Credentials and connection fields are forbidden in settings. Model/settings changes require an idle conversation; a missing model blocks generation. Read guides/chat-context for token fields and compaction.

Queue acceptance is not completion. Poll read and inspect actual tool outcomes. Reuse requestKey for the same send/task without repeating it; changed text or task conflicts. SQLite retains full transcripts despite compaction. Uninstall/data clear removes them; Home reset does not. Screenshots become provider image inputs and persist privately. Screen explanation requires an image-capable model. Cancellation does not request chat reopening.

[Tool contracts and access](dikciz://docs/guides/chat-tools). phone_tools discovers schemas using query and optional offset. Execute with phone_call using name and arguments_json. Use phone_search for relevant guides and recipes, or collection tools for ranked schemas. Read an exact returned URI with phone_resource. Catalog listing is optional. Reuse contracts while the installed build and current access context are unchanged. Tool names are not resource URIs. Rejected arguments/resources return recoverable errors; uncertain effects require inspection before retrying.

settings:{readOnly:true} hides write tools and passes a trusted access flag into the executor. Direct writes and autoRequestPermissions:true fail with read_only_violation. Tool arguments cannot disable it. Grant missing access manually. History/logs still persist; other owner clients retain their access. Writable agents can hide chat and inspect other apps through existing tools. Phone data goes to the selected provider. See docs/embedded-chat.md for the full contract.
aliases: assistant chatbot conversation provider API key model reasoning token budget

title: Safety, journeys and devices
text:
# Safety, journeys and devices

These commands share ordinary HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua execution. Native controls: Settings, Safety, journeys and devices. Discover exact schemas before calls.

Read only the relevant section:

- [Safety and journeys](dikciz://docs/guides/journeys): plans, check-ins, geofences and routes.
- [Device connections](dikciz://docs/guides/connections): retained Bluetooth, USB and NFC.
- [Vision](dikciz://docs/guides/vision): local OCR, barcode reading and raster PDFs.
- [Health](dikciz://docs/guides/health): record catalogue, grants, reads, aggregates and writes.
- [Wi-Fi networks](dikciz://docs/guides/wifi-networks): Android approval and local hotspot.
- [Routines](dikciz://docs/guides/routines): repeatable read-only assistant turns.
- [APK sets](dikciz://docs/guides/apk-sets): split installation and cancellation.

No feature bypasses Android permission, hardware or foreground limits. A missing capability is explicit. Submitted effects are not proof of delivery or installation.

title: Connect to the phone
text:
# Connect to the phone

The default device ports are WebSocket `19001` and HTTP/MCP `19002`, bound to `127.0.0.1`. Loopback is reachable only on the phone or through forwarding. For direct access, the owner can set `listenAddress` to `0.0.0.0` in `/sdcard/Dikciz/control/ports.json`. See [listener changes](dikciz://docs/recipes/listener).

Connect to the phone's real Wi-Fi or private VPN hostname, never `0.0.0.0`. Tailscale policy must allow traffic from the controlling computer to the phone's TCP ports. The listeners have no built-in TLS. Use a trusted private network and bearer authentication.

| Interface | Endpoint | Delivery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP | `http://phone.example:19002/mcp` | Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC tools and resources. |
| HTTP | `http://phone.example:19002/v1/automation` | One JSON command per POST; shell streams use SSE. |
| WebSocket | `ws://phone.example:19001/v1/automation` | Commands and persistent event delivery. |

Send `Authorization: Bearer <password>` when enabled. Native clients omit `Origin`; untrusted browser origins are rejected. The supplied client reads `DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN` from the environment. Keep credentials out of command arguments, logs and shared files.

Modern MCP 2026-07-28 uses stateless server/discover and per-request protocol/capability metadata, MCP-Protocol-Version and matching Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers. Legacy clients initialize with 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 or 2025-03-26, retain Mcp-Session-Id and send notifications/initialized; modern metadata is optional there. The supplied client manages its connection. Resources and tools share authentication and Origin checks.

CLI: `python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp-read dikciz://docs/index --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty`.
aliases: connect endpoint hostname IP port HTTP websocket MCP authentication remote Tailscale

title: Retained Bluetooth, USB and NFC
text:
# Retained Bluetooth, USB and NFC

deviceConnectionOpen returns a process-owned id. Exchange, inspect and close with deviceConnectionExchange/Read/Close. deviceConnectionsList pages metadata. Default lifetime300000ms, max3600000; eight active. Default operation timeout30000ms, max120000; transfer bound65536bytes. Timeout closes hardware; writes can have partial effects. All exchanges count as mutating.

kind rfcomm: address, serviceUuid, optional secure. Exchange optional dataBase64 and readBytes. Returned chunks are not message framing.

kind gatt: address. Exchange action discover/read/write/subscribe/unsubscribe/notifications. Use exact discovered UUIDs and instance IDs for duplicates. Notification cursors report bounded loss.

kind usb: deviceId, optional interfaceIndex. Missing access returns usbRequestAccess recovery. Exchange control requires requestType/request/value/index; bulk/interrupt requires endpointAddress. Use readBytes for input, dataBase64 for output.

kind nfc: foreground unlocked Dikciz plus presented tag; technology defaults IsoDep. Exchange transceive/readNdef/writeNdef. Other supported technologies include NfcA/B/F/V and supported Mifare. Tag loss is failure. No payment interpretation/card emulation.

Expiry, close and process death release hardware. Connected-device notification Stop all closes active connections. The optional Vehicle console template reads ELM327 RPM/coolant/voltage through paired RFCOMM with explicit framing. Real hardware verification remains separate from emulator results.

title: Custom apps
text:
# Custom apps

Owner apps live in /sdcard/Dikciz/apps/<id> with app.json, ui.html, ui.css, ui.js, main.js or main.lua, state.json and files/. Dikciz > Apps manages complete bundles. Bundled SOS, Voice notes, Agenda, Device status and Travel todo use the same platform. See recipes/travel-todo for a GPS checklist. SOS decisions are editable JS; native code hosts Android commands, timers and urgent windows.

Discover customAppsList, customAppRead, customAppInstall, customAppControl, customAppEvent, customAppState, customAppSchedule, customAppAlert and customAppRuntime. MCP uses dikciz_custom_apps_list and dikciz_custom_app_* names. All require owner authority; read-only agents see list/read/runtime only and executor guards still block writes.

Install with manifest plus html/css/javascript/backgroundSource and confirm true. Manifest requires version 1, id, title, description, language lua|javascript, events array; commands is optional legacy metadata. Optional eventSubscriptions uses ordinary native filters/intervals; locationMonitoring requests a location service while timers exist. New apps start enabled with Dikciz Android access. Control enable starts without approval; open starts the app and requests UI. Inspect read.uiVisible or snapshot for actual presentation. Control disable stops pending work; remove requires confirm true and deletes state/files. Export excludes state and recordings; import validates a .dikciz-app.zip. Replacement and edits preserve running/stopped state; no manifest approval is required. New ID means independent state. Bundled updates preserve edited sources.

JS synchronous onEvent(event), Lua on_event(event). Context has immutable state/scriptId/androidAccess. Return optional status, result object and patchState/emitEvent actions. Other actions are rejected. context.request executes phone commands with Dikciz Android access, returning canonical result/error. App-specific read/state/event/schedule/alert default to self and accept another explicit appId. Apps can administer installations and use shell/files/SDK access already granted to Dikciz; this is not an Android process sandbox.

UI uses window.dikciz, selfWidget state/storagePath and dikciz-state events. The UI may invoke its backend with customAppEvent. Backend runs without WebViews or browser timers; globals are fresh. Source/state changes refresh their relevant consumers. Use customAppRuntime clocks and native access observations.

Schedule action schedule requires timerId/event/delayMilliseconds, optional payload. Delay 1000..604800000 ms, max64 pending. cancel needs timerId; cancelAll cancels this app. Timers persist and use monotonic time/native alarms. A claimed interrupted timer or rebooted pending timer becomes needs_review, not replayed; app.resume signals interruption. Android may delay or reject starts. Read latest run/timers for outcomes.

Alert action show requires episodeId/durationMilliseconds/title/detail/cancelLabel/cancelEvent, optional announcement/finalAnnouncement with {seconds}. Duration 1000..3600000 ms. One urgent app at once. Native modal dims background; overlay access allows other apps, otherwise foreground dialog. Notification/channel/keyguard restrictions apply. Cancel invokes the app event; its code cancels timers/state. close clears resources. Pause apps notification disables pending apps. interruptRunning true on an owner customAppEvent blocks subsequent write calls in a running handler except cleanup/state (including geofence deletion); submitted effects remain.

Limits:64 apps,256KiB each source,128KiB state,depth16,2MiB ZIP and exact five source/manifest entries. Encrypted home/chat backups exclude apps. Export sources and preserve data separately. Legacy sos* commands delegate to apps/sos; migrated active runs need review. No automatic SMS on install/migration.

title: Discover the running build
text:
# Discover the running build

Call `dikciz_device_info` first. Its `application` reports the serving package, version, process and `instanceId`. Release is `eu.psyb0t.dikciz.launcher`; debug adds `.debug`. Updating one does not update the other. Both can read the same public configuration and compete for listener ports.

Use `dikciz_search_query` with collection `docs` to find a procedure, or collection `tools` for ranked installed contracts. Read exact result URIs without enumerating resource pages. Call `tools/list` when a complete schema catalog is needed. Call `dikciz_control_status` for live command contracts, ports, events and limits. Call `dikciz_automation_status` for script and Android access state. Do not infer tool names by converting camel case; use discovery.

MCP `tools/call` wraps a command result in `structuredContent` and text blocks. Inspect `isError`, the command envelope, each action outcome and any `permissionRequest`. An HTTP success status only means the protocol request reached the server. A batch may contain both completed and refused actions.

WebSocket and plain HTTP use `{ "requestId": "<UUID>", "type": "<command>", ...fields }`. They return a correlated `result` or `error` envelope. MCP, HTTP, WebSocket, HTML bridge and Lua owner requests share the command target's procedures and access checks. Transport envelopes and streaming delivery differ.

Use fresh `snapshot` results after UI changes. Semantic IDs and Accessibility snapshots describe a particular screen. Verify a resulting state before continuing a dependent operation. For delayed operations such as APK installation and restart, poll the documented completion signal.

[UI guide](dikciz://docs/guides/ui). [Permissions](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions).
aliases: discover supported commands tools schemas parameters installed version API

title: Replay automation events
text:
# Replay automation events

Use eventJournalStatus, eventJournalRead and eventJournalConfigure through HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML or Lua. The persistent SQLite journal records actual automation-bus dispatches. Reads do not activate sensors or other native subscriptions.

Read status for journalId and lastSequence. Use cursor=lastSequence for future events or 0 for retained history. Read requires journalId; cursor defaults0, limit1..200(default50), waitMilliseconds0..30000(default0). Optional eventTypes is1..32 unique exact event names. Omit it for all types.

Each events item has sequence and the normal event document. Save nextCursor even when filters return no matches. Follow hasMore before waiting. Cursors are exclusive; duplicate reads replay retained events, and each reader keeps its own cursor. A future cursor is invalid. event_journal_restarted means the stored journal epoch changed: read status and explicitly choose a new cursor.

Defaults: maximumEvents2048, bufferBytes8388608, retentionMinutes60. eventJournalConfigure accepts maximumEvents1..16384, bufferBytes65536..33554432, retentionMinutes1..1440. Omitted fields retain current values. Lower limits evict immediately. Limits, retained history and epoch survive process death. Retention continues to apply. Byte accounting measures encoded event JSON, not total heap overhead.

Pages contain at most262144 encoded event bytes and split only between events. historyGap/lostEvents report evicted sequence numbers before cursor, including nonmatching types. Documents over65536bytes become omitted:true markers with reason:event_too_large and originalBytes; original payload is absent. omittedEvents counts page markers. This is explicit loss, not silent truncation.

Current Android source access is checked again before disclosure. Missing source permissions or special access use the shared failure/review flow. autoRequestPermissions:true asks owner review where the requirement supports it, then retry. Clipboard replay requires foreground Dikciz. Missing Health Connect steps access returns health_connect_permission_required; grant it in automation settings.

Owner command bindings have the same authority as other direct native APIs. Lua subscription policies continue to control automatic delivery. Replay sees dispatched events after sensor coalescing, cannot recover stopped-process events, and supports named durable acknowledgements through eventConsumerRead/Ack, eventConsumersList and eventConsumerForget. Reads never acknowledge implicitly. See dikciz://docs/guides/operations. Use waitMilliseconds0 inside Lua event handlers to avoid blocking the shared event worker.

[Events](dikciz://docs/guides/events), [Permissions](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions), [Lua](dikciz://docs/guides/lua).
aliases: missed events cursor replay journal reconnect sequence history

title: Custom events
text:
# Custom events

Event names start with a letter, contain 1 through 128 characters, and use letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-`. Use a namespace such as `example.start`. Payloads are JSON values accepted by the current action schema; use small objects with stable keys.

Publish through MCP `dikciz_automation_dispatch`, HTTP or WebSocket `automationDispatch`, or HTML `dikciz.emitEvent`. A Lua handler can return an `emitEvent` action. A network dispatch needs a valid HTML `sourceWidgetAddress` and an action such as:

```json
{"type":"emitEvent","event":"example.start","payload":{}}
```

Lua receives custom events only through enabled subscription records backed by an enabled policy with `manualTrigger` and the required action allowlist. An HTML widget receives matching `eventSubscriptions` through `dikciz.onEvent` only while rendered. Live delivery is transient. The SQLite [event journal](dikciz://docs/guides/event-replay) preserves bounded replay across process death, with explicit loss and named consumer acknowledgements. It never retries side effects automatically.

Subscription records specify `event` and `minimumIntervalMilliseconds`. Use the current schema for filters and coalescing fields. Rate limits and coalescing can intentionally skip repeated work. Avoid emitting the same input event from its own handler.

WebSocket subscribers can observe `automation_event` records. MCP's resources are static documentation; they do not subscribe to automation events. After MCP or HTTP dispatch, inspect script status, saved state or a widget acknowledgement. An `executed` publish outcome confirms publication, not completion of every asynchronous consumer.

Read [pipeline setup](dikciz://docs/recipes/event-setup), then its linked Lua and widget sections for a complete two-input example.
aliases: emit send dispatch publish custom event payload subscribe listen trigger

title: Files and APKs
text:
# Files and APKs

Use `fileList`, `fileRead`, `fileWrite` and `fileMkdir` through their discovered MCP tools or the same HTTP/WebSocket commands. Paths are absolute and access is limited by Android permissions granted to Dikciz. File operations can reach shared storage and the app sandbox where permitted.

`fileList` uses `offset`, `limit` and `hasMore`; default 100 entries, maximum 500. Continue by the number returned. Directory mutation can change enumeration order.

`fileRead` returns base64 bytes, `nextOffset` and `eof`. Default chunk is 64 KiB, maximum 256 KiB. Continue at the acknowledged next offset. File downloads return actual bytes, without the script-log viewer's redaction.

`fileWrite` takes `path`, `dataBase64`, optional `offset` and `overwrite`. Start at zero. Existing files are refused unless overwrite is explicitly intended. Later chunks must use the acknowledged `nextOffset`, equal to the current file size. Each decoded chunk is at most 256 KiB. Create parents first with `fileMkdir` and `parents: true`.

Do not construct shell commands from untrusted filenames to transfer bytes. The supplied CLI `upload` and `download` perform bounded HTTP transfers and report byte count and SHA-256.

`apkInstall` accepts a standalone APK path and optional complete-file `sha256`. It stages asynchronously and returns `sessionId`; poll `apkInstallStatus` until a final state. Owner install-source access and Android confirmation can be required. Upload success and `pending_user_action` are not installation success.

[APK recipe](dikciz://docs/recipes/install-apk). [Credential boundaries](dikciz://docs/guides/security).

## File management

`fileManage` (`dikciz_file_manage`) accepts action and absolute path. `stat` returns metadata. `copy` copies one regular file to destination; `move` renames a file or directory to destination. Neither overwrites existing destinations. Moves across filesystems can fail explicitly.

`delete` removes one file or empty directory. Set recursive=true for a nonempty directory. It preflights the tree, refuses symbolic links and checks maximumEntries (default 10000, range 1..100000) before deleting. An external process can still change files during execution; recursive deletion is not a filesystem transaction.

`search` requires query, a literal case-insensitive name substring. It does not follow symbolic links. Use offset/limit to page matches, maximum 200 per page. maximumEntries bounds scanned entries; increase it or narrow the directory after file_tree_limit. Directory changes can affect enumeration between calls. The empty query matches every name.

Credential record remote-auth.json and its atomic backup/staging aliases are denied through file commands, including canonical path aliases. Move/delete refuse any ancestor containing those credentials. Android still enforces filesystem access. This file-command restriction does not make an authorized privileged shell a sandbox.
aliases: files directories upload download read write copy APK install sideload

title: Hardware controls
text:
# Hardware controls

All operations share HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua validation and Android access. Discover live schemas first.

- torchControl / dikciz_torch_control: required action status/on/off, optional cameraId. Status returns cameraIds and items from Android torch callbacks: enabled/disabled/unavailable, or unknown when none arrives. Optional cameraId filters. timeoutMilliseconds1..5000, default1000, applies only to status. complete means all selected cameras were observed; listeners are removed. On/off requires camera permission and returns submitted with requested enabled. On may set durationMilliseconds from 1 to 5000 for a native automatic off request, independent of JS timers. Later on/off replaces the timer for that camera. autoOffAfterMilliseconds reports the requested duration; status/off reject it. Submission does not prove physical light output.
- vibrationControl / dikciz_vibration_control: required action status/vibrate/waveform/effect/cancel. Status reports available, amplitudeControl and effects with nativeSupport supported/unsupported/unknown. Duration 1..10000 ms, default250. Amplitude -1 (Android default) or1..255, never0. Android settings may suppress vibration. Waveform requires timingsMilliseconds (1..64 integers, 0..10000 each, total1..10000ms), optional matching amplitudes (-1 default, 0 off, 1..255). Without amplitudes timings alternate off/on starting off. No repeats. Effect names click/doubleClick/heavyClick/tick require Android10+; fallbackPossible is explicit. Status support requires Android11+, otherwise unknown. Wrong-action fields fail. Cancel stops Dikciz vibration.
- systemSetting / dikciz_system_setting: action get/set, setting, and value for set only. brightness0..255, automaticBrightness0..1, automaticRotation0..1, rotation0..3, screenTimeoutMilliseconds1..2147483647. Writes require Modify system settings and return stored read-back. Automatic mode or policy can override physical effects. Missing grant uses the common permissionRequest.

Inventories:

- bluetoothDevices / dikciz_bluetooth_devices: paired devices only, address/name/type/bondState. Bluetooth access required on Android12+. No scanning or connection.
- usbDevices / dikciz_usb_devices: attached host devices with IDs, class, interfaces and existing USB access. No permission prompt or transfers.
- wifiScanResults / dikciz_wifi_scan_results: cached SSID/BSSID, frequency, signal, capabilities and timestamp. Requires fine location. Does not start a scan or connect; Android may return an empty cache.
- audioDevices / dikciz_audio_devices: input/output IDs, names, types, sample rates and channels. No routing or playback.
- nfcStatus / dikciz_nfc_status: adapter available/enabled. No tag transactions.
- cameraCapabilities / dikciz_camera_capabilities: required cameraId from cameraList. JPEG sizes, maximum digital zoom, exposure compensation limits and autofocus modes. No capture.

Bluetooth/USB/Wi-Fi/audio accept limit1..200 (default50), offset0..1000000 (default0). Follow hasMore using offset plus returned count. Results include total. Hardware changes can change inventory between calls. No adapter is an explicit unavailable state.

[Permissions](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions), [Hardware](dikciz://docs/guides/hardware), [Speech](dikciz://docs/guides/speech).
aliases: flashlight torch vibration haptic volume brightness airplane hardware

title: Sensors, location, camera and microphone
text:
# Sensors, location, camera and microphone

HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML `dikciz.command` and Lua `context.requestJson` share execution, validation, permissions and outcomes. Discover live tool schemas before calling. Android still controls hardware access.

## Live sensors

`dikciz_sensor_readings` (`sensorReadings`) takes optional `sensorId`, `limit`, `offset` and `timeoutMilliseconds`. Defaults: all sensors, 50 items, offset 0, 1000 ms. Maximum page 200; sample timeout 1 through 5000 ms. Follow `hasMore` using offset plus returned count. Sensor IDs address this device inventory, including duplicate types.

Each item includes name, vendor, type, stringType, reportingMode, range and resolution. `available:true` has actual values, accuracy, monotonic timestampNanoseconds and ageMilliseconds. False has an explicit reason, such as permission_required, android_access_denied, registration_rejected, no_sample_in_window or waiting_for_trigger. Units and vector ordering follow Android's sensor type. Every request unregisters listeners. Poll only while needed. The Sensors page does this while visible; background Lua uses existing sensor subscriptions.

If an item has requirementId, request that access with `dikciz_request_device_access`, then explicitly retry. One denied sensor does not hide other sensors. A direct sensorId request for restricted hardware returns the shared permission error; autoRequestPermissions can request owner review.

## Weather location

`dikciz_location_get` (`locationGet`) accepts maxAgeMilliseconds (default 300000) and timeoutMilliseconds (default 10000, 0 through 120000). It uses a recent cached position or requests a fresh fix. Zero timeout reads cache only. Check available, source, age and accuracy. Missing permissions use the common owner-review flow. Disabled location and timeout return explicit unavailable reasons. placeName is optional; coordinates remain usable without reverse geocoding.

## Capture

`dikciz_camera_list` lists cameraId and facing without capture. `dikciz_camera_capture` accepts optional cameraId, maxDimension (default 1280, range 320 through 4096) and timeoutMilliseconds (default 30000, range 1 through 120000). Quality defaults to 95 (1..100); optional jpegOrientation is 0/90/180/270. cameraCapabilities supplies zoom/exposure/focus limits for zoomPercent (100=1x), exposureCompensation steps and autofocusMode. Unsupported controls fail before opening hardware. Success waits for JPEG bytes and Android completion; requestedControls and captureMetadata distinguish submitted values from actual frame results, with null for missing metadata. No focus convergence is claimed.

`dikciz_microphone_record` accepts durationMilliseconds (default 3000, range 1000 through 120000). It records microphone AAC audio in an M4A file. Camera and microphone require the appropriate Android permission and foreground eligibility. Open Dikciz before capture. Set autoRequestPermissions to true to request missing access, then explicitly retry. Busy, timeout and Android restrictions are errors.

Capture returns state:saved, path, mimeType and bytes after writing actual media. Read or download the returned path through file APIs. No caller filename is accepted. A transport timeout is not proof that capture failed; do not repeat automatically.

## Speech and cellular calls

`dikciz_speech_speak` requires text (at most 2000 characters) and accepts timeoutMilliseconds (default 30000). It speaks through the configured Android engine and returns state:spoken after completion, or an explicit failure. Device output is not call-stream injection.

`dikciz_call_audio` accepts action status, record or speak. Status reports captureSupported:false and injectionSupported:false on this ordinary app installation. Record and speak return call_audio_unsupported. Android cellular call audio needs privileged system integration. Microphone permission does not grant it. Existing callControl places, answers or ends calls subject to Android access.
aliases: sensor accelerometer gyroscope light pressure proximity camera microphone TTS

title: Health Connect records
text:
# Health Connect records

healthRecordsCatalogue reports provider availability, sixteen kinds, exact writeShape, units, timestamp fields, aggregate metrics and read/write grants. Read this before constructing records.

healthPermissionsRequest: kinds array, access read/write/readWrite, optional includeBackground/includeHistory. Android owner approval is required. Missing grants return permissionRequest and explicit retryRequired. Never replay writes automatically.

healthRecordsRead: kind, startTimeMilliseconds,endTimeMilliseconds, optional limit/pageToken. Follow nextPageToken/hasMore; max range366days and Android history rules. healthRecordsAggregate uses provider metrics and origin handling.

healthRecordsWrite: kind and1..50 records. Each has stable clientRecordId, optional clientRecordVersion, correct timestamps and values. UTC Unix milliseconds; manual-entry metadata; strict SDK bounds. healthRecordsDelete: kind, exact recordIds and confirm true. Android enforces record-origin ownership.

Kinds: steps,distance,activeCalories,totalCalories,heartRate,sleep,exercise,weight,height,hydration,bodyFat,bodyTemperature,bloodPressure,bloodGlucose,oxygenSaturation,floors. Native Health tab offers targeted grants and today's data. Missing provider/permission/records remain explicit.

title: HTML widgets
text:
# HTML widgets

An HTML widget stores `html`, `css`, `javascript`, `state`, `itemStates`, layout and optional `eventSubscriptions`. Dikciz injects the native bridge. Register bridge work on `dikciz-ready`; read `selfWidget` for the current widget's address and state.

`dikciz.request(document, options)` returns the full command envelope. `dikciz.command(type, fields, options)` returns the result or rejects with the preserved error. `dikciz.dispatch({actions})` uses typed automation actions. The same command validation and Android access checks apply as network entrypoints.

`selfWidget.visible` reports native page/window visibility. Listen for `dikciz-visibility` and inspect `event.detail.visible` before polling or asking for access. Neighbor pages may preload and receive `dikciz-ready` before selection.

`selfWidget.patchState(values)` persists a replacement state. `dikciz-state` reports state replacement without destroying the document. Use `dikciz.patchWidget(address, values)` for another saved widget; only `title`, `html`, `css`, `javascript`, `state` and `itemStates` are patchable through that action. Subscription changes belong in the widget's saved JSON record or editor. Source changes may recreate the WebView.

`dikciz.emitEvent(name, payload)` publishes an event. `dikciz.onEvent(listener)` receives events matching this widget's configured `eventSubscriptions` while rendered. A hidden page is not a durable background worker. Put durable event handling in Lua. See [events](dikciz://docs/guides/events).

A WebView owns one complete HTML/CSS/JavaScript document and its state. Long press content, background or the top handle for the same whole-widget controls. Edit exposes all source fields. There are no native card preset objects. To change one section, edit its saved markup and rendering code while preserving siblings. Read the [document editing recipe](dikciz://docs/recipes/html-item).

Renderer budgets and document-byte limits are reported by `diagnostics.htmlWidgetResources` and configuration limits. Console warnings, bridge refusals and renderer failures appear in bounded script logs.

The native widget picker lists library templates directly under Dikciz with searchable descriptions. Selecting a template opens its preview; Load creates an independent WebView. Empty HTML widget inserts a blank document directly. The HTML library copies complete templates into independent WebViews. It includes the complete Time and weather, Most used apps, Agenda, Voice notes and Device status starter documents, Home dashboard, clock/search, app search, notes, System dashboard, Live sensors and BTC and economic news. Save to library stores a complete source document without live state. The system template uses local `deviceState`; the market template contacts Coinbase and GDELT only on explicit refresh and keeps dated saved results.

State ownership is `pages/<page-id>/widgets/<webview-id>/state.json` for the wrapper and `items/<instance-id>/state.json` beneath it for each card. Use stable `data-dikciz-item-id` markers and `selfWidget.itemFor(element)` or `selfWidget.item(id)`. An item exposes `state`, `getState()`, `patchState(values)`, `storagePath`, `readFile(name)` and `writeFile(name, dataBase64)`. Document source and state edits can remove a namespace; native Delete removes the whole WebView and its files. `itemStates` patches and valid file edits deliver `dikciz-item-state` without reloading the WebView. Presets never carry live state.
aliases: programmable webview widget HTML JavaScript CSS bridge state storage DOM

title: Background JavaScript
text:
# Background JavaScript

Choose language javascript in a script record; omitted language stays lua. Public scripts/<id>/script.json metadata has id/title/enabled/apiVersion/language. Source is main.js, state.json holds explicit state, run-status.json reports completion. Native Settings > Scripts > New JavaScript script creates one. Expanded configGet/configReplace includes language/source/state. File watching reloads valid main.js changes.

Implement synchronous function onEvent(event). It runs in an embedded interpreter on the existing automation worker, without a WebView. event has type/source/timestampMilliseconds/coalescingKey/payload/time.hour24/time.minute. context has scriptId/state/widgets/androidAccess and optional accessibility. Inputs are read-only and globals reset each invocation.

Return {status:"short text",actions:[{type:"patchState",values:{count:1}},{type:"emitEvent",event:"example.counter.updated",payload:{count:1}}]}. Typed actions and policy checks match Lua. An enabled script needs an enabled policy and subscription. For custom subscriptions set event to the actual name, not custom plus customEventName. manual needs manualTrigger; alarm uses capability alarm and alarmIntervalMilliseconds >=60000. Existing Android background restrictions apply.

context.request(objectOrJsonString) returns the canonical command envelope; context.requestJson returns JSON text. Inspect errors, permissionRequest and actual operation outcomes. Direct commands have owner authority, like Lua; returned-action policies do not sandbox those commands. Enable only trusted code. Network entrypoints and read-only chat retain their normal mutation checks.

No DOM, browser timers, fetch, Node.js or Promise completion. Returning a Promise is invalid_result. Use events and commands. emitEvent reaches subscribed Lua scripts and currently rendered HTML widgets. Closing a page does not stop a background JS script. This does not keep widget WebViews running in the background.

Limits: 50000 observed instructions, setup CPU250ms, handler CPU50ms, observed memory delta2MiB, interpreter stack128, serialized result1MiB. Host command CPU is excluded. These are runtime checks, not a separate heap/process sandbox. Java class access is blocked. Syntax/execution errors record invalid_javascript; invalid returns record invalid_result; unexpected engine failures record runtime_unavailable. Other limits use shared failure statuses. Poll script state/run status and logs after a trigger.

Archives use .dikciz-script.zip with kind dikciz-javascript-script and exactly archive.json/script.json/main.js/state.json. Lua archives keep their old kind/source. Imported scripts still need subscriptions. See guides/lua and recipes/event-setup for shared policy and event wiring.

title: Durable command jobs
text:
# Durable command jobs

Use `dikciz_job_start` with a unique `idempotencyKey` and `command`, a full ordinary command including `type`. It returns `jobId`. The same key and command deduplicate; changed content conflicts. Optional retentionHours is 1..720, default 168. Two workers and at most 256 retained records. Jobs cannot enqueue other jobs, mutate remote authentication or turn shellStream into a durable stream.

Read `dikciz_job_status` with jobId. The persisted response is the original command envelope, including Android permission recovery. completed means a result envelope exists; inspect its actual state. failed contains an error. queued/running are pending. cancelled means queued work never ran. interrupted means a previous process ended without a final outcome. Do not assume the side effect did or did not happen.

`dikciz_jobs_list` pages metadata newest first with offset, limit (default 50, max 200), total and hasMore. Fetch large results individually. Results survive disconnects and process restart until retention expiry. Expired terminal records are pruned on subsequent job operations. App data clearing removes jobs.

`dikciz_job_cancel` cancels queued work or sets cancellationRequested and interrupts a running worker. It does not roll back effects or guarantee Android stopped. Poll final state. No interrupted work is replayed automatically.

Use autoRequestPermissions on the nested command, or inherit it from jobStart, when owner review is intended. Granting access does not rerun a failed job. Explicitly inspect and retry only the authorized operation. Arguments/results stay in app-private storage and are excluded from ordinary operation logs.
aliases: background command job chain workflow batch durable resume cancellation

title: Safety and journeys
text:
# Safety and journeys

sosPlanSave stores contacts [{address,label?}] and optional message/checkInSeconds/graceSeconds/updateSeconds/maximumUpdates/subscriptionId. It stays inactive. sosPreview is a dry run.

sosControl action arm or trigger requires confirm true, foreground location, SEND_SMS and notification access. arm waits the check-in period, trigger begins the grace. checkIn resets the deadline, cancel stops future sends but cannot recall SMS. sosStatus returns run state and receipt keys. Poll smsStatus per key for carrier results. Default check-in 3600s, grace 60s, update 600s, maximumUpdates 3. Minimum check-in/update 60s, grace 5s; maximumUpdates 1..24. At most ten exact contacts. Message tokens: {location}, {accuracyMeters}, {timestamp}.

A visible app foreground service offers Pause apps. Android can delay or stop monitoring. Rebooted/interrupted claimed runs need review and never automatically resume outgoing SMS. Do not claim emergency-service reliability. Recipient/update idempotency keys persist before submission.

geofenceSave requires title/latitude/longitude/radiusMeters, optional id/enabled/dwellMilliseconds. Disabled by default. Radius >=100m, max32 fences. Accurate real fixes plus hysteresis produce geofence.enter/exit/dwell custom events. geofencesList pages results; geofenceDelete needs exact id.

journeyControl action start records one real route, optional title/sampleIntervalMilliseconds (1000..60000, default10000). Stop by id. journeysList and journeyRead use offset/limit/hasMore. Maximum64 journeys,10000 points each. Reboot interrupts recording. journeyDelete needs id and confirm true after stopping. The native preview draws recorded points locally.

SOS decisions live in editable /sdcard/Dikciz/apps/sos/main.js with its own UI/state. Legacy sos* commands delegate to that app. Read dikciz://docs/guides/custom-apps for the general platform. Private geofences/routes and public custom apps are excluded from home/chat backups.

During cancellation grace, the shared service shows a countdown with Cancel SOS using an owner-enabled overlay, or a foreground dialog. The full-screen modal dims the background and blocks background taps and Back; use Cancel SOS to cancel. An urgent notification offers the same cancellation. Alarm pulses, vibration and available offline English speech explain the pending send. Android volume/DND, lock-screen and overlay restrictions apply. sosStatus.warning reports presentation, remainingSeconds, screenVisible, alarmVolume and speechState. Cancel clears warning resources and future sends, not completed SMS or unrelated route monitoring.

title: Location, geocoding and GNSS
text:
# Location, geocoding and GNSS

locationGet reads a recent permitted fix or waits for one. Check available, age, accuracy and source. timeoutMilliseconds=0 reads cache only. Location permission and Android foreground/background restrictions apply.

dikciz_geocode requires action=forward with nonblank query, or action=reverse with finite latitude (-90..90) and longitude (-180..180). Other action fields are refused. language is optional BCP-47, limit is 1..10 default 5, timeoutMilliseconds is 1..120000 default 30000. Android 13+ is required for bounded asynchronous geocoding.

Results contain bounded nullable address fields and coordinates from the installed Android provider. Empty matches are valid. The provider may send supplied text/coordinates to its network service. geocoder_unavailable, geocoder_timeout and geocoder_failed stay distinct. No invented address replaces failure.

dikciz_gnss_status needs fine location. It observes one satellite callback during timeoutMilliseconds 1..5000, default 1000, then unregisters. It does not activate GPS. Results page satellite IDs, constellation, signal, elevation/azimuth, fix-use flags and optional carrier frequency, plus observation time and total. No callback is available=false with no_status_during_window; that is not a location fix.

Use background Lua location subscriptions for existing event processing. These commands do not themselves create a geofence or durable route tracker.
aliases: GPS city coordinates latitude longitude address geocode GNSS satellite accuracy

title: Logs and diagnosis
text:
# Logs and diagnosis

Start with `scriptLogs` for bounded, sanitized records and `automationStatus` for script state and Android access. The log projection includes timestamps, event names, script/widget IDs, outcomes, reasons and bounded Lua diagnostics. It does not return raw source, state, event payloads or entire configuration.

Persistent JSON Lines logs live under `/sdcard/Dikciz/logs/` in daily `YYYY-MM-DD.log` files. Configuration controls `logging.level`, `retentionDays` and `maxTotalBytes`. Defaults are `info`, seven days and 16777216 bytes. Use `debug` only when the owner wants more diagnostic detail. Valid configuration changes reload logging settings. Retention also respects the disk budget.

If a script appears inactive, check script enabled state, subscription event, policy enabled state, capability, action allowlist and Android access. Then inspect final run status and action outcomes. A publish acknowledgement or trigger acknowledgement does not prove a run completed.

Use the file API for selected raw log chunks when the safe viewer lacks the needed detail. Downloaded files are not redacted by that viewer. Avoid exposing personal data or credentials. Read only the authorized diagnostic window.

For process and system messages, [stream logcat](dikciz://docs/recipes/stream-logs). Unprivileged Android logcat cannot expose every system or other-app record. Root is optional and must be explicitly authorized. `diagnostics` also reports HTML renderer counts and document budgets.
aliases: logs debug info warning error failure diagnostics logcat retention

title: Lua automation
text:
# Lua automation

Scripts use `function on_event(event)`. The event contains `type`, `source`, `timestampMilliseconds`, `coalescingKey` and `payload`. Return a short `status` and typed `actions`, or one direct action. `patchState` saves the current script's state. Device and widget actions are validated before execution.

A script's public directory is `/sdcard/Dikciz/scripts/<id>/`: `script.json`, `main.lua`, `state.json` and generated `run-status.json`. Automation policy and subscription records live under `automation/policies/` and `automation/scripts/`. An enabled script alone does not subscribe it to events. Custom subscriptions require the policy capability `manualTrigger` and each returned action must be allowed by policy.

Use `automationStatus` for configured scripts and Android access, `automationTrigger` for a manual run and `scriptLogs` for outcomes. A trigger acknowledgement is not proof that the handler and every action succeeded. Inspect the final run status and persisted state. Keep returned status text short and avoid credentials or private data in logs.

`context.requestJson` lets an enabled Lua script call the shared owner command API. Its requests still undergo command validation and Android permission checks. Declared policy rules govern returned automation actions; do not assume they isolate arbitrary owner commands or unrestricted shell access.

Typed action names and policy capabilities usually match. Volume is an exception: return {type="setMediaVolume",levelPercent=35}, but allow mediaVolume in policy.actions. levelPercent is an integer 0..100. The returned action parser accepts at most eight actions; patchState merges fields into script state. HTML/network patchState replaces the source widget's state. For a Lua-returned patchWidget, itemStates is not supported; use the shared automationDispatch command or edit the saved widget record.
