title: Edit part of an HTML document
text:
# Edit part of an HTML document

An HTML widget is one WebView with its own HTML, CSS, JavaScript and state. Sections and `data-*` attributes are ordinary document content. Long press anywhere for whole-widget controls. Edit exposes the complete source. Delete removes the entire widget, so do not use it to remove one section.

1. Read the saved widget and identify the intended section and the JavaScript that renders it.
2. Change the relevant saved markup, CSS, JavaScript or state. Preserve sibling content and unrelated widget fields.
3. Submit the change through the shared widget patch action or a preserved complete configuration replacement. Page and widget locks apply.
4. Read back the widget and inspect its rendered result. Live DOM patches alone do not persist source edits.

Optional `selfWidget.item(id)` namespaces remain available for a document's own state and files. They do not create native child widgets. Complete reusable documents belong in the HTML widget library.

[HTML guide](dikciz://docs/guides/html).
aliases: edit delete inner HTML component long press DOM item wrapper

title: Inspect and act
text:
# Inspect and act

1. Read `dikciz_device_info` to identify the serving package and instance.
2. Read `dikciz_snapshot`. Find the intended semantic node and inspect its current state. Use discovery to locate the exact tap, text or long-press tool.
3. If another app is visible, use an Accessibility snapshot instead. If access is missing, follow [permission review](dikciz://docs/guides/permissions), then retry explicitly.
4. Act once on the current target. Preserve the returned command envelope and per-action outcome.
5. Read a fresh snapshot or display screenshot. Check the intended screen, package, value or persisted change before the next dependent action.

Use `waitFor` for a launcher node when rendering is asynchronous. A coordinate fallback needs a fresh Accessibility snapshot and visible screen coordinates. Never reuse coordinates after rotation, scrolling or window changes.

For screenshots, `dikciz_display_screenshot` returns the visible display with Accessibility access. `dikciz_screenshot` returns the launcher window. An image error is not evidence of the screen state.

If a click returns success but the screen does not change, inspect logs and the target's actual enabled/actionable state. Do not repeat a potentially destructive click blindly. For content inside an HTML widget, use [document source editing](dikciz://docs/recipes/html-item) rather than deleting the containing widget.
aliases: inspect screen screenshot find button click verify UI

title: Upload and install an APK
text:
# Upload and install an APK

1. Confirm the owner authorized the intended app installation. Choose an accessible absolute destination and create its parent directory if needed.
2. Upload the standalone APK in base64 `fileWrite` chunks of at most 256 KiB decoded. Start at offset zero; only overwrite an existing file when intended. Continue at each acknowledged `nextOffset`. The supplied CLI `upload` handles this over HTTP.
3. Call `apkInstall` with the path and optional complete-file SHA-256. If access is missing, request `installPackages` review or opt in with `autoRequestPermissions: true`. Tell the owner to review the phone, read fresh access status and retry explicitly.
4. Preserve `sessionId` from `preparing`. Poll `apkInstallStatus` through any entrypoint. `pending_user_action` requires Android confirmation. `submitted` is not final success.
5. Accept only final `succeeded` as Android installation success. Report `cancelled` or `failed` with the provided reason and status. Check the package version with `packageInfo` afterward.

Updating Dikciz itself can close listeners and invalidate sessions. Reconnect to a fresh MCP session and verify the serving package and version with `deviceInfo`. Do not uninstall the only controller to install its replacement. A force-stopped process cannot service its own recovery requests.

[Transfer contract](dikciz://docs/guides/files). [Restart and recovery](dikciz://docs/recipes/restart).
aliases: sideload install update upload Android package APK confirmation

title: Install a Lua script
text:
# Install a Lua script

Read `configGet` first and preserve its scripts, automation records and policies. Use a new valid ID, for example `example-events`, and confirm it does not already identify user work.

For an atomic installation, append a script object to the assembled `scripts` array with `id`, `title`, `enabled: true`, `apiVersion: 1`, `source` and initial `state: {}`. Append its policy and subscription objects to the existing `automation.policies` and `automation.scripts` arrays. Submit the complete preserved document with `configReplace`. Never replace an existing automation namespace with only the example.

For direct public-file installation, inspect an existing native-created script's `script.json` and manifest references first. Write `/sdcard/Dikciz/scripts/<id>/main.lua`, its matching metadata and state, and the policy and subscription files under `automation/`. Update the corresponding manifest references without dropping existing IDs. Use base64 file writes and create parents first. Wait for file observers to accept the complete tree.

The native Lua editor creates script source and metadata; it does not create a custom-event policy automatically. Enable the script, policy and subscription. Custom events require `manualTrigger`; returned actions require their policy allowlist and any Android access.

Verify `automationStatus`, read the normalized configuration, trigger the intended event, and inspect final run status, logs and saved state. Source upload success is not execution success.

[Pipeline setup](dikciz://docs/recipes/event-setup). [Lua guide](dikciz://docs/guides/lua).
aliases: upload install enable Lua automation script

title: Install an HTML widget
text:
# Install an HTML widget

1. Read the current selected page and its layout. Confirm the page is editable and has room.
2. Call `addWidget` with `widgetType: "html"`. It uses the first fitting free cells. Read the returned widget ID and address. Do not invent a placement argument at insertion.
3. Use `widgetMove` and `widgetResize` with logical `cell` values if a different placement is needed. Check bounds and collision outcomes.
4. Patch the widget through a typed `patchWidget` action using its actual `widgetAddress` and `values` containing `title`, `html`, `css`, `javascript`, `state` or `itemStates`.
5. Set `eventSubscriptions` through its saved public JSON record or a preserved complete configuration replacement. That field is not a typed widget-patch field.
6. Read the saved widget and inspect its rendered page. Use a persisted bridge acknowledgement when testing event delivery.

Do not replace the full home with a one-widget example. Read and preserve the current configuration before a complete replacement. Source edits can recreate the WebView, so wait for `dikciz-ready` in widget JavaScript. State-only patches send `dikciz-state` or `dikciz-item-state` without reloading the document. Give reusable cards unique `data-dikciz-item-id` values and use `selfWidget.itemFor(element)` for their state and files.

[HTML guide](dikciz://docs/guides/html). [Event receiver source](dikciz://docs/recipes/event-widget).
aliases: add create install HTML webview widget JavaScript CSS page state

title: Open an app reliably
text:
# Open an app reliably

1. Identify the running build with `deviceInfo` and read the current launcher snapshot.
2. Open the app drawer through its current semantic control. Read a new snapshot, locate the intended app by label and package, and use its exact `semanticId` with the discovered `launchApp` tool. This tests the same drawer action as a physical tap.
3. Read the launch outcome. If verification needs Accessibility, request owner review with `autoRequestPermissions: true` or `requestDeviceAccess`, then retry after a confirmed grant.
4. Inspect a fresh Accessibility snapshot or display screenshot. Confirm the destination package and its visible screen. A launch attempt, scheduled intent or Home remaining visible is not verified success.
5. To test resumption, navigate Home through a supported global action, inspect the native recent-app strip and resume the reported task. Verify the destination again.

If the app is absent, check `packageInfo` and Android profile visibility. If it appears then disappears, inspect crash or activity logs available to Dikciz. Do not claim every app's crash log is available without privileges. Preserve the exact launch error and access state.

[Apps guide](dikciz://docs/guides/apps). [UI guide](dikciz://docs/guides/ui).
aliases: open launch installed app verify foreground outcome

title: Change listener endpoints
text:
# Change listener endpoints

Read `/sdcard/Dikciz/control/ports.json` and `controlStatus` before changing the endpoint. Plan the next reachable address and ports first. If direct access is needed, configure and enable bearer authentication through the owner's native settings before exposing a network interface.

Save one complete port record:

```json
{"version":1,"listenAddress":"0.0.0.0","websocketPort":19001,"mcpPort":19002}
```

Use distinct valid ports and a numeric listen address. `0.0.0.0` listens on IPv4 interfaces. It is not a client destination. Use the phone's reachable hostname or IP in clients. A specific interface address must exist when binding. Deleting the record restores loopback defaults and can cut off network access.

The configuration watcher restarts listeners after a valid endpoint change, including while another app is in front. Existing sockets and MCP sessions can close. Reconnect at the new endpoint, initialize and inspect `controlStatus`. Verify the reported binding and actual connection from the intended controlling computer.

Tailscale policy must permit computer-to-phone TCP traffic on both selected ports. A tunnel ping or allowed reverse connection is insufficient. Keep phone and computer connected to the intended private network. A lab emulator port forward cannot prove the physical phone's direct network path works.

[Connection guide](dikciz://docs/guides/connect).
aliases: configure listen bind address port network 0.0.0.0 LAN Tailscale restart listener

title: Restart and reconnect
text:
# Restart and reconnect

1. Read `deviceInfo` and confirm the serving package is the intended release or debug installation.
2. Call `dikciz_restart` with no arguments. Preserve its `state: "scheduled"` and `instanceId` before the connection closes.
3. Reconnect to the same host and port, initialize a new MCP session and read `deviceInfo` until `application.instanceId` differs from the acknowledged value.
4. Verify the expected version, configuration and current Home state. A scheduled acknowledgement is not completed recovery.

Restart recreates the activity and listeners without killing the process or clearing saved configuration. It does not switch debug and release or alter Android's Home role. Use the separately discovered `launcherHandoff` operation for an authorized switch between installed builds and verify which package answers afterward.

APK replacement stops the old process. The package-replaced receiver restores automation and requests Home startup; default Home or overlay access permits automatic reopening when Android allows it. Manufacturer restrictions can still require tapping **Dikciz updated** or opening Dikciz manually. A socket cannot revive a force-stopped package.

Do not use the launcher's own shell to kill its only recovery path. [Discovery](dikciz://docs/guides/discovery) explains instance identity. [Connection](dikciz://docs/guides/connect) explains session recovery.
aliases: restart launcher reload updated APK reconnect services

title: Stream logcat
text:
# Stream logcat

Use a bounded diagnostic window or retain the stream's ownership information so it can be stopped. For ordinary app-visible logs:

```json
{"command":"logcat -v threadtime","root":false,"timeoutMilliseconds":60000}
```

Pass this to MCP `dikciz_shell_stream`, or HTTP/WebSocket `shellStream`. The supplied CLI supports `--stream-raw` to print decoded bytes as they arrive. Without it, the CLI emits JSON Lines. Ordinary `shell` is a single bounded response and has a 30-second default deadline.

An MCP client must keep the same session and request `info` or `debug` in `params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]`, alongside the negotiated protocol metadata. Read SSE `notifications/message` records from logger `dikciz.shell`, then the final tool result. The supplied client handles this automatically.

Preserve the `streamId` from `started`. Output events carry increasing `sequence` and base64 `outputBase64`. A complete event includes final state, exit code and output bytes. Stop through `dikciz_shell_stream_stop` in the same MCP session, or close the originating response. Closing the stream stops its owned process group. A new session cannot cancel another session's stream.

Unprivileged logcat reports only what Android permits the app to read. Request root only when authorized and available. Streams do not replay after reconnect. Keep credentials and unrelated private logs out of shared diagnostics.

[Streaming contract](dikciz://docs/guides/shell).
aliases: continuous stream Android logcat debug logs stop cancellation

title: GPS todo app
text:
# GPS todo app

Dikciz > Apps > Travel todo opens a complete editable example under /sdcard/Dikciz/apps/travel-todo/. The manifest, ui.html, ui.css, ui.js and main.js are the reference source. Initial tasks include Go to New York. No geofence is created on installation or opening.

Read customAppRead appId travel-todo before edits. Use customAppControl action open to request UI; inspect uiVisible/snapshot for actual presentation. The UI sends customAppEvent events todo.open, todo.add payload {title}, todo.toggle payload {id}, todo.watch and todo.stop. Backend returned patchState persists the full list. ui.js listens for dikciz-state and redraws it.

Only start monitoring when the owner asks. Grant precise foreground location using requestDeviceAccess requirementId locationForeground and enable device location. todo.watch creates geofenceSave id travel-todo-nyc, latitude 40.7128, longitude -74.0060, radiusMeters 20000, enabled true. This circle is an example destination, not an exact city boundary. Android location and foreground-service restrictions apply.

The manifest subscribes to geofence.enter. Its payload has id/title/location. main.js ignores other fence IDs and inactive watches, checks only task new-york and deletes its fence after arrival. This runs with the UI closed. Reopen to inspect persisted state. The notification shows native location monitoring. todo.stop and app.stopped delete the owned fence without changing other geofences.

For another event-driven task, publish example.todo.complete with payload {id:"pack"} through automationDispatch with an actual HTML sourceWidgetAddress and an emitEvent action. The backend checks that exact task. Such custom events are owner automation inputs, not proof of physical arrival. Do not publish synthetic geofence events and describe them as GPS evidence.

No messages, calendar entries or external model calls are needed. Task text is rendered using textContent. It uses geofenceSave/geofenceDelete/requestDeviceAccess; legacy command metadata does not restrict its shared Dikciz access. Duplicate with a different app ID for separate state and a separate <app-id>-nyc fence. Export sources only; current encrypted home/chat backups exclude apps. Full walkthrough: docs/todo-app-tutorial.md in the repository.

title: Agent integrations
text:
# Agent integrations

The Android APK is the MCP server. Each owner supplies a reachable phone endpoint such as `http://phone.example:19002/mcp` and, when enabled, an owner credential or scoped bearer token. There is no shared hosted phone service. The plugin supplies operating instructions; the MCP connection points directly to the installed launcher. Use [private-network setup](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb) first.

title: Agent integrations: Assistant inside the launcher
text:
## Assistant inside the launcher

Dikciz also has its own [on-device chat](embedded-chat.md). Add an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible provider connection in the cheese panel, choose its API models per conversation, and configure token budgets or read-only access under Model settings. That agent discovers the existing local MCP tools and documentation directly; external MCP clients still connect as described below. Its profiles, conversations, event rules and visibility use the shared `dikciz_chat` tool.

title: Agent integrations: Find procedures and tool contracts
text:
## Find procedures and tool contracts

Use `dikciz_search_query` with collection `docs` for relevant operating guides and recipes, then read the exact returned documentation URI. Collection `tools` returns ranked installed schemas directly. Reuse current contracts while the build and access context remain unchanged. The embedded assistant exposes `phone_search` and uses the same engine for `phone_tools`. Search is local and requires no embedding model. See [offline search](search.md) for separate owner collections, aliases, spelling correction and access rules.

title: Agent integrations: Codex
text:
## Codex

The repository skill is available from `.agents/skills/dikciz-launcher/`. The Codex plugin manifest packages those instructions. Add the phone as a separate Streamable HTTP server using the real endpoint:

```bash
codex mcp add dikciz --url http://phone.example:19002/mcp --bearer-token-env-var DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN
```

Load the token into that environment variable from your secret store before starting Codex. Omit the bearer option only when phone authentication is disabled. This command configures the client, not the phone listener. It does not install the APK or grant Android access.

title: Agent integrations: Claude Code
text:
## Claude Code

The Claude plugin declares `mcp_url` and sensitive `bearer_token` user configuration. Set the URL to your phone's complete `/mcp` endpoint and the token to the selected bearer credential. Its MCP mapping uses those values, not a maintainer endpoint. Without the plugin, configure a remote HTTP MCP entry with the same URL and `Authorization` header in your private client configuration. Do not place actual credentials in repository settings.

From a repository checkout, load the local plugin with:

```bash
claude --plugin-dir .agents
```

The manifests are packaged under `.agents/`. Marketplace publication requires the corresponding central catalog entries to be released. Do not treat an unlisted plugin as already installable by marketplace name.

title: Agent integrations: Other MCP clients
text:
## Other MCP clients

Use Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. Modern clients use stateless discovery; legacy clients initialize and use their negotiated session. List tools and fetch `dikciz://docs/index` through resources. Follow resource pagination. Prefer focused guides and recipes over reading every section. Authentication is a static bearer credential, not OAuth. Endpoints have no built-in TLS; use an encrypted private network or a correctly configured HTTPS gateway.

title: Agent integrations: Operating contract
text:
## Operating contract

1. Read `deviceInfo` and `controlStatus` to identify package, version, supported commands and listeners.
2. Inspect `automationStatus` for Android access. Set `autoRequestPermissions` only when owner review is intended, then explicitly retry after access changes.
3. Read fresh snapshots and use returned identities. Prefer direct data and hardware commands to UI tapping when implemented.
4. Treat acceptance, submission, completion and actual observed effects separately. Poll SMS and APK status. Reconnect and compare launcher instance IDs after restart.
5. Read the requested outcome back. Respect unavailable hardware, secure windows, app sandboxing and Android privilege boundaries.

No plugin lifecycle hook runs a local shell or installs an Android package. Explicit MCP tool calls can act with the phone's granted permissions. File writes, shell, SMS, app installation and configuration reset require the owner's requested scope. Sensitive phone data stays between the phone and the configured client except when a requested operation sends it elsewhere, such as SMS or the selected system speech provider.

title: Agent integrations: Directory metadata
text:
## Directory metadata

`glama.json` identifies the repository maintainer for Glama ownership. It is not proof that a listing has been submitted, reviewed or approved. A private phone address is not a public hosted MCP endpoint. Public catalog submissions must describe installation of the APK and user-supplied connection settings accurately.

The official registry descriptor uses its embedded-application format and links to installation instructions. It advertises no shared remote URL and no invented npm or Docker package. A tag-gated OIDC job publishes metadata only after APK release. Schema validity does not establish publication or directory approval; those are checked after release.

Use a separate [named token](remote-access-tokens.md) for each external agent. Read `dikciz_remote_access_info` and discover its filtered catalog before invoking tools. A denied call cannot gain additional access through a different transport. Built-in chat retains its direct owner binding and independent read-only checks.

title: Android access and execution boundaries
text:
# Android access and execution boundaries

Dikciz acts with the Android identity and grants of its installed package. HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and enabled Lua ordinary commands share validation, Android access checks and outcomes. Root, network reachability, bearer authentication, Android permissions, special access, foreground state and hardware availability are separate checks.

Read `deviceInfo` for the serving package/version, `controlStatus` or `tools/list` for supported commands, `automationStatus.deviceAccess.requirements` for current setup and `nativeDataStatus` for provider columns and grants. Discover the installed build, not just the latest repository documentation. Release and debug packages have independent Android grants.

title: Android access and execution boundaries: Feature access map
text:
## Feature access map

This map describes prerequisites, not permission grants. Android version, hardware, provider ownership and device policy can further restrict an operation.

| Feature | Access and execution requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Home, pages, files, widgets and Lua | Shared-storage access for the public home; file APIs also use app-sandbox access. Scripts and widgets execute only when enabled and configured. Native provider widgets need Android binding/configuration approval. |
| Remote controls | A reachable running listener, allowed network route, configured bearer credential and accepted Origin. The default bind is phone loopback; direct private access requires an appropriate listen address. |
| Contacts and calendars | Corresponding read/write Android grants and the allowlisted resource/columns. Only raw contacts, contact data, calendar events and reminders are writable. Account/provider rules remain in force. |
| SMS | Read SMS for history, Receive SMS for incoming events, Send SMS for outgoing messages; SIM discovery can additionally need phone-state access. No default SMS role is requested. Tracked sends need a caller idempotency key. |
| Own SIM phone numbers | `READ_PHONE_STATE` lists subscriptions; `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS` reads their numbers. The `phoneNumbers` review requests these read permissions only. Missing number permission preserves SIM metadata with explicit status; Android may supply no number despite a grant. |
| Calls, call history and USSD | Phone/call-history grants as reported by discovery. Place/USSD need call access; answering/ending depend on Android version, role and policy. USSD is a real carrier operation and may have an unknown outcome after timeout. |
| Clipboard | Android foreground/default-input-method rules can block reads. A declared grant does not create unrestricted background clipboard access. |
| Notifications and media sessions | Owner-enabled notification-listener special access for reading/control; Android posting access for Dikciz notifications. Do Not Disturb policy access is separate. Inline replies can send messages through the originating app. |
| UI across apps | Owner-enabled Dikciz Accessibility service. Node/gesture actions need fresh snapshots; stale windows are refused. Secure windows and Android UI restrictions still apply. |
| Screenshots | Launcher-window screenshot is distinct from actual-display capture. `displayScreenshot` needs Android 11+ and Accessibility; it cannot bypass secure-window restrictions. |
| Locking | `lockDevice` needs Device Administration; Accessibility global lock uses that separate service and supported Android version. |
| Sensors and Health Connect | Ordinary sensors may need no runtime grant; restricted sensors can need body-sensor/activity-recognition access. Inspect each sensor's requirement/reason. Health Connect availability and daily-step read consent are separate from generic body-sensor permission. |
| Location, geocoding and GNSS | Appropriate coarse/fine location access and enabled providers; background subscriptions can need separate background access. GNSS status needs precise access and an actual callback. Geocoding can send queries/coordinates to Android's provider. |
| Photos and video | Camera grant, foreground eligibility and available camera. Audio-enabled video additionally owns microphone access. These commands provide bounded capture, not a preview or background video service. |
| Microphone and recognition | Microphone grant, foreground eligibility at start and exclusive microphone ownership. Managed/bounded recording and recognition remain foreground operations. PCM streaming can continue under its dedicated microphone foreground service; Android privacy controls still apply. |
| Speech and local playback | Available TTS engine or readable audio file and permitted audio focus/routing. Network-required voices and system speech recognition can use a provider's network service. Strict on-device recognition never silently falls back to it. |
| Torch and vibration | Flash/vibrator hardware. Torch changes need camera access; Android haptic settings can suppress vibration. Submission is not measured physical output. |
| Selected system settings | Owner-granted Modify system settings for writes to the explicit allowlist. Read-back shows stored values, not proof that automatic brightness/rotation or device policy obeyed them. |
| Bluetooth | Enabled adapter; Android 12+ scan/connect grants as needed, older scan location requirements, and peer pairing/security. No silent radio enablement or persistent connections. |
| Wi-Fi | Fine location and applicable location/scan services. Android throttling remains. Cached results are separate from a requested scan; neither API changes networks. |
| NFC | Available/enabled adapter, foreground unlocked Dikciz and a presented compatible tag. NDEF and raw ISO-DEP are different formats. No EMV decoder, persistent tag sessions or card emulation. |
| USB host | Attached peripheral, Android approval for that device and supported endpoint/interface. Per-device access expires on disconnect. This is not ADB or fastboot access to the phone. |
| APK install/update | Owner-approved installation from Dikciz plus Android installer confirmation when required. Standalone APK support does not imply split-APK support or silent installation. |
| Shell, root and other apps' data | `root:false` uses the app UID, not the ADB shell UID. Root defaults true and requires a working approved `su`; denial does not fall back. No Shizuku backend is implemented. |

Use [native data](native-device-control.md), [hardware controls](hardware-controls.md) and the [documentation index](index.md) for each operation's fields, errors and limits.

title: Android access and execution boundaries: Request missing access
text:
## Request missing access

Use requirement IDs from live discovery. `requestDeviceAccess` asks for one requirement explicitly. Ordinary commands default to `autoRequestPermissions:false`; opting into true requests owner review only for missing access encountered by that operation. It does not open every permission screen.

Inspect `permissionRequest.state`, `requirementId`, `notificationPosted`, `promptState`, `retryRequired`, `deduplicated` and `instructions`. Tell the owner which review to complete. Check access again and explicitly retry the authorized operation. A notification or closed Android dialog is not proof of a grant. Partial batches can already have completed actions.

The complete **Settings**, **Automation**, **Set up full device access** checklist is a separate task that survives another Settings panel taking the foreground. It refreshes actual grants on return. Optional or unsupported requirements can remain unmet; that does not imply unrelated commands are broken.

title: Android access and execution boundaries: Entrypoints and persistence
text:
## Entrypoints and persistence

| Interface or operation | Delivery and lifetime |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP/WebSocket/MCP ordinary commands | Shared command results and errors inside transport-specific envelopes. MCP resources are packaged documentation and exist only on MCP. |
| Persistent WebSocket events | Push while the connection and listener remain alive. Disconnect is not durable delivery. |
| Network `shellStream` | Connection/session-owned push output; HTTP/MCP use SSE. Disconnect stops the owned process. HTML/Lua cannot receive this streaming transport. |
| Shell sessions, event journal and PCM streams | Ordinary cursor reads, including HTML/Lua, with bounded process-memory replay and explicit gaps. They survive network reconnects; process death loses history. Each feature has its own capacity and cleanup rules. |
| Durable command jobs | App-private persisted arguments/results and caller idempotency; interrupted work is not replayed automatically. Cancellation does not undo external effects. |
| HTML rendering and scripts | HTML visible interaction/polling uses native visibility. Lua and headless JavaScript handle configured background events; complete apps can subscribe through their native host. None creates an Android permission or an unlimited background-execution exemption. |
| Activity restart and APK update | `restart` recreates the activity within the same process. APK replacement kills the old process; listeners need reconnection and process-owned histories are lost. Public saved configuration survives compatible updates. |

Read the operation's terminal status. Request acceptance is not verified app launch, message delivery, successful install or measured camera/audio quality. A client timeout can leave external work with an unknown outcome; do not repeat it blindly.

title: Android access and execution boundaries: Credentials and privilege limits
text:
## Credentials and privilege limits

File commands deny `/sdcard/Dikciz/control/remote-auth.json`, its atomic `.bak`/`.new` aliases, record lock and canonical aliases. File management also refuses moves/deletes of containing ancestors. HTTP binary transfers use the same file-command checks. This restriction covers those APIs, not an independently authorized shell: an app-UID or root shell can access what its Android identity permits. The verifier is not guaranteed ADB-only.

Enabling a Lua script or installing trusted HTML gives its command binding owner authority. Lua returned-action policies control automatic delivery and returned typed actions; they do not sandbox `context.request`. Keep untrusted code out of enabled scripts/widgets. Safe mode blocks ordinary mutations while preserving documented diagnostics and recovery.

Dikciz does not expose every Android SDK method. Ordinary permissions do not grant cellular call-audio capture/injection, silent grants, arbitrary private databases or protected system settings. Camera/microphone privacy controls remain active. A stopped app cannot revive itself over its absent listener; fastboot/bootloader modes run outside the Android process. The [coverage table](capability-coverage.md) lists remaining implementations separately from platform restrictions.

[Named access tokens](remote-access-tokens.md) restrict remote clients before Android access checks. Grants are separate from Android permissions and from local chat read-only mode. Shell, SDK and scripting authority require owner access because they can bypass narrower data grants.

title: Public Android SDK bridge
text:
# Public Android SDK bridge

The shared Android SDK bridge supplements the dedicated [native commands](native-device-control.md). `androidApiDiscover` indexes the pinned API 36 public SDK, including exact overloads, positional types, nullability, permission annotations and inheritance. A catalogue entry does not grant permissions or prove that a method exists on the running Android version. Inspect `bridgePermitted` and `runtimeAvailable` before execution. Hidden and private APIs are outside this contract.

MCP, HTTP, WebSocket, HTML and Lua execute these commands through the same native target. MCP names use `dikciz_android_api_` followed by `discover`, `read`, `invoke`, `objects`, `callback` or `release`. The [command reference](command-reference.md) records request schemas. The packaged guide is `dikciz://docs/guides/android-sdk`.
aliases: Android framework API methods signatures network statistics traffic mobile data usage

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Discover before calling
text:
## Discover before calling

Omit `className` to list classes, or supply an exact name to list its public members and inherited overloads. `query` is a literal case-insensitive filter. Lists use `offset`, `limit` and `hasMore`; the default page is 50, the maximum 200. Continue with offset plus the number of returned items. Method IDs include erased positional parameter types, such as `getPhoneNumber(int)`. Constructors use `new(...)`; field reads use `field:NAME`. A mutable field is set with `set:NAME` through the writable invocation command.

```json
{"type":"androidApiDiscover","className":"android.os.BatteryManager","query":"getIntProperty"}
```

```json
{"type":"androidApiRead","className":"android.os.BatteryManager","member":"getIntProperty(int)","target":"service:batterymanager","arguments":[4]}
```

Battery property 4 is Android BATTERY_PROPERTY_CAPACITY. Prefer discovering constants over assuming other numeric SDK values. Existing `deviceState` provides a higher-level battery result.

Instance targets are `context`, `activity`, `service:NAME`, or an `objectRef` returned by an earlier call. Use the public SDK class name, even when Android returns a hidden implementation subclass. Static members and constructors reject a target. `arguments` is always required, including an empty array for no arguments. No overload is guessed.

Primitive values, explicit nulls, enum names and arrays are accepted according to the exact parameter type. Object tags are `{"objectRef":"ID"}`, `{"className":"PUBLIC_SDK_CLASS"}`, `{"long":"SIGNED_DECIMAL"}`, `{"bytesBase64":"BASE64"}` and `{"arrayType":"COMPONENT_TYPE","values":[...]}`. Nested calls and arbitrary object maps are rejected. Null is rejected for primitives and explicitly non-null parameters. Integral narrowing checks overflow. Results outside JavaScript integer precision use the decimal long tag.

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Read-only access
text:
## Read-only access

The conversation access flag is executor metadata, not an argument supplied by the model. Every call rechecks saved access, so enabling read-only access during a running turn blocks subsequent writes immediately. A settings patch containing only readOnly:true is accepted during an active turn; other settings changes require stopping it first. Read-only agents see only approved read tools. SDK discovery also removes mutating and unaudited members. `androidApiRead` independently requires its exact member to be approved, even for a writable caller. A write sent through that command returns `read_only_violation` before resolving its target, arguments or permissions. Setters, writable invocations, callback creation and handle release are hidden and blocked in read-only conversations. `autoRequestPermissions: true` is also rejected in read-only mode.

New members default to write access. The explicit policy is [read-policy.json](../app/src/dikciz/sdk/read-policy.json). Names beginning with `get`, `is` or `read` do not imply safety. Approved constructors create data-only output holders, such as ActivityManager.MemoryInfo. Reading an SDK output holder can update that in-memory holder without changing phone configuration.
aliases: Android framework API methods signatures network statistics traffic mobile data usage

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Invocation and outcomes
text:
## Invocation and outcomes

`androidApiInvoke` requires an `idempotencyKey`. Identical requests reuse the first invocation; changed arguments with the same key fail. Pre-dispatch validation and annotated missing-permission failures do not reserve a key. Android rejections and completed attempts remain cached. Keys remain in memory until process exit, with a 1024-entry capacity. They survive activity recreation. Use [command jobs](command-jobs.md) when durable submission/results are required. Neither layer automatically repeats an interrupted Android side effect after process death.

The wait timeout defaults to 30000 milliseconds and accepts 1 through 300000. `thread` is `auto`, `main` or `background`. Auto follows SDK UiThread/MainThread annotations, which are not present on every platform method. At most two background SDK workers execute concurrently, with a bounded queue. A timeout reports unknown completion. Android operations already running cannot be rolled back; retrying the identical write key observes the original operation. An SDK `completed` state means the method returned. It does not turn an asynchronous submission into a verified external effect.

SDK exceptions become stable access-denied, unsupported, argument-rejected, unavailable or failed outcomes. Exception text and argument values stay out of logs. Permission annotations describe declared requirements; Android is authoritative about runtime grants, AppOps, roles, foreground eligibility and privileged permissions. Known permission families use the same opt-in owner review as dedicated commands. No API grants access silently.
aliases: Android framework API methods signatures network statistics traffic mobile data usage

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Handles, callbacks and cleanup
text:
## Handles, callbacks and cleanup

Nonprimitive results receive process-owned handles. There are at most 256 live handles. They survive launcher activity recreation, but not process death or APK replacement. Release unused handles with `androidApiRelease`. `close: true` explicitly calls AutoCloseable.close when supported. Unregister listeners, stop capture and close sessions through the corresponding SDK methods before releasing their handles. Releasing a reference does not undo Android side effects.

Inline list/array previews contain at most 16 elements; longer text includes an explicit preview marker. `androidApiObjects` pages complete indexed array/list/map or text contents by objectRef. Text offsets count UTF-16 code units. Large bytes remain available through indexed reads. List contents may change between calls; this is not a transactional snapshot.

`androidApiCallback` creates a public SDK interface proxy or a generated subclass of a public non-final SDK callback class. Select its exact constructor and arguments when `new()` is insufficient. `returns` must provide explicit constant values for non-void callback overloads. Callback methods record events, never execute supplied commands. Read them with `androidApiObjects`, `objectRef` and `afterSequence`. Each callback retains at most 256 events; `droppedEvents` and `gap` report loss. The automation bus also receives the custom event `android_api_callback`, with objectRef, overload, sequence and arguments. Unregister before release.
aliases: Android framework API methods signatures network statistics traffic mobile data usage

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Protected boundaries
text:
## Protected boundaries

The generic bridge excludes reflection, dynamic class loading, raw filesystem/database/content-provider access and launcher internals. Protected credential paths return android_api_protected_path without suggesting that an Android permission grant can bypass the restriction. Use the existing protected file, provider, shell and HTML commands for those tasks. Public Context/Activity access is restricted to selected service, permission and resource getters. SDK class discovery still describes excluded APIs honestly through `bridgePermitted: false`. Android version, optional modules, hardware, permissions and callback-constructor restrictions can prevent execution. This bridge does not claim unrestricted Android access or complete device testing of every catalogue member.
aliases: Android framework API methods signatures network statistics traffic mobile data usage

title: Public Android SDK bridge: Source and dependency verification
text:
## Source and dependency verification

[source.json](../app/src/dikciz/sdk/source.json) pins the official AOSP public signatures by commit and SHA-256. `make dikciz-android-sdk` regenerates deterministic indexed assets; `ANDROID_SDK_SOURCE=relative/path/android.txt` uses a supplied source file while enforcing the same checksum. `make dikciz-android-sdk-test` checks parsing, exact types, policy entries, checksums, offsets and repeatability. Do not edit generated assets by hand.

Callback subclasses use LinkedIn DexMaker 2.28.6 and its repackaged Dalvik DX 9.0.0_r3 dependency, both Apache-2.0. [Pinned dependency metadata](../gradle/dikciz-sdk-dependencies.json) records the downloaded artifacts and hashes. Dikciz debug, release and minified builds verify the JAR checksums before compiling. SDK signatures come from the [AOSP SDK repository](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/prebuilts/sdk/).
