title: Dikciz configuration: HTML instance state and files
text:
### HTML instance state and files

The complete ownership path is `/sdcard/Dikciz/pages/<page-id>/widgets/<webview-id>/items/<instance-id>/`. `selfWidget.storagePath` identifies the wrapper directory. `selfWidget.itemFor(element)` resolves the nearest saved `data-dikciz-item-id`, while `selfWidget.item(id)` selects that instance explicitly. An instance exposes `state`, `getState()`, `patchState(values)`, `storagePath`, `readFile(name, options)` and `writeFile(name, dataBase64, options)`. State patches replace that instance's object while preserving its siblings. Native edits and automation state patches read the latest saved configuration inside a shared file transaction, preserving unrelated state during concurrent changes. File methods accept basenames; use `patchState` for the reserved `state.json`.

Card state changes deliver `dikciz-item-state`, whose detail is the wrapper's current item-state map. `selfWidget.itemStates` and each instance's `state` getter update without reloading the WebView. Valid external edits to a wrapper or card state file use the same watcher. Malformed state retains the last valid running home. Instance IDs use 1 to 80 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. A wrapper accepts at most 1024 instance states; normal configuration size and state-value limits also apply.

Optional item-state namespaces remain available to document scripts. Removing their HTML marker and state entry removes their owned files on save. Deleting a wrapper removes its descriptor and owned state directory. Moving the same wrapper ID to another page moves its owned files with it. Adding a complete template creates fresh state; saving a library package excludes live state. The `.dikciz-widget` marker identifies wrapper directories owned by Dikciz for cleanup. Files outside those owned directories remain untouched.

title: Dikciz configuration: Private chat settings
text:
## Private chat settings

Provider connections, encrypted API credentials and conversation model/token settings live in the app's private chat database, separately from the public home tree. Add a provider once, select its API models from the chat dropdown, and edit budgets/reasoning through Model settings. Home reset does not clear these records. The database upgrade preserves existing providers, keys and conversations and adds independent conversation overrides. See [embedded chat](embedded-chat.md) for the shared API and settings fields.

Embedded chat supports per-conversation `settings:{"readOnly":true}`. Discovery hides mutating tools and the trusted executor flag blocks direct writes and permission prompts with `read_only_violation`. Tool arguments cannot disable it. Chat history and logs still save; other owner entrypoints retain their configured access. See the embedded chat guide for the full contract.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant
text:
# On-device Dikciz assistant

Tap the cheese beside the launcher controls to open chat. It starts at half height; the resize button expands it to the available screen. Closing the panel leaves a running turn active. Hidden replies and subscribed events add an unread badge; reply notifications reopen the conversation. Android notification access controls whether those notifications appear.

The native panel renders streamed Markdown, including headings, lists, code fences, tables and strikethrough. Reasoning and tool records expand on a tap. Scrolling up stops automatic scrolling; **Latest** resumes it. The panel resizes above the keyboard. Quick-task buttons sit above a divider; the conversation scrolls within its own padded viewport, keeping message text clear of the controls. Conversation selection, creation, renaming, provider changes and deletion are available from its header. Stop a busy conversation before changing its provider or deleting it.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Background activity and Stop
text:
## Background activity and Stop

Open the notification shade in any app and tap **Open chat** on **Dikciz chat**. This quiet ongoing shortcut opens the normal half-screen conversation over that app, including while the assistant is idle. It does not keep an extra service running and does not require overlay access for a user-initiated tap. Opening it does not send a message. With no configured conversation, it opens the first-run chat instead.

Tap **Explain this screen** from that panel to dismiss chat and capture the app underneath. Notification permission and the **Chat shortcut** channel must be enabled. Android channel settings can hide the shortcut; reopening Home refreshes it after permission changes or dismissal. Android force-stop and device restart still follow normal app/notification lifecycle rules.

While a turn runs, the **Dikciz is working** notification shows its current phase: thinking, writing a reply, finding tools, reading the screen or running a phone tool. It updates quietly in place and contains no prompt, tool arguments, screen contents or reply text. Tap it to reopen that exact conversation, including when another conversation was previously selected.

The notification's **Stop** action uses the same cancellation path as the chat panel and shared command API. It shows **Stopping** and cancels active and queued work in that conversation. Already completed phone actions remain completed, and a synchronous Android operation may finish before cancellation takes effect. A notification from an earlier turn cannot cancel a newer turn. Stop does not delete history, disable event subscriptions or undo phone changes.

After work ends, the active notification disappears when no event rules remain, or returns to waiting for configured events. Hidden replies still have their separate notification. Android's notification permission and channel settings must allow notifications to see these controls; denying them does not prevent opening chat and stopping work there.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Quick tasks
text:
## Quick tasks

**Make me a widget** opens a description field. Describe the result, then tap **Create**. Dikciz saves the current page identity with the queued request and asks the selected model to build a complete HTML/CSS/JavaScript document with independent widget state through the existing phone tools. It preserves existing content and reports missing, locked or full pages. Widget creation requires writable conversation access. Inspect the generated widget and tool results; the model can fail or leave a partial result.

**Explain this screen** uses an optional question from the composer. It hides chat, waits for dismissal, captures the visible Android display and reads its accessibility tree before contacting the provider. The capture becomes an image attachment in the private chat transcript. This turn exposes and executes only read-only tools even if the conversation normally permits writes. It does not change that conversation's saved access setting. Chat requests reopening when the turn finishes; Android background-activity restrictions still apply. A new screen task is rejected while other assistant work is active, so it cannot silently capture a much later screen. Missing screenshot access fails visibly without a provider request. Secure windows, lock screens and Android capture limits still apply.

These shortcuts use the configured model and can incur API usage. Screen explanation requires a model that accepts image input. Captured screen data goes to that provider and remains in the private conversation history. Opening chat from Home explains Home; to inspect another app, open that app and request the task through the remote API or show chat over it through the shared visibility command.

All ordinary entrypoints accept the same task request:

```json
{"action":"task","task":"widget","conversationId":"CONVERSATION_ID","requestKey":"UNIQUE_REQUEST_KEY","text":"Create a small editable note widget."}
```

Use `task: "explainScreen"` with an optional `text` question for screen explanation. HTTP adds `type: "chatControl"`; MCP uses `dikciz_chat`. The response reports queue identity, not completion. Poll `read`. Reusing a key with the same task and text returns the existing turn without recapture or generation; changed content returns `chat_request_conflict`. Capture and tool failures remain in the transcript. Cancelling a screen task does not request reopening.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Connect a provider
text:
## Connect a provider

Tap the header gear, then **Add provider**. Choose **OpenAI**, **Anthropic** or **Custom** from **Provider template**. OpenAI and Anthropic fill their standard API base URL and protocol. Custom lets you enter your own HTTP or HTTPS base URL and choose the compatible protocol. Enter the API key and save the connection. Switching templates clears any key typed into the form; existing saved keys still follow the host/protocol retention rules below. Create or select a conversation using that connection, then use the **Chat model** dropdown to choose from its API catalogue. **Refresh chat models** fetches the current list again. Each conversation can choose a different model from the same provider without copying its connection or key. If discovery is unavailable or a private model is not listed, enter its exact ID under **Tune** (model settings). A conversation without a model cannot send messages or enable event rules.

Model limits come first from provider discovery, then from the bundled exact-ID catalog. OpenAI's Models API does not report token limits, so its documented models use that catalog. Anthropic and compatible hosts can supply context and output metadata directly. Unknown IDs show unavailable limits and keep manual budgets. Discovery follows all bounded model pages; refreshing discovery or opening a conversation never rewrites its saved budgets. Cached provider limits survive launcher restarts and are invalidated when the connection is edited.

The native model settings show the known context/output ceilings. Selecting a model or typing a known ID fills its context size. The editable reply reserve stays at the current value when it fits; it is reduced when needed to leave room for the safety margin and summary. An inherited thinking budget that no longer fits is disabled. Providing explicit context/output values in `create` or `configure` keeps those values. Re-selecting a known model without token fields restores its context default. A separate documented input ceiling also bounds outbound chat and summary requests.

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Protocol | `openai` uses streaming Chat Completions; `anthropic` uses streaming Messages. These are wire protocols, including compatible hosts. |
| API base URL | Owner-selected HTTP or HTTPS host, optionally ending in `/v1`. Use HTTPS for public providers. HTTP supports private local/VPN endpoints. Credentials in the URL, query strings and fragments are rejected; redirects are disabled. |
| API key | Stored separately from public profile data, encrypted with Android Keystore AES-GCM. Reads omit it. Blank in an existing profile's UI retains the key. An explicit empty `apiKey` in the API clears it. Changing host or protocol without explicitly supplying a replacement clears the old key. |
| Read-only phone access | Boolean `readOnly`, default `false`. Filters tool discovery and enforces access in the executor for this conversation. |
| Model ID | Per-conversation model selected in the API-backed dropdown or entered manually. Selecting a known model fills its context window and clamps the current reply reserve to its output ceiling and available input space. Explicit context/output values in the same request win. Unknown models retain the current budgets. |
| Total context tokens | Combined input and output allowance, filled from known model limits when selecting a model. Unknown models start at `131072`; manual values remain editable. |
| Maximum output | Actual provider output cap and reserved reply allowance, default `4096`. |
| Context policy | `drop-oldest` or `summarize`. See below. |
| Summary model | Optional model ID at the same provider. Blank uses the chat model. It must support the configured context size. |
| Summary output | Summary response cap, default `2048`. |
| Reasoning | `auto` leaves provider defaults. OpenAI-compatible hosts receive an explicit `reasoning_effort` for other values; supported values depend on the model. Anthropic accepts `none`, or adaptive thinking with `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`, where the model supports that effort. |
| Thinking tokens | Anthropic explicit thinking budget. Use at least `1024`, less than maximum output, with reasoning `auto`. `0` leaves the provider default. |
| OpenAI output field | [`max_completion_tokens`](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create) by default. Choose `max_tokens` for compatible hosts requiring it. Only the selected field is sent. |
| Maximum rounds | Default `32` provider/tool rounds per turn. Exhaustion is a visible failure. |
| Turn timeout | Default `300000` milliseconds for the complete turn, including tool work and compaction. |
| Context safety margin | Default `1024` reserved tokens beyond the output allowance. |
| Additional system instructions | Owner instructions appended to the built-in Dikciz identity and phone-operation rules. |

**Tune** opens model settings for the current conversation and edits its context size, maximum output/reply reserve, reasoning, thinking budget, compaction, summary model/output, timeout, tool-round limit, safety margin and additional instructions. These values do not change another conversation or create another provider. Changes require an idle conversation; stop active work first. Switching to a different provider retains read-only access and resets the other conversation overrides to that provider's defaults so incompatible model/thinking settings do not carry over.

No provider is contacted until a model-discovery request, owner message or configured event requires it. A model with different reasoning or token constraints can reject a profile; inspect the visible failed turn and correct its settings.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Conversations and context
text:
## Conversations and context

Android SQLite stores shared provider connections, independent conversation settings, full messages, reasoning, tool calls/results, queue state and summaries in private app storage. Outbound context selection never deletes the transcript. Uninstalling or clearing app data removes this database and its keys. Home-page resets do not reset chat history.

Existing profiles keep their model and budget defaults. The database upgrade adds conversation overrides without deleting messages, subscriptions, provider IDs or encrypted credentials. Provider edits retain existing defaults; models and tokens are edited per conversation in the native UI. A running turn uses one connection/settings snapshot.

Before every provider request, Dikciz subtracts maximum output and the safety margin from total context. It estimates input conservatively using UTF-8 bytes, framing and tool-schema allowances, plus an image allowance. This is not the provider's exact tokenizer or billing count. Set a larger margin when a host has extra framing or image costs.

`drop-oldest` removes complete old exchanges from the outgoing request until it fits. `summarize` sends a completed old prefix to the summary model, saves its summary and checkpoint, then continues with that summary and recent complete exchanges. The summary request reserves its own output allowance. Current user input and current tool results stay together. If they cannot fit, the turn fails explicitly. Failed summaries leave original history available. Switching provider/model omits incompatible saved reasoning on replay. Anthropic thinking signatures, omitted-text blocks and redacted blocks are retained for tool continuations and later turns; opaque thinking is never decrypted. See the provider's [thinking contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking).

Failed, cancelled and interrupted requests remain available to later turns under both context policies, together with completed tool results. Replayed tool calls always have a matching result. A call interrupted before its result was saved receives an explicit unknown-outcome result, which is context only and never re-executes the action. Queued future requests stay out of the current turn.

Queue records survive process death. Active generation or tool execution becomes **interrupted**, with no automatic replay of uncertain side effects. Queued work resumes when the launcher/service reconnects. A foreground service keeps active work and configured event listeners visible to Android; force-stop, system restrictions, revoked access or unavailable networking can still interrupt them. Read actual tool results before retrying.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Phone tools and visibility
text:
## Phone tools and visibility

Enable **Read-only phone access** in **Model settings**, or configure `settings:{"readOnly":true}` through any entrypoint. It defaults to `false`. Only tools explicitly marked read-only are exposed to that conversation. The turn's trusted access flag also travels through MCP to the shared command executor, which rejects write/control calls with `read_only_violation` before execution. Tool arguments cannot override this flag. Shell execution, jobs that start commands, scripts, settings changes, app launches, messaging, permission prompts and mixed read/write tools are blocked, even when called directly without discovery. Documentation and permitted phone reads remain available. Read-only reads cannot set `autoRequestPermissions:true`; grant missing access manually. Chat history, summaries and logs still persist. This setting restricts the embedded agent, not separately authenticated owner clients. An API settings patch containing only `readOnly:true` can restrict an active turn immediately. Other access changes require stopping active work first.

Each provider request includes a toolCatalogueRevision fingerprint of the installed contracts and trusted launcher access context: `conversationReadOnly` is the saved setting, `turnReadOnly` is the effective restriction, `reason` distinguishes a saved restriction from a screen explanation, and `writeAccessResumesNextTurn` identifies a temporary restriction on an otherwise writable conversation. The executor applies that turn's restriction independently. Screen explanation never rewrites saved access. This current context takes precedence over access claims in older conversation messages.

The model gets five compact tools: search documentation and collections, discover phone tool schemas, call a discovered tool, list documentation resources and read one resource. Calls run through the same local MCP handlers used by external clients, including input checks, Android permission handling and outcome reporting. API keys are never added to model context. Requested phone data, screen captures and tool results are sent to the selected provider as conversation context.

The assistant is instructed to rediscover relevant installed contracts for each new owner request and follow every `inputSchema` requirement, type, enum and nested field. On a rejected `phone_call`, its result includes the current `toolContract` when that native tool is exposed for the current turn. The original error and permission recovery remain intact. Unexposed tools receive discovery guidance instead of an invented schema. This supplies correction data; it never retries a phone action automatically or guarantees that a model will follow the contract.

`phone_tools` only discovers schemas; `phone_call` executes a discovered tool using its exact name and JSON arguments. Use `phone_search` for ranked offline guides and recipes, or collection `tools` for installed schemas. Its optional collection and pagination parameters are strings. `phone_tools` shares the ranked search engine. Read a returned URI directly with `phone_resource`; listing `phone_resources` first is unnecessary. Reuse discovered contracts while the installed build and current access context are unchanged. See [offline search](search.md) for owner collections, aliases, spelling correction and limits. Rejected JSON arguments, unknown tools and invalid or missing resources return structured tool errors, allowing the model to correct its request within the same turn. They do not authorize automatic execution or retries. Provider failures, cancellation, timeouts and round exhaustion still end the turn visibly.

Empty streamed tool arguments become `{}` before they are saved. Nonempty arguments must be strict JSON objects; malformed input is rejected without executing an action. Provider replay retains rejected text in a valid JSON object together with the recorded tool outcome. Existing conversations with empty or malformed saved arguments can continue after an update or restart without deleting history or repeating completed operations.

In writable mode, the agent can call `dikciz_chat` to hide its panel, inspect another app through existing launch/UI/screenshot tools, and request chat again. Screenshot PNG results become image attachments for the provider. Visibility requests report `show_requested` or `hide_requested`; poll status or inspect the UI to confirm the result. Android can block background activity launches without the required access. These requests do not unlock the phone or bypass Android permissions.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Event-driven conversations
text:
## Event-driven conversations

Open a conversation's **Events** editor or use `subscribe`. Rules replace that conversation's complete rule list. Each has an optional unique ID, a canonical automation `subscription`, and task `instructions`. For example:

```json
{
  "action": "subscribe",
  "conversationId": "CONVERSATION_ID",
  "rules": [{
    "id": "owner-check",
    "subscription": {"event": "example.check", "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 60000},
    "instructions": "Read this event and report the relevant phone state."
  }]
}
```

Native and custom events use the existing event names and filters described in [automation control](automation-control.md). Rules persist across panel closure and launcher restart. They can cause paid provider requests while the panel is hidden. The default interval is 60 seconds, minimum one second; each conversation admits at most one queued event turn while work is active. Dikciz excludes its own notification events to avoid reply loops. Clear rules with `rules: []` to disable automation. In writable mode, the model can configure rules through `dikciz_chat` when the owner's task calls for it.
aliases: assistant providers OpenAI Anthropic chat conversation model context read only

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Shared command API
text:
## Shared command API

Use WebSocket `chatControl`, HTTP `/v1/automation` with `type: "chatControl"`, MCP `dikciz_chat`, or the existing Lua/HTML native-command bindings. They share the command implementation and response/error contract. Discover schemas from the installed build before use.

| Action | Fields and result |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Busy/visible/full-screen state, active conversation and total unread count. |
| `profiles` / `profileSave` | List public profiles, or save validated `profile`. Credentials are write-only. |
| `models` | Discover models for `profileId`. |
| `create` | Create with `profileId`, optional `title` and `settings` overrides. |
| `list` | Conversation pages with `limit` and `offset`. |
| `read` | `conversationId`, optional message `limit`/`offset`; returns conversation metadata, display messages and effective `settings`. |
| `rename` | Set `title` for `conversationId`. |
| `settings` | Read effective `settings`, saved `overrides`, `profileId` and protocol for `conversationId`; no credentials. |
| `configure` | Patch `settings` and/or change `profileId` for an idle `conversationId`. A patch containing only `readOnly:true` may restrict an active conversation. Settings accept model and execution fields only. A provider change retains read-only access and clears other prior overrides before applying the patch. |
| `delete` | Delete an idle conversation and its messages/rules. |
| `send` | `conversationId`, `text`, unique `requestKey`. Returns queue identity and state. Reusing the key with the same text returns the existing turn; different text fails with `chat_request_conflict`. |
| `task` | `conversationId`, `requestKey`, and `task` (`widget` or `explainScreen`). Widget creation requires `text`; screen explanation accepts an optional question. See Quick tasks. |
| `stop` | Cancel active and queued work for `conversationId`. Completed effects remain completed. |
| `subscribe` | Replace `rules` for `conversationId`. |
| `show` / `fullscreen` / `hide` | Control the panel independently of running work. `show` accepts optional `conversationId` and `fullScreen`. |

A connection-only profile needs `name`, `protocol`, `baseUrl` and optional `apiKey`. Legacy model/budget defaults remain accepted for existing clients. After `models` discovery, configure the selected conversation through any binding:

```json
{"action":"configure","conversationId":"CONVERSATION_ID","settings":{"model":"MODEL_ID","contextTokens":131072,"maxOutputTokens":8192,"reasoning":"medium"}}
```

Partial settings patches preserve the other overrides. Credentials, host and protocol are rejected inside `settings`; use `profileSave` to edit a connection. Invalid budgets leave persisted settings unchanged.

Queue acceptance is not completion. Poll `read` for complete, failed, cancelled or interrupted messages and inspect tool outcomes. Common errors include `validation_failed`, `chat_profile_missing`, `chat_conversation_missing`, `chat_provider_error`, `chat_busy` and `chat_request_conflict`.

title: On-device Dikciz assistant: Development and tests
text:
## Development and tests

[Koog 1.3.0](https://github.com/JetBrains/koog) supplies provider protocol clients and streaming frames; [Markwon 4.6.2](https://github.com/noties/Markwon) renders native Markdown. Both use Apache-2.0. The Ktor adapter uses its OkHttp engine on Android. A small Dikciz adapter preserves Anthropic signature/redacted blocks and places OpenAI screenshot images in user content after the tool results. Dikciz owns SQLite persistence, context policies, the durable queue, event routing and its MCP adapter. The native UI follows [Chatz](https://github.com/psyb0t/chatz)'s chat behavior.

The private Android Lab suite serves fake OpenAI/Anthropic model discovery and SSE responses through a lab-only reverse mapping to Android loopback, so tests work without emulator Wi-Fi. It exercises the real Android database, shared commands, native panel and MCP tools without a paid API key:

```bash
make dikciz-test DIKCIZ_TEST_SELECTOR=test_chat_agent
```

See the [source architecture](../app/src/dikciz/README.md) and [test guide](../tests/README.md) for the pinned build and lab workflow.

title: Replay automation events
text:
# Replay automation events

`eventJournalStatus`, `eventJournalRead` and `eventJournalConfigure` work through ordinary HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua. The journal records events actually dispatched by the automation bus, including custom events and configured native sources. Reading it does not activate sensors, location or other subscriptions.

title: Replay automation events: Read and resume
text:
## Read and resume

1. Read status and save `journalId`. Use `lastSequence` as the cursor to start with future events, or 0 to request retained history.
2. Read with that `journalId` and `cursor`. Optional `eventTypes` contains 1 through 32 unique exact names. Omit it for every event type.
3. Process `events`, each containing `sequence` and the ordinary `event` document. Persist `nextCursor`, including when no matching events were returned.
4. Continue while `hasMore` is true. Otherwise poll again or set `waitMilliseconds`, 0 through 30000, default 0. `limit` is 1 through 200, default 50.

~~~json
{"type":"eventJournalRead","journalId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","cursor":0,"eventTypes":["example.refresh"],"waitMilliseconds":30000}
~~~

Replace the example epoch with status from the running app. Cursors are exclusive sequence numbers. Duplicate reads replay the same retained events; different clients keep independent cursors. Filters advance over unmatched events. A cursor ahead of the journal is invalid. `event_journal_restarted` means the stored journal epoch changed; inspect status and choose a new starting point rather than silently treating old cursors as current.

title: Replay automation events: Bounds and loss
text:
## Bounds and loss

Defaults are 2048 events, 8388608 encoded JSON bytes and 60 minutes. Configure `maximumEvents` (1 through 16384), `bufferBytes` (65536 through 33554432) and `retentionMinutes` (1 through 1440). Omitted fields retain their current values. Lower limits immediately evict old history. Configuration, retained history and the journal epoch persist in private SQLite storage across process death. Retention still expires old history. Clearing application data creates a new epoch.

Status reports retained count/encoded bytes, eviction count, first/last sequence and limits. The byte budget measures encoded event documents, not total Java heap overhead. A page contains at most 262144 encoded event bytes. Large pages split between whole events and set `hasMore`. No event is split.

`historyGap` and `lostEvents` report sequence numbers no longer retained before the supplied cursor. With a filter, the loss count includes all evicted event types; it cannot prove how many matching events were lost. Individual documents over 65536 encoded bytes become a small `omitted:true` marker with `reason:event_too_large` and `originalBytes`. The page reports `omittedEvents`. Markers do not contain the original payload.

title: Replay automation events: Access and delivery
text:
## Access and delivery

The journal rechecks current Android source access before returning retained payloads. Revoked contacts/calendar/SMS/phone/location/Bluetooth/sensor, notification-listener or Accessibility access fails the read through the shared error path. `autoRequestPermissions:true` uses the existing owner-review flow for supported requirements; grant access and explicitly retry. Retained clipboard content requires Dikciz in the foreground. Health Connect step history checks current provider grants and returns `health_connect_permission_required` when missing; grant step reading through the existing automation settings screen.

These are owner commands with the same authority as other direct native commands. Installing and enabling a script or widget grants its command binding that authority. Lua event-subscription policies still govern automatic delivery; a native owner command is a separate explicit read.

Replay observes dispatched events, after sensor coalescing. It cannot recover sensor samples discarded before dispatch, native callbacks that never arrived or events from a stopped process. It provides at-least-once consumption within retained history. Named consumer acknowledgements persist separately; they never run or retry side effects. See [activity and recovery](operations.md). Keep Lua reads nonblocking while handling an event because Lua and native event dispatch share the event worker.

For sources and policies, see [scripting](scripting-tutorial.md). For custom event setup, see [MCP resources](mcp-resources.md).

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands
text:
# Files, APK installation and shell commands

Dikciz exposes filesystem commands through WebSocket, MCP and plain HTTP. They use Android permissions granted to Dikciz and accept absolute filesystem paths, including shared storage and the app sandbox. They cover paths outside `/sdcard/Dikciz/`. Android still controls access to protected locations.

Use the [connection guide](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb) to configure a reachable listen address and bearer authentication. HTTP commands share the MCP listener and its configured port, normally `19002`. `controlStatus.transports.http` reports the endpoint in use.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Browse and read files
text:
## Browse and read files

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http fileList --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"path":"/sdcard/Download","offset":0,"limit":100}' --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_file_list --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"path":"/sdcard/Download","offset":0,"limit":100}' --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py websocket fileRead --host phone.example --port 19001 --arguments '{"path":"/sdcard/Dikciz/config.json","offset":0,"limit":65536}' --pretty
```

| WebSocket or HTTP command | MCP tool | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fileList` | `dikciz_file_list` | Required `path`; optional `offset` and `limit`. |
| `fileRead` | `dikciz_file_read` | Required `path`; optional byte `offset` and byte `limit`. |
| `fileWrite` | `dikciz_file_write` | Required `path` and `dataBase64`; optional byte `offset` and `overwrite`. |
| `fileMkdir` | `dikciz_file_mkdir` | Required `path`; optional `parents`. |
| `apkInstall` | `dikciz_apk_install` | Required APK `path`; optional complete-file `sha256`. |
| `apkInstallStatus` | `dikciz_apk_install_status` | Required `sessionId` returned by `apkInstall`. |
| `shellStream` | `dikciz_shell_stream` | Required `command`; optional `root`, `timeoutMilliseconds` and `chunkBytes`. Streams live output. |
| `shellStreamStop` | `dikciz_shell_stream_stop` | Required `streamId`. Stops an owned live stream. |
| `shell` | `dikciz_shell` | Required `command`; optional `root`, `timeoutMilliseconds` and `maxOutputBytes`. Use `root: false` for the app shell. |

`fileList` returns `path`, `parent`, `items`, `offset`, `limit` and `hasMore`. Entries include their name, absolute path, kind, byte size, modification time and read/write flags. An unavailable entry carries an error instead of fabricated metadata. The default limit is 100, with a maximum of 500. Continue with the previous offset plus the number of returned items. An empty page has `items: []` and `hasMore: false`.

Directory entries follow filesystem enumeration order. Changes to a directory between requests can change that order. Start a new walk when a consistent listing matters.

`fileRead` returns `dataBase64`, `bytesRead`, `offset`, `nextOffset`, `eof` and file metadata. Continue at `nextOffset` until `eof` is true. The default chunk is 64 KiB, with a 256 KiB maximum. Reading at or beyond EOF returns empty data and `eof: true`. Empty files work too. File tools return the requested bytes; log-viewer redaction does not alter file downloads.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Upload and download binary files
text:
## Upload and download binary files

The supplied client transfers files in bounded HTTP chunks and reports the byte count and SHA-256:

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py upload ./example.apk /sdcard/Download/example.apk --host phone.example --port 19002
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py download /sdcard/Dikciz/config.json ./phone-config.json --host phone.example --port 19002
```

An existing destination is refused by default. Pass `--overwrite` when replacement is intended. The client reads the bearer password from `DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN`, as it does for WebSocket and MCP.

A client using MCP or WebSocket can make the same transfer with `fileWrite` and `fileRead`. Encode each upload chunk as base64 and start at offset zero. For later chunks, send the acknowledged `nextOffset`. Appending requires the offset to match the current file size, which prevents duplicate or out-of-order chunks from silently changing the file. Each upload chunk can contain at most 256 KiB of decoded data.

`fileWrite` at offset zero creates a new file. `overwrite: true` permits replacing an existing file there. An empty `dataBase64` creates an empty file. Parent directories must exist; use `fileMkdir` with `parents: true` to create missing parents. File writes never execute the uploaded content.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Install an uploaded APK
text:
## Install an uploaded APK

Upload one standalone APK, then submit its absolute phone path:

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_apk_install --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"path":"/sdcard/Download/example.apk"}' --pretty
```

The `sha256` argument is optional. Supply the checksum returned by the upload when the installer must verify the exact uploaded bytes. Android verifies the APK and its signing/update rules during installation. The maximum APK size is 512 MiB. APK bundles and split-package sets need their own packaging workflow.

If Android has not granted installation from Dikciz, the result is `permission_required` with `permissionRequest` for `installPackages`. Pass `autoRequestPermissions: true` to queue owner review with a targeted **Allow access** notification, or explicitly request `installPackages` through `requestDeviceAccess`. Without opt-in, no permission UI opens. Grant the access on the phone, return to Dikciz and retry `apkInstall` against the same uploaded path.

Revoking APK-install access can make Android restart Dikciz and invalidate existing MCP sessions. Reconnect after that permission change.

An accepted request returns `preparing` with a `sessionId`. Staging and checksum verification run in the background. Poll that ID through any transport:

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http apkInstallStatus --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"sessionId":123}' --pretty
```

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `preparing` | Dikciz is staging and checking the APK. |
| `submitted` | The completed session was submitted to Android. |
| `pending_user_action` | Android requires confirmation and Dikciz requests its installer screen. |
| `succeeded` | Android reported successful installation. |
| `cancelled` | Android reported an aborted installation, including cancellation. |
| `failed` | Staging or Android installation failed. Read `reason`, `statusCode` or `message` when present. |

Uploading a file, accepting a request and displaying confirmation do not prove installation succeeded. Only the final `succeeded` state reports Android success. A staging checksum mismatch reports `failed` with reason `apk_checksum_mismatch`. Status records are private to the installer and retain up to 64 sessions.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Execute Android CLI commands
text:
## Execute Android CLI commands

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_shell --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"command":"id; ls -la /sdcard/Download","root":false}' --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http shell --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"command":"printf example; exit 7","root":false}' --pretty
```

The command timeout defaults to 30 seconds. Each request can set `timeoutMilliseconds` from 1 to 2147483647 and `maxOutputBytes` from 1 to 1048576. The output default is 65536 bytes, shared by stdout and stderr. These are per-command options; changing one request does not change later commands. The output ceiling keeps even JSON-escaped results within the supplied clients' frame and response budgets.

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_shell --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"command":"sleep 35; printf done","root":false,"timeoutMilliseconds":60000,"maxOutputBytes":262144}' --pretty
```

The same arguments work with WebSocket and HTTP `shell`. MCP tool schemas advertise the defaults and ranges; `controlStatus.limits` reports them too. The supplied client extends its response wait to the requested command timeout plus cleanup and transport time. Other clients must allow that time themselves.

The result includes `executionScope`, `exitCode`, `output` and `outputTruncated`. A nonzero process exit is still a completed command result. `outputTruncated: true` means the combined output exceeded the requested byte budget; Dikciz returns its initial bytes and discards the rest. A command exceeding its timeout returns error code `timeout`. Commands use `/system/bin/sh`; available programs depend on the binaries installed on Android. Root requests require a working, approved `su` and return `root_unavailable` when it is missing or denied. The existing shell behavior requests root when `root` is omitted, so pass `root: false` for normal app-permission commands.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Stream logs and long-running commands
text:
## Stream logs and long-running commands

`shellStream` sends output while the process runs. Use it for continuous logcat, file tails or commands whose progress matters. Its timeout defaults to zero, which means keep running until stopped or disconnected. An optional positive `timeoutMilliseconds` sets a deadline up to 2147483647 milliseconds. Ordinary `shell` keeps its 30-second default.

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py websocket shellStream --host phone.example --port 19001 --arguments '{"command":"logcat -v threadtime","root":false}' --stream-raw
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_shell_stream --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"command":"logcat -v threadtime","root":false}' --stream-raw
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http shellStream --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"command":"logcat -v threadtime","root":false,"timeoutMilliseconds":60000}' --stream-raw
```

Press Ctrl+C to close the stream and stop its owned process group. Android restricts unprivileged logcat to logs the app may read. Full device logs require privileged access. Existing log files can also be read with the file APIs. Streaming adds no Android permissions and does not grant root.

Without `--stream-raw`, the client prints JSON Lines as events arrive. Raw mode writes decoded output bytes directly to stdout. Stdout and stderr share one stream. Chunks contain base64 `outputBase64`, so binary bytes and UTF-8 split across chunks survive unchanged. `chunkBytes` defaults to 4096 and accepts 1 through 65536. There is no cumulative output ceiling. Each listener permits four active streams, and a stalled consumer is disconnected instead of growing an unbounded output buffer.

WebSocket receives a normal `result` acknowledgement containing `streamId`, followed by `shellStreamEvent` messages with the original `requestId`. Their `result` contains `streamId`, increasing `sequence`, and `event`: `output`, `heartbeat` or `complete`. Completion includes `state`, nullable `exitCode` and total `outputBytes`. States include `exited`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `slow_consumer` and `failed`; a startup failure can carry an error `code`. A nonzero exit code still means the process exited normally.

Send `shellStreamStop` with the stream's ID to stop it explicitly. WebSocket cancellation belongs to the connection that opened the stream. MCP cancellation belongs to the same MCP session. HTTP cancellation uses the same Authorization header and the unguessable stream ID. A separate MCP client session cannot cancel another session's stream. Closing the originating response, losing authorization, or stopping the listener also stops the stream and its process group. Completed streams are removed, so a later stop returns `shell_stream_not_found`.

MCP returns `Content-Type: text/event-stream` for `dikciz_shell_stream`. Output arrives as standard `notifications/message` records with logger `dikciz.shell` and the event object in `params.data`; one final JSON-RPC tool result completes the call. The current MCP protocol requires per-request log opt-in. Set `params._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]` to `info` or `debug`, alongside the existing protocol version and client capabilities. The supplied client sets this automatically. Requests without that opt-in are rejected rather than opening a stream whose output the client cannot receive. SSE comments keep silent processes connected.

Plain HTTP `shellStream` also returns SSE. Each `data:` record contains the usual command envelope, first the acknowledgement and then the correlated stream events. `shellStreamStop` returns ordinary JSON. This is push delivery; clients do not poll for output. Reconnecting creates a new process, and streams do not replay old output.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Plain HTTP protocol
text:
## Plain HTTP protocol

POST a JSON command to `http://phone.example:19002/v1/automation` with `Content-Type: application/json` and the configured bearer header. The body and response use the WebSocket command envelope:

```json
{"requestId":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","type":"fileList","path":"/sdcard/Download","offset":0,"limit":100}
```

Each request needs a UUID `requestId`. Responses preserve it and return either `type: "result"` with a result object or `type: "error"` with a finite code and message. The HTTP endpoint needs no MCP initialization or session. It dispatches the same validated command target, including shell commands and normal launcher actions.

Most commands return JSON; `shellStream` returns SSE. It uses the same bearer and browser-Origin rules as the other controls. Browser origins outside device loopback are refused; native clients can omit `Origin`. The endpoint has no built-in TLS, so use the private-network setup described in the connection guide.

Common file errors are `file_access_denied`, `file_not_found`, `not_a_file`, `not_a_directory`, `file_exists`, `file_offset_mismatch`, `invalid_base64`, `file_chunk_too_large`, `file_io_failed` and `validation_failed`. A failed command does not claim a completed write or installation. File contents, APK bytes, bearer credentials and shell output are excluded from operation logs.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: File management
text:
## File management

`fileManage` (`dikciz_file_manage`) accepts action and absolute path. `stat` returns metadata. `copy` copies one regular file to destination; `move` renames a file or directory to destination. Neither overwrites existing destinations. Moves across filesystems can fail explicitly.

`delete` removes one file or empty directory. Set recursive=true for a nonempty directory. It preflights the tree, refuses symbolic links and checks maximumEntries (default 10000, range 1..100000) before deleting. An external process can still change files during execution; recursive deletion is not a filesystem transaction.

`search` requires query, a literal case-insensitive name substring. It does not follow symbolic links. Use offset/limit to page matches, maximum 200 per page. maximumEntries bounds scanned entries; increase it or narrow the directory after file_tree_limit. Directory changes can affect enumeration between calls. The empty query matches every name.

Credential record remote-auth.json and its atomic backup/staging aliases are denied through file commands, including canonical path aliases. Move/delete refuse any ancestor containing those credentials. Android still enforces filesystem access. This file-command restriction does not make an authorized privileged shell a sandbox.

title: Files, APK installation and shell commands: Incremental shell sessions
text:
## Incremental shell sessions

Use shellSessionStart/Read/Stop/Forget and shellSessionsList when output must be readable through any ordinary binding, including HTML and Lua, or after transport reconnects. Follow cursors, inspect explicit history gaps and wait for a terminal state. See [shell sessions](shell-sessions.md) for parameters and lifecycle. Existing WebSocket/MCP push streams remain connection-owned.

title: Hardware controls and discovery
text:
# Hardware controls and discovery

These commands use the same registry, schemas, native executor and Android permission recovery across HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua. Inventory reads do not enable radios, pair devices, record audio or request transfers. All fields are strict; unknown fields and invalid values fail before device work.

title: Hardware controls and discovery: Torch
text:
## Torch

`torchControl` / `dikciz_torch_control` requires `action`: `status`, `on` or `off`. Status returns flash-capable `cameraIds` and one `items` entry per selected camera. It registers CameraManager callbacks for up to `timeoutMilliseconds` (1 through 5000, default 1000), then unregisters. Entries report `enabled`, `disabled`, `unavailable` or `unknown`, with `observed`, nullable `enabled` and a callback delivery timestamp in elapsed milliseconds. Unknown means no callback arrived within the window. `complete` means every selected camera was observed. Optional `cameraId` selects one camera; no flash hardware returns an empty complete result. Timeout applies only to status. On accepts optional `durationMilliseconds` from 1 through 5000 for a native automatic off request independent of WebView timers. A later on/off request replaces the pending timer for that camera. The response includes nullable `autoOffAfterMilliseconds`; automatic-off failures are logged. Duration is rejected for status/off. On/off accept optional `cameraId`, defaulting to the first flash camera. Use IDs from this result or `cameraList`. Android camera permission is required for changes. The response is `state: submitted`, `cameraId` and requested `enabled`; it confirms Android accepted the call, not that the light was physically observed. Another camera user or Android policy can make the torch unavailable.

title: Hardware controls and discovery: Vibration
text:
## Vibration

`vibrationControl` / `dikciz_vibration_control` requires `action`: `status`, `vibrate`, `waveform`, `effect` or `cancel`. Status returns `available`, `amplitudeControl` and named predefined `effects` with native support `supported`, `unsupported` or `unknown`. Support queries require Android 11; older devices report unknown. Vibrate accepts `durationMilliseconds` from 1 through 10000, default 250, and `amplitude` of -1 for Android's default or 1 through 255. Zero is invalid. Submission returns `state: submitted` and duration. Android sound/haptic settings can suppress the physical effect. Cancel stops Dikciz vibration and returns `state: cancelled`. Devices without a vibrator report unavailable and reject vibration.

Waveform requires `timingsMilliseconds`, 1 through 64 integer segments. Each is 0 through 10000 ms and their total must be 1 through 10000 ms. Without amplitudes, segments alternate off/on starting with off. Optional `amplitudes` must match the timing array; each is -1 for Android default, 0 off or 1 through 255. Segments with zero duration do not add time. Waveforms never repeat; cancel stops a submitted pattern.

Effect requires `effect`: `click`, `doubleClick`, `heavyClick` or `tick`, on Android 10 or newer. Android may use its predefined fallback when the exact hardware effect is unsupported. Submission returns the name and `fallbackPossible: true`; it does not claim native playback or measured output. Fields belonging to another action are rejected.

title: Hardware controls and discovery: System settings
text:
## System settings

`systemSetting` / `dikciz_system_setting` requires `action: get` or `set` and `setting`. Set also requires integer `value`; get rejects a value. Only the following settings are accepted:

| Setting | Allowed values |
| --- | --- |
| `brightness` | 0 through 255. Automatic brightness may override the effect. |
| `automaticBrightness` | 0 manual, 1 automatic. |
| `automaticRotation` | 0 fixed, 1 automatic. |
| `rotation` | 0 through 3 quarter-turns. Automatic rotation may override it. |
| `screenTimeoutMilliseconds` | 1 through 2147483647. Android policy may constrain the effective timeout. |

Reads return `setting`, stored `value` or null, and `writeAccess`. Writes require owner-granted Modify system settings, then return the actual stored read-back. Missing access uses `native_permission_systemSettings` and the standard owner-review flow. `settings_write_rejected` means the platform rejected the write. This is not an arbitrary Settings provider interface and does not grant protected settings privileges.

title: Hardware controls and discovery: Inventories
text:
## Inventories

| Command | MCP tool | Results and requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bluetoothDevices` | `dikciz_bluetooth_devices` | Paired devices: address, name, type and bond state; adapter available/enabled. Requires Bluetooth access on Android 12+. No discovery scan or connection. |
| `usbDevices` | `dikciz_usb_devices` | Attached host devices: ID, name, vendor/product, class, interfaces and whether USB permission is already granted. See [USB access and transfers](usb-control.md). |
| `wifiScanResults` | `dikciz_wifi_scan_results` | Cached SSID/BSSID, frequency MHz, signal dBm, security capabilities and Android timestamp. Requires fine location. Does not trigger a new scan. Android may restrict or empty the cache. |
| `audioDevices` | `dikciz_audio_devices` | Device ID/type/name, input/output direction, sample rates and channel counts. No routing or playback. |
| `nfcStatus` | `dikciz_nfc_status` | Adapter availability and enabled state. No tag transaction. |
| `cameraCapabilities` | `dikciz_camera_capabilities` | Required `cameraId`. JPEG sizes, maximum digital zoom, exposure compensation bounds/EV step, sensor orientation and autofocus modes. See [camera controls](camera-control.md). |

Bluetooth, USB, Wi-Fi and audio inventories accept `limit` (1 through 200, default 50) and `offset` (0 through 1000000, default 0). Follow `hasMore` using offset plus returned item count. Their result includes `total`; device changes can change membership between requests. Bluetooth without an adapter returns `available: false` and an empty list. Camera IDs are strings; audio and USB device IDs are integers.

Hardware controls and discovery: Live camera and display frames

Use imageStreamStart/Read/Stop for bounded JPEG preview and Accessibility display capture with owner Stop and cursor replay. See [the guide](visual-streams.md).

title: Health Connect records
text:
# Health Connect records

`healthRecordsCatalogue` reports provider availability, exact record kinds, timestamp/value shapes, aggregate metric names and current read/write grants. The installed catalogue is authoritative. Availability is separate from permission.

Supported kinds are steps, distance, activeCalories, totalCalories, heartRate, sleep, exercise, weight, height, hydration, bodyFat, bodyTemperature, bloodPressure, bloodGlucose, oxygenSaturation and floors. Units appear in field names. Interval records use startTimeMilliseconds/endTimeMilliseconds; instantaneous records use timeMilliseconds. Times are UTC Unix milliseconds.

Request only needed kinds with `healthPermissionsRequest`, `kinds` array and `access` read/write/readWrite. Optional includeBackground/includeHistory request Android's separate grants where supported. The phone owner must approve. A missing grant returns targeted recovery and requires explicit retry, never an automatic write replay.

`healthRecordsRead` requires kind and a time range, supports limit and opaque pageToken. Follow nextPageToken/hasMore. Ranges are at most 366 days; platform history restrictions still apply. `healthRecordsAggregate` uses the provider's metrics and origin handling rather than summing possibly duplicated raw records.

`healthRecordsWrite` accepts one to fifty records with stable clientRecordId, optional nonnegative clientRecordVersion, timestamps and values. Record validation and SDK bounds apply. Writes use manual-entry metadata. `healthRecordsDelete` requires exact recordIds and confirm true; Health Connect enforces data-origin ownership. It does not delete arbitrary records from other apps.

Open the native Health tab to inspect supported grants, request chosen access and read today's records. A provider, owner grants and actual stored records are required for meaningful results. These operations are not medical interpretation.

title: Images, barcodes and documents
text:
# Images, barcodes and documents

`imageRecognize` reads an accessible local file with bundled ML Kit Latin text and barcode models. Set `mode` to text, barcodes or both. The image is not uploaded. Decoded links and text are returned as untrusted data and never opened or executed.

Inputs are limited to 32 MiB and 64 million source pixels. Decode resolution is bounded. `maxDimension` defaults to 2048 (320..4096). `rotationDegrees` is 0, 90, 180 or 270; correct image orientation explicitly. Returned bounds refer to the processed, rotated image. `maximumResults` defaults to 200, `maximumTextCharacters` to 65536 and `timeoutMilliseconds` to 30000. At most two recognition jobs run at once. Result limits are explicit; an oversized text or response fails rather than silently dropping content.

`documentScan` accepts `pages: [{path: "..."}]`, one to twenty images. Optional page `corners` contains exactly four normalized x/y points in top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left order. It applies perspective correction when supplied and grayscale by default. It returns owned JPEG page paths and a raster PDF path in app capture storage. Documents share the two-job image-work limit and accept at most 16777216 processed pixels in total. Reduce maxDimension or split a larger batch. It does not automatically find edges or create a searchable text layer. Recognize returned pages separately for OCR. Use ordinary file operations to transfer or delete results.

Open **Settings**, **Safety, journeys and devices**, **Scan** to pick images, recognize them or save a PDF. Camera capture remains a separate operation with Android camera access. Model processing itself does not require a provider key or an external AI endpoint.

The APK bundles Google ML Kit dependencies. Their SDK/model terms apply in addition to the launcher's license. See [dependencies](dependency-licenses.md).

title: Documentation: Outcome rules
text:
## Outcome rules

A transport reply proves only what its result states. Accepted intents are not verified app launches; submitted SMS is not carrier delivery; an install session is not a completed installation; submitted torch/vibration is not measured physical output. Read the terminal status or observed effect documented for that operation.

Android permissions, special access, roles, hardware, foreground state and system privilege are independent checks. A manifest declaration is not an implementation or grant. Missing capability is explicit. Root shell is optional privileged access, not a portable replacement for ordinary Android APIs.

[Activity, resources and visual rules](operations.md) covers command history, resource measurements, interruption and simulated rule testing.

[Background JavaScript](background-javascript.md) covers the second script backend, headless events, state, limits and archives.

title: Geocoding and GNSS status
text:
# Geocoding and GNSS status

locationGet reads a permitted cached or fresh position. geocode resolves supplied text/coordinates through Android's geocoding provider. gnssStatus observes satellite status. These are separate operations; a resolved address or visible satellite is not proof of the phone's current position.

title: Geocoding and GNSS status: Geocoding
text:
## Geocoding

geocode, MCP dikciz_geocode, requires action=forward or action=reverse. Forward requires a nonblank query of at most 1024 characters and refuses coordinates. Reverse requires finite latitude within -90..90 and longitude within -180..180 and refuses query.

Optional language is a BCP-47 tag, at most 64 characters. limit is 1..10, default 5, selecting the maximum provider matches, not an exhaustive paginated address database. timeoutMilliseconds is 1..120000, default 30000. The bounded callback API requires Android 13 or newer.

Results contain items, limit, hasMore=false, source=android_geocoder and language. Address fields include nullable coordinates, address line, locality, administrative area, country code/name and postal code, each text field at most 1024 characters. Empty matches are valid. Android's provider can use a network service and receives the supplied query or coordinates.

Missing provider, timeout and provider failure return geocoder_unavailable, geocoder_timeout and geocoder_failed. Older Android returns unsupported_android_version. No synthetic address replaces a missing response. Provider accuracy and coverage vary.

title: Geocoding and GNSS status: GNSS observation
text:
## GNSS observation

gnssStatus, MCP dikciz_gnss_status, needs precise location access. It listens for a satellite-status callback for timeoutMilliseconds (1..5000, default 1000), then unregisters. It does not turn on GPS or start a tracking job. Location may need to be active elsewhere before Android supplies GNSS status.

A received status returns available=true, observedAtMilliseconds, total and an offset/limit page. Fields include satellite ID, constellation, signal C/N0 in dB-Hz, elevation/azimuth degrees, usedInFix, ephemeris/almanac flags and optional carrier frequency in Hz. This is status observation, not raw navigation-message capture or a location fix.

No GPS provider, rejected registration or no callback returns available=false with no_gps_provider, registration_rejected or no_status_during_window. Missing permission uses the common locationForeground owner-review procedure. Do not report a fix from unavailable status.

All ordinary entrypoints and local script/widget bindings share these commands. For background location subscriptions and precision policies, read the [scripting tutorial](scripting-tutorial.md) and [native device guide](native-device-control.md).
