title: MCP protocol compatibility
text:
# MCP protocol compatibility

The phone serves Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. Authentication and browser-Origin checks apply before either protocol mode. POST uses JSON content and accepts both application/json and text/event-stream. GET returns 405 because Dikciz does not provide a general server event stream there; WebSocket carries persistent launcher events. Shell streaming is a per-tool SSE response.

title: MCP protocol compatibility: Modern requests
text:
## Modern requests

Protocol 2026-07-28 uses stateless requests. No initialize handshake or session ID is required. Every request carries:

- `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` and `Mcp-Method` matching its method.
- `Mcp-Name` matching the tool name for tools/call or the URI for resources/read.
- params._meta containing io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and an object io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities. Client identity is optional.

Start with server/discover or directly call tools/list. Discovery returns supportedVersions, capabilities, instructions and server identity in result._meta. Discovery/list/resource results include resultType, ttlMs and cacheScope. These results are private to the authorized connection context; current caching TTL is zero.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"server/discover","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28","io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities":{}}}}
```

The HTTP headers must mirror that body. Missing/mismatched required headers return HTTP 400 and JSON-RPC -32020. Unsupported stateless versions return HTTP 400 and -32022, with requested/supported versions in error.data. Unknown modern methods return HTTP 404 and -32601. Mcp-Name supports the standard `=?base64?<UTF-8 bytes encoded as Base64>?=` sentinel when plain ASCII is insufficient; decoded values must match the body.

title: MCP protocol compatibility: Legacy clients
text:
## Legacy clients

Initialize supports 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26. Keep the returned Mcp-Session-Id and send notifications/initialized. Subsequent requests carry that session and negotiated MCP-Protocol-Version. Modern params._meta is optional for these legacy sessions. Unknown offered initialization versions receive the latest supported legacy version; clients must check the negotiated response.

Legacy sessions expire after ten idle minutes, with at most eight sessions. DELETE with the session ID closes one session and its owned streams. Reinitialize after a process restart or session expiry. Legacy ping returns an ordinary result.

Earlier Dikciz custom clients used an initialized session with version 2026-07-28. That compatibility path remains accepted, including its request metadata. New clients should use the standard stateless modern flow or a negotiated legacy version. The supplied Python client manages its connection automatically.

title: MCP protocol compatibility: Results and operation access
text:
## Results and operation access

Tool results preserve ordinary command data in structuredContent and add text/image content for MCP clients. isError identifies a tool failure; its structured code and permissionRequest match the shared dispatcher. Successful protocol delivery does not prove the requested external effect. Poll the documented operation status or read the observed state.

Read [resources](mcp-resources.md), [agent setup](agent-integrations.md), [commands](command-reference.md) and [connection setup](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb). Public standards: [modern version negotiation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning), [Streamable HTTP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http) and [legacy lifecycle](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle).

title: MCP documentation resources
text:
# MCP documentation resources

Dikciz packages short operating guides and recipes in the APK. MCP clients can discover and read them without downloading the repository or placing its full documentation in a model's context. Search the task with `dikciz_search_query` in collection `docs`, then read the relevant returned URI. `dikciz://docs/index` remains the browsing entry point. The [offline search guide](search.md) covers ranking, tool contracts and custom collections. The [packaged index](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/index.md) is the content source.

title: MCP documentation resources: Discover and read
text:
## Discover and read

Initialization advertises `capabilities.resources: {}` and instructions pointing to the index. `resources/list` returns at most eight descriptors, each with `uri`, `name`, `title`, `description`, `mimeType` and UTF-8 byte `size`. Follow the opaque `nextCursor` until it is absent. Do not synthesize or alter cursors.

Call `resources/read` with one exact URI. It returns one `text/markdown` content record. Every guide in the browsable catalog is at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Search also returns manual sections under `dikciz://docs/library/`, each bounded to 12000 characters. A read does not bundle linked sections automatically. The 69 browsable resources include connection, permissions, UI, apps, pages, HTML, Lua, headless JavaScript, custom apps, events, files, shell, logs, security, native Android data, sensors, location, camera, microphone, speech and focused recipes. Separate resources cover feature access and typed actions for state/events, device operations and Accessibility. The contact/SMS recipe covers direct lookup, SIM selection, duplicate protection and receipts. The custom-event example splits setup, Lua source and HTML source into separate resources.

```json
{"method":"resources/read","params":{"uri":"dikciz://docs/recipes/event-setup"}}
```

This shows the method and parameters only. A real request needs the JSON-RPC envelope and its protocol mode: modern request metadata/routing headers, or a negotiated legacy session. Existing clients handle those details. `resources/templates/list` returns an empty template list. These packaged resources do not advertise subscriptions or list-change notifications.

SIM reads have a dedicated [numbers and permissions guide](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/sim.md). The assistant has a [tool-contract and access guide](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/chat-tools.md). Chat also has separate resources for [operation](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/chat.md), [context budgets](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/chat-context.md) and [event rules](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/chat-events.md).

The [Travel todo recipe](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/recipes/travel-todo.md), at `dikciz://docs/recipes/travel-todo`, explains the shipped app, geofence setup, custom-event input, state and cleanup. The [full illustrated tutorial](todo-app-tutorial.md) links every source file.

title: MCP documentation resources: Use the supplied client
text:
## Use the supplied client

Run from a checkout so companion modules are available. Replace `phone.example` and the port with the phone's actual endpoint. The client reads bearer credentials from `DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN`.

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp-resources --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp-read dikciz://docs/index --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp-read dikciz://docs/recipes/event-setup --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
```

Pass the returned `nextCursor` to `mcp-resources --cursor '<returned-cursor>'` for another page. Each CLI operation manages its own connection. The supplied client uses modern stateless requests; legacy clients initialize and close negotiated sessions.

title: MCP documentation resources: Version and access
text:
## Version and access

Content describes the serving APK. Use `deviceInfo` to identify that package and version, `tools/list` for executable schemas, and `controlStatus` for live limits. Recipes require verifying persisted or visible effects after a request. The event recipe proves Lua state and a rendered HTML acknowledgement separately.

Resource requests use the existing bearer, browser-Origin and protocol-mode checks. Reads accept only exact packaged guide or indexed manual-section `dikciz://docs/` URIs. They never read device paths, follow external URLs or expose credentials. Invalid parameters and unknown URIs return JSON-RPC `-32602`; unknown-resource errors include the URI in `error.data.uri`. Packaged-content load failures return `-32603`.

These are MCP resource methods. Search and full-text reads also have shared HTTP, WebSocket, HTML and Lua commands described in [offline search](search.md). Other command APIs retain the shared contract described in [automation control](automation-control.md). See [connection setup](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb) and the [source map](../app/src/dikciz/README.md) for transport and implementation details.

Speech recognition and hardware controls have separate focused guides. Read `dikciz://docs/guides/speech` for recognition modes and cancellation, or `dikciz://docs/guides/hardware-controls` for torch, vibration, settings and device inventories.

The [public SDK resource](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/android-sdk.md) covers exact signatures, typed values, callbacks, runtime restrictions and both read-only enforcement layers.

title: MCP documentation resources: Operations and recovery guides
text:
## Operations and recovery guides

Short resources dikciz://docs/guides/operations, dikciz://docs/guides/backups and dikciz://docs/guides/visual-streams cover activity, visual rules, encrypted restore, image/speech replay and recorded-file transcription. See [the guide](operations.md).

The [companion index](../app/src/dikciz/assets/mcp/guides/companion.md) links eight focused sections for safety/journeys, device connections, image recognition, health, Wi-Fi, routines and APK sets.

title: Microphone PCM streams
text:
# Microphone PCM streams

Use microphoneStreamStart, microphoneStreamRead, microphoneStreamStop, microphoneStreamsList and microphoneStreamForget through HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML or Lua. MCP names use dikciz_microphone_stream_start/read/stop/forget and dikciz_microphone_streams_list. Discover the exact schemas first.

Starting requires Android microphone permission and an eligible foreground Dikciz process. Recording then runs under a dedicated microphone foreground service and can continue while another app is open. Android privacy controls, permission revocation or service loss can stop it. The notification has a Stop recording action. When notifications are blocked, Android may show foreground work only in its active-apps UI; inspect notificationPostingEnabled. This records the microphone, not cellular call audio.

Defaults: sampleRateHz=16000, channels=1, chunkMilliseconds=100, maximumDurationMilliseconds=30000, startupTimeoutMilliseconds=30000, bufferBytes=2097152, maximumEvents=1024 and retentionMinutes=60. Optional inputDeviceId prefers an audioDevices input; routedInputDeviceId reports the actual route after samples arrive. Hardware can reject formats advertised by the input schema.

Start returns streamId and metadata. Read with streamId, cursor=0, limit=200 and optional waitMilliseconds up to 30000. Each audio event contains sequence, audioBase64, firstFrame, frames and observedAtElapsedNanoseconds. Decode signed 16-bit little-endian interleaved PCM using the returned sampleRateHz and channels. The byte count is frames * channels * 2. audioTimestampNanoseconds/audioFramePosition may be null; their timebase is monotonic. Start and exit events share the sequence.

Save nextCursor, drain hasMore, and inspect historyGap/lostEvents before treating audio as continuous. Replay stores whole events. A page holds at most 393216 encoded JSON bytes. Event/count/byte limits evict old history explicitly. Read metadata is sampled before its optional wait; poll again for updated lifecycle state. Long polling inside a Lua event handler delays that handler, so use waitMilliseconds=0 there.

Stop requests cancellation. Poll reads or list until state is stopped, expired or failed and hardwareReleaseConfirmed=true. Read the exit event and any remaining pages. A stop acknowledgement alone does not prove release. Forget then removes retained audio. Cleanup failure keeps hardware ownership reserved and prevents forgetting until the app process is restarted.

Only one microphone owner runs across streaming, ordinary recording, managed recording, speech recognition and video with audio. At most eight stream records and 32 MiB of reserved replay buffers are retained per process. Each buffer accepts 65536 through 8388608 bytes; event count is 1 through 4096; retention is 1 through 1440 minutes. Startup accepts 1 through 120000 ms; duration accepts 100 through 2147483647 ms. Every encoded chunk must fit both its buffer and a complete response page.

History is process-owned memory and survives client disconnects and activity recreation within that process. App process death, force-stop, reboot and APK replacement lose it. The `restart` command recreates the launcher activity without killing the process; it is not a way to clear retained audio or a failed hardware lease. Stop, observe hardware release and forget explicitly. Terminal records expire on subsequent operations. List uses offset/limit pagination. Audio payloads are not written to application logs. Explicitly saving returned data or wrapping reads in durable jobs can persist it. A failed start can leave a retained record; inspect list and observe cleanup before forgetting it.

title: Direct Android data and control
text:
# Direct Android data and control

Use native commands instead of opening Contacts, Messages or Settings and tapping their UI. WebSocket, HTTP, MCP, HTML and enabled Lua use the same validator, executor, permission recovery and result. These operations call Android APIs without root or a shell.

Start with `nativeDataStatus` or MCP `dikciz_native_data_status`. Its `resources` list reports each resource's columns, writable columns, required create fields, foreign keys, search fields and current grants. Discover executable schemas through `controlStatus` and MCP `tools/list`.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Read provider data
text:
## Read provider data

`contentQuery` and MCP `dikciz_content_query` accept:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | Required name from native data discovery. Arbitrary URIs and authorities are rejected. |
| `columns` | Optional array of unique allowlisted columns, at most 32. Defaults to the first 12 declared columns. |
| `filter` | Exact equality filters combined with AND. Null matches SQL NULL. |
| `query` | Literal substring search over the resource's declared search fields. SQL wildcards are escaped. |
| `limit`, `offset` | Integer page size and row offset. Defaults 50 and 0. Ranges 1 through 200 and 0 through 1000000. |

Results are `{resource, items, limit, offset, hasMore}`, ordered by `_id` ascending except for the chronological `calendarInstances` resource described below. Continue at `offset + items.length` while `hasMore` is true. Concurrent edits can change page membership. A page is limited to 512 KiB and text fields to 4096 characters. Shortened fields appear in each row's `truncatedFields` array. Empty results return an empty array. Binary provider columns are excluded.

Resources cover `contacts`, `phones`, `emails`, `rawContacts`, `contactData`, `calendars`, `calendarEvents`, `calendarInstances`, `calendarReminders`, `sms`, `callLog`, `images`, `audio` and `videos`. Provider column names remain native. For phone rows, `display_name` is the contact name and `data1` is the number.

~~~json
{"type":"contentQuery","resource":"phones","filter":{"display_name":"Example Contact"},"columns":["contact_id","raw_contact_id","display_name","data1"]}
~~~

Use `query` for partial name or number search. Resolve multiple matches before choosing a recipient.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Write records atomically
text:
## Write records atomically

`contentWrite` and MCP `dikciz_content_write` accept `resource`, `operation`, optional `id` and `values`. Operations are `create`, `update` and `delete`. Create omits `id`; update and delete require one positive row ID. Updates preserve unspecified columns. Delete accepts no values. No delete-all or raw selection argument exists.

Writable resources are raw contacts, contact data, calendar events and reminders. Other resources are read-only. Dikciz never requests the default SMS role to edit message history.

`contentBatch` and MCP `dikciz_content_batch` accept up to 32 write records in `operations`. Every operation must use the same provider. A failed operation rolls back the entire batch. Batch records may add `backReferences`, mapping an allowlisted foreign-key column to an earlier create-operation index.

Create a local contact, name and phone number:

~~~json
{"type":"contentBatch","operations":[
  {"resource":"rawContacts","operation":"create","values":{"account_name":null,"account_type":null}},
  {"resource":"contactData","operation":"create","values":{"mimetype":"vnd.android.cursor.item/name","data1":"Example Contact"},"backReferences":{"raw_contact_id":0}},
  {"resource":"contactData","operation":"create","values":{"mimetype":"vnd.android.cursor.item/phone_v2","data1":"4085550100","data2":"2"},"backReferences":{"raw_contact_id":0}}
]}
~~~

Results contain one `results` entry per operation, with a created `id` or changed-row `count`. Save IDs before updates or deletes. To remove this contact, delete its raw-contact ID; Android removes dependent data. Synced-account rules still apply.

Calendar values use native fields including `calendar_id`, `title`, `dtstart`, `dtend`, `eventTimezone`, `allDay`, `description`, `eventLocation`, `rrule` and `duration`. Read `calendars` first and choose a writable one. Timestamps use Unix milliseconds. Use `UTC` or an IANA zone in `eventTimezone`. Android validates recurrence and calendar-specific requirements.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Send SMS and inspect receipts
text:
## Send SMS and inspect receipts

`smsSend` and MCP `dikciz_sms_send` require `idempotencyKey`, `recipient` and `body`; `subscriptionId` is optional. Numbers use digits and an optional leading plus. Common spaces, parentheses, dots and hyphens from contact formatting are normalized before sending and duplicate checks. Bodies are limited to 4096 characters and 32 segments. Read `simList` to select a SIM. Missing defaults return `no_default_sms_subscription`.

~~~json
{"type":"smsSend","idempotencyKey":"example-message-1","recipient":"4085550100","body":"Example message"}
~~~

Use the same key for retries. Dikciz reserves it durably before the modem call. Identical retries return the same receipt with `duplicate: true`. Different content or an explicitly different SIM returns `sms_idempotency_conflict`. A changed system default never turns an identical retry into another send.

Poll `smsStatus` or MCP `dikciz_sms_status` with that key. Receipts return message ID, selected subscription, segment counts, per-part callback codes and state, without recipient or body:

| State | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `submission_unknown` | The durable reservation exists; completion of the modem call is unknown. |
| `accepted` | Android accepted submission. Sent callbacks are pending. |
| `sent` | Every part received a successful Android sent callback. Delivery is unconfirmed. |
| `delivered` | Successful carrier delivery reports confirm every part. |
| `failed` | Submission threw or a sent callback reported failure. |
| `delivery_failed` | A delivery report explicitly reported failure. |

Delivery reports depend on the carrier and can remain absent. `deliveryConfirmed` is true only for `delivered`. Never resend an uncertain submission under a new key without checking what happened. Receipts survive recreation and process restart. The private store retains up to 512 keys until app data is cleared and refuses new sends when full rather than discarding duplicate protection. SMS can cost money.

Read permitted SMS history through `contentQuery` resource `sms`. Android can save messages sent by non-default SMS apps into its SMS provider. The legacy typed `sendSms` action confirms submission only; use tracked `smsSend` when receipts and duplicate protection are needed.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Direct system commands
text:
## Direct system commands

| Command | MCP tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `simList` | `dikciz_sim_list` | Active subscription IDs, slots, display/carrier names, own phone numbers with availability status, and default SMS SIM. Private SIM identifiers are not returned. |
| `callControl` | `dikciz_call_control` | `action` is `state`, `place`, `answer` or `end`. Place requires `recipient` and reports acceptance, not connection. Android may restrict call control by role. |
| `clipboardGet` | `dikciz_clipboard_get` | Plain text and availability. Android can restrict background reads. |
| `clipboardSet` | `dikciz_clipboard_set` | Required plain `text`, including an empty string. |
| `locationGet` | `dikciz_location_get` | Recent permitted position, accuracy, age, source and optional place name. `maxAgeMilliseconds` defaults to 300000. If needed, waits for a new fix for `timeoutMilliseconds` (default 10000, range 0 through 120000). Zero reads cache only. Disabled location, no cached fix and timeout return `available: false` with a reason. |
| `notificationsList` | `dikciz_notifications_list` | Current notification text and short-lived action tokens through the connected listener. |
| `mediaSessionsList` | `dikciz_media_sessions_list` | Active packages, playback state, position and bounded track metadata. |
| `deviceState` | `dikciz_device_state` | Screen/keyguard, battery/charging, power save, volume, ringer and connectivity state. |

`simList` adds `phoneNumber` (string or null) and `phoneNumberStatus` for each subscription. Status is `available`, `unavailable` when Android supplies no number or its telephony service is temporarily unavailable, `permission_required`, `access_denied` for an Android restriction, or `unsupported`. `phoneNumberPermissionGranted` reports the runtime grant independently of whether Android supplies a number. It uses `SubscriptionManager.getPhoneNumber(subscriptionId)` on Android 13+ and the subscription number on older Android. Carrier data is not guaranteed present, correctly formatted or verified; an empty result is never replaced with an invented value.

Listing SIM metadata requires `READ_PHONE_STATE`; numbers additionally require `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS`. Missing number access preserves SIM metadata and adds the shared `permissionRequest` for `phoneNumbers`. `autoRequestPermissions:true` opts into owner review for those read permissions, without requesting call placement or answering access. Explicit recovery is `requestDeviceAccess` with `requirementId:"phoneNumbers"`. Retry after the actual grant. These results and recovery apply to MCP, HTTP, WebSocket, HTML and Lua through the shared executor.

SIM, notification and media lists accept page fields. Existing typed actions control notifications, media, volume, intents and locking. Existing subscriptions provide sensors, live location, Health Connect, Bluetooth and other events programmatically.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Sensors, camera, microphone and speech
text:
## Sensors, camera, microphone and speech

All commands below share the same schemas, execution and permission recovery in WebSocket, HTTP, MCP, HTML `dikciz.command` and Lua `context.request` or `context.requestJson`.

| Command | MCP tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sensorReadings` | `dikciz_sensor_readings` | Sample all sensors or one `sensorId` from the current device inventory. Accepts `limit` and `offset`; follow `hasMore`. `timeoutMilliseconds` defaults to 1000 and accepts 1 through 5000. |
| `cameraList` | `dikciz_camera_list` | Camera IDs, front/back/external facing and flash availability. Does not start capture. |
| `cameraCapture` | `dikciz_camera_capture` | Save an actual JPEG. Optional `cameraId` defaults to the first camera. `maxDimension` defaults to 1280 and accepts 320 through 4096; no fitting camera size returns an explicit error. Quality, orientation, crop zoom, exposure and autofocus controls return requested settings and actual capture metadata. See [camera controls](camera-control.md). |
| `microphoneRecord` | `dikciz_microphone_record` | Save AAC audio in an M4A container. `durationMilliseconds` defaults to 3000 and accepts 1000 through 120000. |
| `speechSpeak` | `dikciz_speech_speak` | Speak required `text` through Android device output, at most 2000 characters. Reports completion or failure. |
| `callAudio` | `dikciz_call_audio` | `action: status` reports cellular audio capture and injection support. `record` and `speak` return `call_audio_unsupported` without privileged system integration. |

Sensor discovery includes static and connected dynamic sensors. Records include ID, type, name, vendor, dynamic status, reporting mode, range, resolution and power. Actual samples contain `values`, Android accuracy, monotonic `timestampNanoseconds` and sample age. Unavailable samples contain a reason. All-sensor pages report permission failures per sensor, so one restricted sensor does not hide others. Targeting a restricted sensor by ID uses the shared permission error and optional owner-review flow. Trigger-only sensors can remain `waiting_for_trigger`. IDs address the current device inventory; rediscover after hardware changes. Every request releases its listeners. Poll only while data is needed; background Lua subscriptions remain available for event-driven use.

Camera and microphone require their Android grants and foreground eligibility. Open Dikciz before capture. Concurrent requests for the same capture resource return `hardware_busy`. Successful capture returns `state: saved`, `path`, `mimeType` and byte count. Paths are generated under app-specific external `captures` storage. Read or download them through the existing file APIs. Incomplete files are removed. Android microphone silencing returns an explicit failure when reported by the recorder.

Camera and speech accept `timeoutMilliseconds`, default 30000, range 1 through 120000. The supplied client adjusts HTTP, WebSocket and MCP response waits to cover requested hardware durations. Other clients must allow the same time. Timeouts and interruption release capture resources. Speech uses the configured Android engine and fails explicitly if unavailable. Device speaker output is not cellular audio injection. Stock Android reserves call-stream capture for privileged components; granting microphone permission does not grant call-stream access.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Calendar occurrences and next alarm
text:
## Calendar occurrences and next alarm

`contentQuery` resource `calendarInstances` reads Android-expanded occurrences, including recurring events, from local midnight today through local midnight seven calendar days later. The window follows the device time zone and DST. It is read-only and requires calendar access. Columns are `event_id`, `title`, `begin`, `end`, `allDay`, `eventLocation`, `calendar_id` and `visible`. Results are ordered by `begin`, `end` and `event_id`; use `limit`, `offset` and `hasMore`. Results include `rangeStartMilliseconds` and `rangeEndMilliseconds`. Restart pagination if calendar data changes or the date/time zone crosses a window boundary. Filter `visible: 1` for displayed calendars. All-day dates use UTC date semantics.

`deviceState.nextAlarmAtMilliseconds` is the next user-visible Android alarm timestamp, or JSON null when none is reported. It does not enumerate or create alarms. These additions use the existing shared commands across MCP, HTTP, WebSocket, HTML and Lua. See Android [calendar instances](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/provider/CalendarContract.Instances) and [next alarm](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/AlarmManager#getNextAlarmClock()).
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Permissions and limits
text:
## Permissions and limits

Missing grants return `native_permission_<requirementId>` with the shared `permissionRequest`. Opt into owner review with `autoRequestPermissions`, then explicitly retry after checking the grant. `native_access_denied` means Android rejected the operation despite declared grants, for example because of a role, ownership or foreground restriction.

Malformed fields, columns, types, ranges, authorities and references return `validation_failed`. Read-only writes return `native_read_only`. Provider failures return `native_operation_failed` or `native_unavailable`. Logs omit contact and message values.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider

title: Direct Android data and control: Capability gaps
text:
## Capability gaps

| Operation | Current route |
| --- | --- |
| Contact/calendar data, SMS/history, call history, SIMs and system snapshots | Direct commands above. |
| Apps, packages, files, APK installation, shell, screenshots and restart | Existing direct commands. |
| Notifications/media control, volume, intents and lock | Existing typed actions. |
| Hardware sensor snapshots and current location | Shared direct commands and existing background subscriptions. |
| Camera, microphone and device speech | Shared direct commands above, subject to Android foreground access. |
| Health Connect and other background sources | Existing event subscriptions. |
| Proprietary app features without a public API | Accessibility/UI automation or an API supplied by that app. |
| Silent permission grants, arbitrary private app databases, unrestricted clipboard and protected settings | Android privilege and foreground restrictions apply. |
| Fastboot and bootloader | Outside the running Android app. |

Arbitrary third-party databases, account management and privileged system settings are not implemented by these commands. Permission declarations are not a promise that every possible feature exists. Discover the running build's commands.
aliases: contacts SMS calendar subscriptions SIM clipboard Android native provider
