title: NFC tags
text:
# NFC tags

NFC commands share schemas, permissions and the native executor across HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua. Open and unlock Dikciz, enable NFC in Android settings, then present a tag. An absent adapter, disabled radio, foreground restriction or deadline is an explicit failure. Each request owns reader mode and closes its tag connection afterward.

title: NFC tags: Read and select a tag
text:
## Read and select a tag

`nfcRead` / `dikciz_nfc_read` waits up to `timeoutMilliseconds`, default 30000 and range 1 through 120000. It returns `tagIdBase64`, Android technology names, NDEF support and available NDEF bytes. A tag without NDEF support still returns its identity and technologies.

Every tag operation accepts `expectedTagIdBase64` from a prior read. Other presented tags are ignored until the deadline. The ID is at most 64 decoded bytes. A tag ID is a selector, not proof of identity or authorization.

title: NFC tags: Write NDEF
text:
## Write NDEF

`nfcWrite` / `dikciz_nfc_write` requires `dataBase64` containing a complete Android-compatible NDEF message, at most 32768 decoded bytes. Malformed messages fail before reader activation. Read-only tags and insufficient capacity fail explicitly. `format: true` permits formatting an unformatted compatible tag; its default is false.

Successful writes report `state: written` and `verified`. An ordinary NDEF write attempts read-back comparison. Formatting reports `verified: false`. A lost tag, failure or timeout can leave partial effects. Inspect the tag before retrying a write.

title: NFC tags: Raw transaction
text:
## Raw transaction

`nfcTransceive` / `dikciz_nfc_transceive` requires `technology` and `dataBase64`. Supported technologies are IsoDep, NfcA, NfcB, NfcF, NfcV, MifareClassic and MifareUltralight, subject to the presented tag and phone. Android's per-technology maximum also applies.

`ioTimeoutMilliseconds` defaults to 5000, range 1 through 60000, for technologies with configurable I/O timeouts. The outer deadline still applies. Responses include Base64 bytes and their count, bounded to 32768 bytes. Raw commands may modify a tag. Use the tag manufacturer's protocol and do not treat successful transport as application-level success.

title: NFC tags: Payment cards and multi-command protocols
text:
## Payment cards and multi-command protocols

A payment card can advertise `IsoDep` and `NfcA` without supporting NDEF. `ndefSupported: false` means there is no NDEF message through this API; it does not mean the phone cannot communicate with the card. The returned tag ID is not an account number.

Contactless payment terminals implement EMV application selection and APDU exchanges over ISO-DEP. Dikciz exposes raw `nfcTransceive` transport, not an EMV decoder, wallet provisioning or a payment terminal. JavaScript or Lua can encode commands and decode responses through that transport, subject to the card's own access rules.

Each `nfcTransceive` request opens one tag connection, sends one command and closes it. There is no persistent session or multi-command batch. Card application selection or authentication state may be lost between requests, so a stateful EMV conversation is not guaranteed by chaining independent calls. A higher-level protocol needing a continuous connection requires additional native session support. No secret card keys, PIN or payment authority are implied by a successful raw exchange.

References: [Android IsoDep](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/nfc/tech/IsoDep), [EMV contactless](https://www.emvco.com/emv-technologies/emv-contactless-chip/).

title: NFC tags: Example
text:
## Example

```json
{"type":"nfcRead","timeoutMilliseconds":30000}
```

No tag is emulated by this API. RF transactions need a compatible physical tag. See [hardware inventories](hardware-controls.md) and [command schemas](command-reference.md).

title: NFC tags: Companion workflows
text:
## Companion workflows

See [the focused companion guide](device-connections.md) for the new shared commands, native screens, required access and actual outcome states.

title: Notification management
text:
# Notification management

`notificationsList` returns active notifications with their Android key, package, title, text, post time and action tokens. Its new `actions` array describes each exposed action with `actionToken`, bounded `title` and `supportsReply`. Tokens expire after 60 seconds, are single-use and become unavailable when the notification changes or disappears.

Use `notificationManage`, MCP tool `dikciz_notification_manage`, through any ordinary binding. Notification-listener access is required. Set `autoRequestPermissions: true` for the shared owner-review flow when access is missing, then explicitly retry after granting it.

| Action | Required fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dismiss` | `notificationKey` | Ask Android to cancel that active notification. |
| `snooze` | `notificationKey`, `durationMilliseconds` | Snooze for 1000 through 604800000 milliseconds. |
| `reply` | `actionToken`, `text` | Submit a nonblank free-form inline reply through an action advertising `supportsReply`. Text is at most 4096 characters. |

Fields belonging to another action are rejected. Dismiss/snooze return `state: submitted`. Poll `notificationsList` or observe notification events to verify disappearance; Android can restrict removal of ongoing notifications. Snoozed notifications can return after the duration or an app update. No API success claims a remote message was delivered.

Reply returns `state: submitted`, `delivered: false` after Android accepts its PendingIntent. The receiving application owns processing, network transmission and delivery. Resolve the correct notification and action before submitting. Tokens are consumed even if Android later rejects dispatch, preventing accidental duplicate retries.

A missing active key returns `native_record_not_found`. Expired/consumed tokens return `notification_action_unavailable`. Plain actions return `notification_reply_unsupported` without consuming the token. Android rejection returns `notification_action_rejected`. A disconnected listener returns `notification_listener_unavailable`.

The existing Lua `notificationControl` action remains the policy-gated way to invoke a plain action token. The shared `notificationManage` command adds typed dismissal, snooze and reply without changing that action's contract.

title: Activity, resources and automation rules
text:
# Activity, resources and automation rules

Open **Dikciz settings**, **Activity & resources** to inspect command outcomes and measured resource use. The activity view shows caller identity, command, request ID, duration and status. It records metadata without command arguments, SMS bodies, screenshots, shell text, provider responses or credentials.

title: Activity, resources and automation rules: Activity history
text:
## Activity history

HTTP, WebSocket, MCP and local owner commands share the activity recorder. Local scripts and widgets retain their source identity; assistant tool calls identify the conversation. The activityRead command accepts limit, offset, optional exact actor, optional outcome and mutatingOnly. Outcomes are running, completed, rejected, failed and interrupted. The problem filter combines the last three problem states.

History survives process death, retains up to 10,000 finished records and expires finished records after seven days. Work still marked running when the process restarts becomes interrupted with outcomeKnown=false. A completed command does not imply an external effect was verified. Inspect the operation's own result, such as SMS delivery or activity-launch verification.

The activityCancel command takes activityId from a history row. It requests thread interruption for running work. The Android main thread is never interrupted; main-thread work needs its subsystem stop action. Cancellation is best effort, does not roll back effects and does not prove Android stopped an accepted operation. Read history again and use the subsystem's dedicated stop command where available.

History and administration require owner access. Read-only assistant turns can inspect activity and resources but cannot cancel work or change resource settings.

title: Activity, resources and automation rules: Resource measurements
text:
## Resource measurements

The resourceUsage command returns process CPU, memory/storage measurements, UID network counters, command executor CPU grouped by caller, and configured Lua scripts with their event subscriptions. Counters describe their measurement scope:

- Network counters cover the Android UID since boot.
- Command CPU covers the executor thread and excludes main-thread and WebView JavaScript work.
- Android does not expose reliable per-widget battery drain. The batteryAttributionAvailable field is false.
- The resource page samples only while visible. CPU needs two samples before reporting a percentage.

The resourceControl command takes target and id. A script target disables that Lua script; widget disables the exact HTML wrapper and also requires pageId. A conversation target clears its event rules and requests cancellation. imageStream and speechStream stop capture. The earlier scriptId form remains accepted alone. Configuration reload stops future deliveries; an action already in flight may finish. The resource page offers confirmations for scripts, HTML widgets, conversations and active visual capture.

The resource result reads the current saved home and lists its HTML widget subscriptions, conversations and retained visual captures. Shared-storage access is required to inspect configured resources. It cannot identify which individual JavaScript timer consumed battery. Use the measured process trend, source identity and explicit pause controls to isolate the cause.

title: Activity, resources and automation rules: Visual automation rules
text:
## Visual automation rules

Open **Dikciz settings**, **Automation rules**, **Create a rule**. Choose a trigger, optional payload condition, cooldown and speech, vibration or bounded torch action. Test a sample payload before enabling live events. Rules default to disabled.

The editor generates ordinary Lua and an event subscription. The script remains editable in the Lua script manager. Editing generated Lua manually does not rewrite the visual rule definition; saving that visual definition again replaces its generated source.

| Command | MCP tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| automationRulePreview | dikciz_automation_rule_preview | Compile Lua and simulate a sample without invoking Android. |
| automationRuleSave | dikciz_automation_rule_save | Validate and persist a rule, script and subscription. |
| automationRuleDelete | dikciz_automation_rule_delete | Remove one visual rule, script and owned subscription. |
| automationRulesList | dikciz_automation_rules_list | Read saved visual definitions with pagination. |

The installed tool schema documents nested rule fields. Supported triggers are custom events, time, battery, charging, alarms, approximate location and sensors. Other event families remain available through advanced script subscription configuration.

~~~json
{
  "rule": {
    "title": "Battery reminder",
    "event": "battery",
    "enabled": false,
    "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 60000,
    "conditionOperator": "always",
    "commands": [{"type": "speechSpeak", "text": "Automation reminder"}]
  },
  "sample": {}
}
~~~

Send this to automationRulePreview. It returns simulated=true, generated source and proposed commands. Remove sample when sending the rule to automationRuleSave. Set enabled=true only when live delivery is intended. Android permissions still apply to actual actions.

Rule definitions persist in the automationRules root namespace. Generated scripts, source capabilities and subscriptions use the existing public configuration tree and watcher.

The rule manager reopens saved definitions and confirms deletion. The native form supports one speech, vibration or torch action; the API supports up to eight. Multi-action definitions require the API or Lua editor, preventing silent loss when reopened. Alarm triggers require at least 60 seconds.

The activity page defaults to Actions. All activity includes reads; Problems combines rejected, failed and interrupted work. Refresh pauses while reading scrolled history. Both tabs and confirmation dialogs remain available to semantic UI commands.

Getting started in Settings links the owner to Android access, reusable widget documents, assistant setup and private-network listener configuration. It grants nothing automatically.

The resource screen shows enabled scripts and HTML widgets, active chat work/event rules, live visual capture and the five largest recorded callers. The API retains the full configured inventory for inspection. Disabled resources and inactive conversations remain in their normal managers.

title: Activity, resources and automation rules: On the phone
text: ## On the phone

title: APK installation sets
text:
# APK installation sets

`apkInstallSet` stages one base APK followed by its split APKs into one Android PackageInstaller session. Supply `apks: [{path: "...", sha256: "..."}]`; SHA-256 is optional, exact and verified while staging. The first file must be the base. There are at most 32 unique APKs, 512 MiB each and 1 GiB total. Paths obey the ordinary protected-file rules.

The installer checks readable APK containers and public package/signing metadata where Android can parse it. Android authoritatively validates split identities, versions, signatures and compatibility at commit. Unknown-source access and owner installation confirmation remain necessary. A queued or staged result is not installation success. Poll `apkInstallStatus` and inspect terminal callbacks.

`apkInstallCancel` requires a Dikciz-owned sessionId. It abandons a still-cancellable staging/pending session. cancellationAccepted false means the operation was terminal or too late. It never uninstalls an installed app. A raced actual success is recorded as installed; do not claim it was undone.

The existing `apkInstall` remains the standalone convenience entrypoint and shares the staging/callback machinery. See [files and APKs](files-and-apks.md) for upload, status and handoff.

Android may leave a cancelled session's confirmation visible. The cancellation result reports confirmationMayRemainOpen and instructions; close that confirmation before beginning another installation.

title: Remote access tokens
text:
# Remote access tokens

Create separate bearer credentials for clients that need different phone access. HTTP, WebSocket and MCP enforce the same grants in the shared executor, including direct calls to hidden tools. Android permissions remain a separate requirement.

title: Remote access tokens: Set up a client
text:
## Set up a client

1. Open **Settings**, **Automation**, **Configure remote bearer authentication**. Set an owner password and enable authentication.
2. Open **Manage access tokens**, then **Create token**. Name the client and select its grants.
3. Copy the generated token once into the client's secret storage. Closing the copy screen discards the recoverable value. Revoke and create another token if it is lost.
4. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every HTTP/MCP request and the WebSocket upgrade. The controller reads `DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN` from its environment. Never put credentials in URLs, prompts or command arguments.
5. Read `remoteAccessInfo` or `dikciz_remote_access_info`, then discover the permitted tools.

The existing owner password still grants full access. **Full owner access** tokens have the same authority, including creating or revoking other tokens. Keep them private. A scoped token cannot administer tokens or change authentication.

title: Remote access tokens: Choose grants
text:
## Choose grants

Grants are additive. Select **Full owner access** alone, or combine specific grants. The native picker and `remoteTokens` action `catalog` provide the current list and descriptions.

| Need | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| Read SMS history only | `sms.read` |
| Read and send SMS | `sms.read`, `sms.send` |
| Resolve a recipient from contacts and send SMS | `contacts.read`, `sms.send` |
| Read sensor samples only | `sensors.read` |
| Capture the visible screen | `screen.capture` |
| Inspect visible UI text/components | `ui.read` |
| Inspect and act on other apps' components | `ui.control` |
| Discover and open installed apps | `apps.launch` |
| Read own SIM numbers | `sim.read` |

Other grants cover contact/calendar reads and edits, call history/control, app metadata, device readings/settings, location, notification reads/actions, media metadata, file reads, script logs, all automation events, custom search indexes, speech output, Bluetooth scans, Wi-Fi scans, USB inventory and NFC reads. Check the catalog for exact IDs.

Provider access is checked by resource and action. An SMS reader can query only `sms`, even though `contentQuery` serves several providers. Write grants do not imply provider read grants. `sms.send` includes send-status and SIM selection; it hides own phone numbers unless `sim.read` is also granted.

Some grants confer broad authority. `ui.control` can send messages or change settings through another app's UI. It blocks component actions inside Dikciz itself. `notifications.control` can send inline replies. `files.read` can read every Android-accessible file outside protected credentials. `events.read` receives the shared event feed, including other operations' payloads. Combine grants only for trusted clients.

Shell, arbitrary SDK calls, Lua/HTML installation, intents, configuration changes, durable jobs and background capture/session APIs require full owner access. These operations could execute arbitrary code or retain authority beyond a narrow grant. A token grant does not bypass Android restrictions or turn a normal shell into ADB/root.

title: Remote access tokens: Administration API
text:
## Administration API

All three network transports use the same procedure:

| Action | Required fields | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | `action` | Available permission IDs, titles and descriptions. |
| `list` | `action` | Token metadata, never secrets or digests. |
| `create` | `action`, `name`, `permissions` | Metadata plus `token`, returned once. |
| `update` | `action`, `id`; at least one of `name`, `permissions`, `enabled`, `expiresAt`, `requestsPerMinute`, `smsAddresses` | Updated metadata. |
| revoke | action, id | Remaining metadata. Revocation is permanent. |
| rotate | action, id | Replacement token, returned once. The old secret stops working immediately; identity and grants remain. |

HTTP/WebSocket use command `remoteTokens`; MCP uses `dikciz_remote_tokens`. Example arguments, sent with an existing owner credential:

```json
{"action":"create","name":"Sensor dashboard","permissions":["sensors.read"]}
```

Create and update also accept expiresAt (epoch milliseconds, zero for no expiry), requestsPerMinute (0 to 10,000, zero for unlimited), and smsAddresses (up to 64 unique exact addresses; empty allows all). Omitted update fields retain their values. Expired credentials fail authentication, including on established connections. Rotation preserves expiry and limits.

When smsAddresses is nonempty, an SMS history query must include filter.address with one exact permitted address. A send must use an exact permitted recipient. An unrestricted query is denied before Android provider access. This filter does not grant SMS reads or sends by itself.

The request limit counts accepted ordinary commands across all network entrypoints in a rolling minute. The remote_rate_limited error rejects excess commands before execution. Usage survives process restart. Token metadata includes lastUsedAt (null until an accepted command), expired, and configured limits. Discovery and handshake requests do not consume this command allowance.

Call remoteAccessInfo to inspect your own effective grants, expiry, request limit and exact SMS address restrictions before choosing query arguments. The native manager offers expiry choices, limits, SMS address restrictions and rotation. Copy a rotated secret before closing the copy screen.

Names contain 1 to 80 printable characters. At most 32 tokens may exist, including disabled tokens. Grants must be known, nonempty and unique. Unknown fields are rejected. Each token has a public ID, display name, grant list, enabled flag and creation timestamp in epoch milliseconds.

Updates and revocations take effect on the next authorization check without restarting listeners. In-flight side effects cannot be rolled back. Connection-bound streams stop when their authorization monitor fails. Accepted process-owned capture sessions or jobs need their dedicated stop command or owner notification; revocation does not undo previously accepted work. Reconnect WebSocket after editing its token and initialize a fresh MCP session when changing credentials. MCP sessions are bound to the authenticated identity; another valid token cannot reuse or delete them.

Revoke every token before disabling or clearing authentication. Disabled tokens still count because opening the listeners would bypass their restrictions. Replacing the owner password preserves tokens. After the last token is revoked, the existing enable/disable and phone password-clear flows work normally.

title: Remote access tokens: Discovery and errors
text:
## Discovery and errors

`tools/list`, `controlStatus` and installed-schema search in collection `tools` filter commands by grants. Mixed provider/action schemas narrow their enums. Tool search filters before ranking and pagination. Custom collection names and documents require `search.read`; index changes require `search.write`. Packaged documentation remains readable as reference.

Restricted WebSocket hello replies contain an empty, marked snapshot unless UI reads are granted. Clients without `events.read` receive their own command replies, but no shared broadcasts. Owner clients retain full snapshots and event feeds.

A valid credential calling an unauthorized operation gets `remote_permission_denied`. A missing, malformed, disabled or revoked credential gets HTTP 401 at the network boundary, or `remote_auth_required` on an established WebSocket. An out-of-scope tool document is absent and returns `search_not_found`. A denied command does not trigger Android permission prompts or execute the operation.

title: Remote access tokens: Storage and local bindings
text:
## Storage and local bindings

The protected `/sdcard/Dikciz/control/remote-auth.json` record retains the owner's bcrypt cost-12 verifier. Generated tokens contain 256 random secret bits; only their SHA-256 digests and metadata are stored. File APIs reject the credential record, its atomic aliases and lock file. Full shell/SDK authority is an independent privilege and can reach files available to its Android identity.

Existing password-only records remain compatible. Token records use an extended version, saved atomically under a shared record lock. Invalid records fail closed. Tokens survive activity recreation and app updates.

The built-in chat, HTML bridge and enabled Lua scripts keep their direct in-process owner bindings. They do not store a bearer token or make a loopback MCP connection. Chat's read-only mode still hides write tools and independently blocks writes in the executor. Remote token grants do not weaken that check.

title: Remote device operations
text:
# Remote device operations

Connect over a private network with the [USB-free setup](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb). WebSocket, MCP and HTTP expose the same commands and Android access checks. Discover the installed build before acting, especially when release and debug packages are both installed.

title: Remote device operations: Identify the running build
text:
## Identify the running build

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http deviceInfo --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_package_info --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"packageName":"eu.psyb0t.dikciz.launcher"}' --pretty
```

`deviceInfo` returns `application`, `android` and `uptimeMilliseconds`. `application` identifies the serving package, installed version, process ID and launcher `instanceId`. The Android object reports SDK level, release, manufacturer and model. `packageInfo` reports a requested installed package, including its version, enabled/debuggable flags, target SDK and nullable launch component. It returns `package_not_found` when the package is absent or invisible. Package names are validated before PackageManager access.

Release uses `eu.psyb0t.dikciz.launcher`; debug uses `eu.psyb0t.dikciz.launcher.debug`. Updating one does not update the other. Both read the public listener settings, so running both can cause port conflicts. A listener that cannot bind retries quickly at first and then every 30 seconds while the activity remains alive. Once the conflict clears, both listeners recover without reopening the launcher.

title: Remote device operations: Recover after an APK update
text:
## Recover after an APK update

After Obtainium, Android's installer or `adb install -r` replaces the APK, Android stops the old process. The new package receives `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` and starts its automation service independently of Home. The service enters foreground before requesting Home startup, then reloads the saved configuration, background event sources, configuration observers and alarm schedules. It stops again if no configured automation needs it. Recovery also requests rebinding for notification access already enabled by the owner; Android restores enabled Accessibility bindings. It requests a fresh launcher activity when Dikciz is the default Home app or has **Draw over other apps** access. Home startup reloads scripts, authentication, configuration watchers, WebSocket and HTTP/MCP listeners. Reconnect WebSocket and HTTP clients and create a fresh MCP session. Verify the new version and instance with `deviceInfo`.

If background startup is unavailable or blocked by the device, tap the **Dikciz updated** notification. Its action opens the updated launcher directly. Opening Dikciz clears this notification. Notification permission must be enabled to see it; otherwise open Dikciz from the app list. This recovery does not change the default Home app or grant permissions. An update to one installed package does not update or select the other package.

The update receiver ships in the new APK, so it also handles the first update from an older version. It only handles package replacement, not a manual force-stop, reboot or crash. Manufacturer background restrictions can still require opening the app manually.

title: Remote device operations: Restart without dropping the only recovery path
text:
## Restart without dropping the only recovery path

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py websocket restart --host phone.example --port 19001 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_restart --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http restart --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
```

Use one of these commands. Each accepts no arguments. HTML can request the same operation with `dikciz.request({ type: "restart" })`; enabled Lua scripts can use `context.requestJson([[{"type":"restart"}]])`. The server returns `{ "state": "scheduled", "instanceId": "..." }` before recreating the launcher activity and both listeners. HTML acknowledges response delivery after its promise handlers run; Lua schedules the lifecycle action after the current script result is handled. Saved configuration, widget state, files and the app process remain intact. The command also permits recovery from safe mode or a missing-storage screen and opens normal mode.

Reconnect using the same endpoint. Start a fresh MCP session. Read `deviceInfo` until its `application.instanceId` differs from the acknowledged value, then verify the home or configuration. A scheduled reply alone does not prove recovery. `restart` recreates the running package, so inspect its package name before requesting it. It does not switch between release and debug packages.

Do not kill the launcher through its own shell to restart it. An in-process socket cannot revive an Android force-stopped package. If Android has stopped the whole app, open it on the phone or use a separately authorized privileged controller.

title: Remote device operations: Switch between debug and release
text:
## Switch between debug and release

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_launcher_handoff --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"packageName":"eu.psyb0t.dikciz.launcher"}' --pretty
```

`launcherHandoff` accepts only the installed Dikciz release and debug package names. It requires a target version of 0.15.3 or newer and checks that the target has file access before releasing the current listeners. Missing access returns `target_access_required`; an older build returns `unsupported_launcher_version`. Neither refusal disconnects the serving build. Grant file access to each build once through Android setup. A same-package request returns `already_active` and changes nothing.

A cross-package request writes its `scheduled` reply, closes the serving listeners, stops the source automation service and launches the target without killing the source process. It probes both target ports, including a real interface for wildcard bindings. Once the ports respond it finishes the source activity. If startup fails or the target does not respond within 30 seconds, the source retries its original listener configuration and resumes its permitted automation service. Reconnect and inspect `deviceInfo` or the actual snapshot package to verify the requested build took control. The acknowledgement alone is not proof. This changes the running build, not the Android default Home role.

title: Remote device operations: See and operate other apps
text:
## See and operate other apps

Enable **Dikciz cross-app automation** in Android Accessibility settings. `accessibilitySnapshot` and `accessibilityAction` inspect and act on the current Android window. Gesture and global navigation actions are available through `automationDispatch`. Android keeps permission dialogs, protected windows and other restrictions under its control.

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py websocket displayScreenshot --host phone.example --port 19001 --png-file ./display.png
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http displayScreenshot --host phone.example --port 19002 --png-file ./display.png
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_display_screenshot --host phone.example --port 19002 --png-file ./display.png
```

`displayScreenshot` captures the visible Android display, including other apps, on Android 11 or newer with enabled Accessibility access. Every interface retains `pngBase64` and dimensions in its operation result. MCP also returns the standard image content block. Existing `screenshot` remains a capture of the launcher window. The client supports `--png-file` on WebSocket, HTTP and MCP, and refuses to replace an existing output file unless you pass `--overwrite`.

Missing Accessibility returns `accessibility_not_enabled`; older Android returns `unsupported_android_version`. Platform screenshot rejection returns `display_screenshot_failed`, including the Android status number. Android rate limits and secure-window restrictions still apply. A callback timeout returns `timeout`.

title: Remote device operations: Existing operations without a computer-side ADB connection
text:
## Existing operations without a computer-side ADB connection

| Operation | Control | Android requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read version and package details | `deviceInfo`, `packageInfo` | Installed package visibility. |
| Restart the running launcher | `restart` | Reachable running listener. |
| Switch debug/release controller | `launcherHandoff` | Installed target with file access and shared listener support. |
| Browse, upload and download files | `fileList`, `fileRead`, `fileWrite`, `fileMkdir` | Read/write access to the path. |
| Install or update an APK | `apkInstall`, `apkInstallStatus` | Unknown-source access and Android confirmation. |
| Inspect logs | `scriptLogs`, file APIs | Dikciz logs; other apps and system logs have separate restrictions. |
| Launch apps and Android settings | `appAction`, `intent` | Exported destination and Android access. |
| UI inspection, input and navigation | Accessibility commands and typed actions | Owner-enabled Accessibility service. |
| Capture the visible display | `displayScreenshot` | Android 11+ and Accessibility. |
| Execute ordinary CLI commands | `shell` with `root: false` | Dikciz app permissions. |
| Execute privileged commands, force-stop other apps or request reboot modes | `shell` with `root: true` | A working, approved root provider. |

An ordinary app shell has different permissions from `adb shell`. It cannot silently grant protected permissions, read other apps or system logs, force-stop arbitrary packages, or reboot the device. Root is optional and never silently substituted after a denial. Dikciz currently has no Shizuku backend. Use native controls where available and read `automationStatus` for missing Android access. The [files, APKs and shell guide](files-and-apks.md) owns timeout, output and installer contracts. Bootloader and fastboot operation happens outside Android and cannot be served by an Android app socket.

title: Safety, places and journeys
text:
# Safety, places and journeys

Open **Settings**, **Safety, journeys and devices** for the SOS app and native Places/Trips screens. SOS is also under **Dikciz**, **Apps**. Its complete HTML/CSS/JavaScript interface, JavaScript backend and state live in `/sdcard/Dikciz/apps/sos/`; its decisions use the same [custom-app platform](custom-apps.md) available to owner-created apps. The same operations are available through HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua. Discover the installed schemas before sending commands.

title: Safety, places and journeys: Contact plans and check-ins
text:
## Contact plans and check-ins

Save exact contact addresses with `sosPlanSave`. Each contact has `address` and optional `label`. The app can search phone contacts without modifying them. Saving a plan stays inactive. Preview with `sosPreview`; it does not submit SMS. These compatibility commands invoke the bundled app backend; removing or disabling that app makes its commands unavailable until restored or enabled. Preview enforces read-only host commands even if its source has been edited.

`checkInSeconds` defaults to 3600, minimum 60. `graceSeconds` defaults to 60, minimum 5. `updateSeconds` defaults to 600, minimum 60. `maximumUpdates` defaults to 3, range 1..24. Up to ten distinct recipients are allowed. The optional message supports `{location}`, `{accuracyMeters}` and `{timestamp}`; absent or stale fixes remain explicitly unavailable. Optional `subscriptionId` chooses an SMS SIM.

Use `sosControl` with `action: arm` or `trigger` and `confirm: true`. Arming waits for the check-in deadline, then enters a cancellation grace. Triggering begins the grace immediately. `checkIn` resets the check-in deadline. `cancel` prevents future submissions. It cannot recall submitted SMS. Read `sosStatus` for saved plan, run state and receipt keys. Query the existing `smsStatus` command for carrier outcomes; submission is not delivery.

Monitoring requires foreground location, SMS sending and notification access. A visible custom-app foreground notification provides **Pause apps**. Android can delay inexact alarms, restrict background starts, stop processes or lose service. Rebooted or interrupted claimed runs become `needs_review` and do not resume outgoing messages automatically. This is an owner automation, not a guaranteed emergency service. Review permissions and test cancellation before relying on a plan.

Each recipient/update has a persisted idempotency key and frozen message before dispatch. The native SMS ledger preserves accepted submissions; interrupted claimed batches need review rather than automatic replay. A completed run stops at the configured update limit; rejected submissions need review.

title: Safety, places and journeys: Audible cancellation warning
text:
## Audible cancellation warning

During cancellation grace, Dikciz shows a large countdown and **Cancel SOS** button over other apps when Draw over other apps access is granted. The alert uses a full-screen dark backdrop and a centered card with a pinned action. Background taps and Back do not dismiss the alert or reach the app underneath; use **Cancel SOS** to stop pending messages. Without that access, it shows a dialog while a Dikciz activity is visible and retains an urgent **SOS message pending** notification with its own **Cancel SOS** action. Tapping the notification opens Safety controls. Android controls whether a heads-up or lock-screen notification appears; an overlay cannot bypass the keyguard or system-protected windows.

The warning pulses an alarm tone and vibration and uses an installed offline English TTS voice to explain that SOS messages are pending and how to cancel. For grace periods longer than ten seconds, it speaks another warning near the final ten seconds. The app does not change volume or Do Not Disturb. An absent speech engine or offline voice leaves the visual and tone warning available. Arming requires the separate SOS countdown notification channel to remain urgent.

`sosStatus.warning` reports whether a warning episode is active, the observed presentation, attached unlocked-screen visibility, remaining seconds, requested audio/vibration, alarm volume and speech state. These are execution observations, not proof that a person heard the alert. The same presentation runs for manual triggers, missed check-ins and the grace interval before subsequent configured updates. API/native cancellation stops future sends and warning resources. A message already submitted cannot be recalled. Ordinary geofences and route recording stay quiet and continue when only SOS is cancelled.


The warning card above was captured on the isolated emulator before cancellation.

title: Safety, places and journeys: Places
text:
## Places

`geofenceSave` accepts `title`, latitude, longitude and `radiusMeters` (100..1000000), optional ID, `enabled` (false by default) and `dwellMilliseconds`. Up to 32 fences can be saved. Monitoring uses Android location callbacks, accuracy checks and crossing hysteresis, with a visible location service. It emits `geofence.enter`, `geofence.exit` and optional `geofence.dwell` through the ordinary custom-event bus. Event payloads identify the fence and observed fix. Dwell uses elapsed time. A reboot establishes a fresh observation.

List with `geofencesList` and ordinary offset/limit pagination. Delete one exact ID with `geofenceDelete`. A renamed fence keeps its observation state when its geometry and monitoring settings remain unchanged.

title: Safety, places and journeys: Recorded journeys
text:
## Recorded journeys

`journeyControl` with `action: start` starts one active route, optionally naming it and choosing `sampleIntervalMilliseconds` (1000..60000, default 10000). `action: stop` requires the journey ID. No location is invented between samples. Distance sums accepted sampled segments and includes GPS uncertainty.

`journeysList` lists saved summaries. `journeyRead` pages ordered points using ID, offset and limit; follow `hasMore`. Each point includes fix time and accuracy. Up to 64 journeys and 10000 points per journey are retained. Reboot interrupts recording. Stop before deleting; `journeyDelete` requires ID and `confirm: true`, and removes owned route points too. The native route preview draws recorded coordinates locally.

SOS plans and run state live in `/sdcard/Dikciz/apps/sos/state.json`, while running/stopped flags, timer claims and native run observations remain private SQLite records. Existing private SOS plans migrate once; previously active runs require review. Geofences and route history remain private companion data. These records and custom apps are not currently included in portable home/chat backups.

A public-home reset does not recall SMS. Cancel active safety monitoring explicitly before resetting a setup, and preserve the SOS app state separately if needed.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial
text:
# Dikciz scripting tutorial

For installation, the starter home, AI chat, remote connections and Android hardware, start with the [complete Dikciz tutorial](tutorial.md). This guide is the hands-on HTML and Lua companion. For a smaller complete app with JavaScript UI/backend, start with [the GPS todo tutorial](todo-app-tutorial.md).

Dikciz has two ways to make the home react to the phone. HTML widgets draw and handle visible interaction. Lua and background JavaScript scripts run when an event arrives. Both use the same event bus, page and widget addresses, action executor, Android access state, and logs.

This tutorial builds one small pipeline that you can copy and extend:

```text
HTML button -> custom event -> Lua script -> saved widget state + custom result event -> HTML update
```

The same shape works for battery, location, notifications, calendar changes, sensors, media sessions, Android accessibility events, and the other native event sources listed below.

The [configuration guide](dikciz-configuration.md) owns the public file schema. [Automation control](automation-control.md) owns the exact WebSocket and MCP protocol. This guide explains how to combine them into working automations.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Start with the right pieces
text:
## Start with the right pieces

For an installable package containing both an interface and background logic, read [custom apps](custom-apps.md) and build the bundled [Travel todo example](todo-app-tutorial.md). An app has its own UI files, Lua/JavaScript backend, state, subscriptions and shared Dikciz command access. The bundled SOS workflow uses this public platform. The standalone script/widget pipeline below remains available.

Install Dikciz, make it your Android Home app, and grant shared-storage access. The first run creates `/sdcard/Dikciz/`, which holds every script, policy, subscription, widget, package, state file, and log.

Use the native launcher for the visible parts:

1. Add an **HTML widget** from **Add to this page** when you need a visible control or display.
2. Open **Settings**, then **Scripts**, then **New Lua script** or **New JavaScript script** for background or event-driven logic. The [JavaScript guide](background-javascript.md) documents `onEvent`, shared actions and runtime limits; the Lua examples below use `on_event`.
3. Open **Settings**, then **Automation**, then **Set up full device access** before using an Android source or action that needs owner approval.

The script editor writes a script's title, enabled state, source, and state. The public automation files choose which events it receives and which actions it may return. A script without both an enabled policy and an enabled subscription can show source in the editor but cannot complete an automation action.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Know what talks to what
text:
## Know what talks to what

Every native event and custom event has the same envelope:

```json
{
  "type": "notificationPosted",
  "source": "notification-listener",
  "timestampMilliseconds": 0,
  "coalescingKey": "optional-key",
  "payload": {}
}
```

`type` selects the event. `payload` carries the event-specific data. Lua receives the event as its `event` argument. An HTML widget receives the same record through `dikciz.onEvent(...)` and the browser `dikciz-event` event.

The delivery path is deliberately simple:

```text
Android source or custom event
          |
          +--> enabled Lua subscription --> on_event(event) --> typed actions
          |                                           |              |
          |                                           |              +--> Android or launcher work
          |                                           |              +--> saved widget state
          |                                           |              +--> custom result event
          |
          +--> rendered HTML widget subscription --> dikciz.onEvent(listener) --> DOM update
```

An HTML widget only receives events while its page is selected and its WebView exists. Lua continues to receive enabled subscriptions in the background. Put durable work in Lua. Put rendering and taps in HTML.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Use stable page and widget addresses
text:
## Use stable page and widget addresses

A page has a human-readable address such as `1H1V`. A widget address joins that page and the widget ID:

```text
1H1V-command-deck
2H1V-weather-card
```

Use a full address only when talking to another widget. An HTML widget should use `selfWidget` for itself so moving it to another page does not break its code.

```javascript
console.log(selfWidget.id);       // command-deck
console.log(selfWidget.page);     // 1H1V
console.log(selfWidget.address);  // 1H1V-command-deck
console.log(selfWidget.cell);     // { column, row, columnSpan, rowSpan }
```

Use `dikciz.pages()` to inspect the current page map. It exposes page IDs, addresses, and the `home` alias. Use `await dikciz.home()` or `await dikciz.widget(address)` after a configuration change when you need a fresh saved record.

```javascript
const pages = dikciz.pages();
const home = pages.home;
const target = await dikciz.widget("2H1V-weather-card");
```

Do not save pixel coordinates. `cell` is the persistent grid rectangle. Screen bounds change with rotation, density, and the current device.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Subscribe to events
text:
## Subscribe to events

Each Lua subscription, and each HTML widget `eventSubscriptions` entry, has this common shape:

```json
{
  "event": "battery",
  "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 60000,
  "coalescingKey": "battery-card"
}
```

`minimumIntervalMilliseconds` is a per-subscription delivery floor. It prevents that one subscriber from receiving the same source too often. `coalescingKey` is optional and helps make repeated work identifiable. It is not a global throttle.

Lua also needs the matching policy capability, and the policy must be enabled. Dikciz does not deliver an event to a script whose policy lacks it, and logs `capability_denied` instead. Where an event has a metadata and a content capability, either one admits the event, but the content fields listed below reach the script only with the content capability. HTML widgets do not use Lua policy files, but Android still requires the relevant permission or special access.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Every built-in event
text:
### Every built-in event

| Event | Lua capability | Extra subscription fields or notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | `time` | Current time source. |
| `battery` | `battery` | Battery level and status changes. |
| `charging` | `charging` | Charging state changes. |
| `powerSaveMode` | `powerSaveState` | Power Saver changes. |
| `deviceIdleMode` | `deviceIdleState` | Device idle changes. |
| `nightMode` | `nightModeState` | System night-mode changes. |
| `deviceConfiguration` | `deviceConfiguration` | Device configuration changes, including font scale. |
| `packageChanged` | `appPackagesMetadata` | Installed package metadata changes. |
| `ringerMode` | `ringerModeState` | Ringer-mode changes. |
| `interruptionFilter` | `interruptionFilterState` | Do Not Disturb interruption-filter changes. |
| `connectivity` | `connectivity` | Network state changes. |
| `thermalStatus` | `thermalState` | Thermal-status changes. |
| `bluetoothState` | `bluetoothState` | Bluetooth state changes. |
| `screen` | `screen` | Screen on and off changes. |
| `userPresent` | `userPresence` | Android reports that the user is present. |
| `alarm` | `alarm` | Requires `alarmIntervalMilliseconds`. |
| `sensor` | `sensors` | Requires `sensorTypes` and `samplingPeriodMicroseconds`. |
| `healthDailySteps` | `healthSteps` | Requires `healthRefreshIntervalMilliseconds`. |
| `location` | `locationApproximate` or `locationPrecise` | Requires `locationPrecision`, either `approximate` or `precise`. |
| `calendarEvent` | `calendarEventsMetadata` or `calendarEventsContent` | `calendarEventsContent` adds `title`, `description`, and `location`. |
| `contactsChanged` | `contactsMetadata` | Contacts change notification. |
| `phoneState` | `phoneState` | Phone call-state changes. |
| `smsReceived` | `smsMetadata` or `smsContent` | `smsContent` adds the `messages` list with each sender and body. |
| `notificationPosted` | `notificationsMetadata` or `notificationsContent` | Optional `packages` filter. `notificationsContent` adds `title` and `text`. |
| `notificationRemoved` | `notificationsMetadata` or `notificationsContent` | Optional `packages` filter. `notificationsContent` adds `title` and `text`. |
| `mediaSession` | `mediaSessionsMetadata` or `mediaSessionsContent` | Optional `packages` filter. `mediaSessionsContent` adds `title`, `artist`, and `album`. |
| `clipboardChanged` | `clipboardMetadata` or `clipboardContent` | `clipboardContent` adds `text` and `textTruncated`. |
| `accessibilityWindow` | `accessibility` | Requires the owner to enable Dikciz in Android Accessibility settings. |
| `accessibilityServiceState` | `accessibility` | Reports `connected`, `interrupted`, or `disconnected`. |
| `widgetChanged` | `widgetState` | A Dikciz widget state change. |
| `deviceAdminState` | `deviceAdministration` | Device Administration state changes. |
| `manual` | `manualTrigger` | Produced by the script dashboard, an HTML command, WebSocket, or MCP trigger. |

Any other valid event name is a custom event. It must start with a letter, be 1 through 128 characters, and use only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, or `-`. Lua custom subscriptions use the `manualTrigger` capability.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: The special subscription fields
text:
### The special subscription fields

Use these fields only on the event that supports them:

```json
{
  "event": "alarm",
  "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 0,
  "alarmIntervalMilliseconds": 60000
}
```

```json
{
  "event": "location",
  "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 300000,
  "locationPrecision": "approximate"
}
```

```json
{
  "event": "sensor",
  "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 0,
  "sensorTypes": [1],
  "samplingPeriodMicroseconds": 200000
}
```

```json
{
  "event": "notificationPosted",
  "minimumIntervalMilliseconds": 0,
  "packages": ["com.example.app"]
}
```

An approximate location payload rounds latitude and longitude to two decimal places. A precise subscription needs fine-location access and carries provider, latitude, longitude, accuracy, altitude, bearing, and speed. A precise subscription without fine location receives no event.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Build a complete custom-event workflow
text:
## Build a complete custom-event workflow

This example makes an HTML button ask a Lua script to update the widget and report back. It proves the full pipe without relying on a device sensor or third-party app.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: 1. Add an HTML widget
Dikciz scripting tutorial: 2. Create the Lua script and policy
Dikciz scripting tutorial: 3. Check the result
text:
### 3. Check the result

Open the native script dashboard or **Settings**, then **Scripts**, and open the script logs. You should see the event, its final status, both action outcomes, and any reason for a failure. The dashboard, Settings log viewer, WebSocket `scriptLogs`, and MCP `dikciz_script_logs` show the same bounded safe log projection.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Read and change widget state
text:
## Read and change widget state

Use saved state for data that must survive page changes, a renderer restart, or a phone restart.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Current widget state
Dikciz scripting tutorial: Another widget's saved state
Dikciz scripting tutorial: Patch the current DOM only
Dikciz scripting tutorial: HTML bridge reference
text:
## HTML bridge reference

The native bridge creates `window.dikciz`, `window.selfWidget`, and a `dikciz-ready` event. Start bridge work from that event. Do not call the transport-only `receiveEvent` or `receiveState` functions yourself.

`selfWidget.visible` reports whether the owning WebView is visible in the launcher window. Listen for `dikciz-visibility` and inspect `event.detail.visible` to start or stop foreground polling. A preloaded neighboring page can receive `dikciz-ready` while invisible; readiness alone does not mean the user opened the page.

Long press the HTML content, background or top handle for whole-widget controls. Edit opens the complete HTML, CSS, JavaScript and state; Delete removes the WebView and its owned files. To change one section, edit the document source while preserving its siblings. DOM sections and `data-*` attributes do not create native preset objects or independent native Edit/Delete menus.

| API | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `dikciz.request(document, options)` | Return the complete canonical command response, including error and permission metadata. `options.responseTimeoutMilliseconds` defaults to at least 60 seconds or the command timeout or duration plus five seconds; zero disables the response timer. A response timeout does not cancel dispatched work. |
| `dikciz.command(type, fields, options)` | Run one launcher command and receive its result or rejected promise. Errors retain permission recovery and the raw response. Response timeout options match `dikciz.request`. Examples: `diagnostics`, `automationStatus`, `homeGet`, `widgetGet`, `scriptLogs`, `accessibilitySnapshot`, `shell`, and `intent`. The full command list is in [Automation control](automation-control.md). |
| `dikciz.dispatch({ actions })` | Run one non-empty array of typed actions through the same executor Lua uses. Read `result.actions` for each outcome. |
| `dikciz.emitEvent(name, payload, coalescingKey)` | Emit one custom event. This is shorthand for a one-action dispatch. |
| `dikciz.onEvent(listener)` | Receive matching configured events while the widget renders. It returns an unsubscribe function. |
| `dikciz.fitContent()` | Ask the native frame to remeasure a `heightMode: "content"` widget. It never expands past the assigned grid cells. |
| `dikciz.pages()` | Read the current page map by ID, address, and `home`. |
| `dikciz.home()` | Read the current saved home document. |
| `dikciz.widget(address)` | Read one current saved widget record. |
| `dikciz.patchWidget(address, values)` | Persist a full allowed widget-field patch. HTML widgets accept `title`, `html`, `css`, `javascript`, `state`, `itemStates`, and `eventSubscriptions`. Subscription patches replace the array; read existing entries through `selfWidget.get()` first. Replacing source can destroy the calling WebView. |
| `dikciz.patchWidgetState(address, values)` | Persist only another HTML widget's `state`. |
| `dikciz.patchDom(address, selector, values)` | Change a rendered HTML target without saving it. |
| `selfWidget.get()` | Read this widget's current saved record. |
| `selfWidget.patch(values)` | Persist an allowed patch to this widget. |
| `selfWidget.patchState(values)` | Persist this widget's state and receive `dikciz-state`. |
| `selfWidget.patchDom(selector, values)` | Change a selected, rendered element inside this widget. |
| `selfWidget.itemFor(element)`, `selfWidget.item(id)` | Resolve a card instance with independent state and an owned storage directory. |
| `item.getState()`, `item.patchState(values)` | Read or replace one card's state while preserving its siblings. `item.state` reads the current live value. |
| `item.readFile(name, options)`, `item.writeFile(name, dataBase64, options)` | Use file commands inside the instance directory. File contents use base64; `state.json` is reserved for `patchState`. |

Wrapper state lives in `pages/<page-id>/widgets/<webview-id>/state.json`. Card state lives in that directory's `items/<instance-id>/state.json`. Use a stable `data-dikciz-item-id` on each authored card and scope DOM queries to its root. When authoring or copying a section, give its state namespace a distinct ID. Separate WebView instances already have separate owning directories. For example, inside a `dikciz-ready` handler:

```javascript
const root = document.querySelector("[data-dikciz-item-id]");
const item = selfWidget.itemFor(root);
const previous = await item.getState();
await item.patchState({...previous, text:"Saved for this instance"});
```

`selfWidget.itemStates` is the current map of card states. `dikciz-item-state` delivers its replacement without recreating the document. Wrapper state continues to use `selfWidget.state` and `dikciz-state`. A source edit that removes a namespace marker and state entry removes its owned files on save. Native Delete removes the entire WebView. Removing the wrapper removes all its owned instance files. Do not use a shared library directory for live state.

The browser also receives these events:

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `dikciz-ready` | The native bridge is ready. |
| `dikciz-visibility` | Native page/window visibility changed; `event.detail.visible` is a Boolean. |
| `dikciz-state` | This widget's saved state was replaced. Read `event.detail`. |
| `dikciz-event` | A matching native or custom automation event arrived. Read `event.detail`. |

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Return device and launcher actions from Lua
text:
## Return device and launcher actions from Lua

Lua returns one status plus an `actions` array. The matching policy capability must appear in the script policy's `actions` list. Most names match the action type; `setMediaVolume` uses `mediaVolume`. The [typed action reference](typed-actions.md) lists every action's fields, policy name and binding-specific constraints. HTML can dispatch the same actions directly because its owner pressed a visible widget control, but Android access checks still apply.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `selectPage` | Select a page by `pageId`. |
| `patchWidget` | Persist allowed HTML widget fields or state by full widget address. |
| `patchState` | Persist the current script's state. |
| `patchDom` | Change a currently rendered HTML target without saving it. |
| `launchApp` | Open a flattened Android component. |
| `appAction` | Launch, open app info, uninstall, or force stop a component. Lua cannot use `addShortcut` because it has no selected-page context. |
| `postNotification` | Post an Android notification. |
| `sendSms` | Send an SMS when Android grants `SEND_SMS`. Android may show its own confirmation or rate-limit a non-default SMS app. |
| `explicitIntent` | Send an explicit Android activity or broadcast intent. Android decides whether it accepts it. |
| `emitEvent` | Publish a custom event with a JSON payload. |
| `mediaControl` | Control an allowed media session. |
| `setMediaVolume` | Set integer `levelPercent` from 0 through 100. The Lua policy action name is `mediaVolume`. |
| `notificationControl` | Invoke a supported notification action token. |
| `lockDevice` | Lock the screen after the owner enables Dikciz Device Administration. |
| `accessibilityAction` | Act on a fresh bounded Accessibility snapshot node. |
| `accessibilityGesture` | Send a bounded tap or swipe tied to a fresh Accessibility snapshot. |
| `accessibilityGlobalAction` | Ask Accessibility to perform back, home, recents, notifications, quick settings, lock screen, or screenshot. |

App and activity launch actions use the [shared foreground verification contract](automation-control.md). `launched` means the target package was observed as the active visible window. Missing Accessibility returns `launch_unverified`; a target that never appears returns `launch_not_observed`. A locked device returns `device_locked`. These outcomes also appear in Lua action logs and script run status. Broadcast intents retain their dispatch outcome.

For cross-app actions, first obtain a fresh `accessibilitySnapshot`. Its `snapshotId` expires after five seconds. Dikciz rechecks the active window and rejects an expired or changed snapshot instead of acting on stale UI.

Enabled Lua scripts can call ordinary launcher commands through `context.request(json)` or `context.requestJson(json)`. Both accept a JSON object encoded as a string or a bounded Lua object table and return the canonical result or error envelope. Table inputs are encoded by the runtime, so names, message bodies and provider filters need no manual JSON escaping. Encoding rejects cyclic tables and permits at most eight nesting levels and 2048 expanded field entries. A conservative one-MiB JSON estimate is checked before allocation, counting up to six bytes per text character. Nested tables with consecutive integer keys become arrays; empty tables become objects, and nil fields are omitted. Use a JSON string when explicit null or an empty array is required. `request` returns a read-only Lua table; `requestJson` preserves the complete JSON representation, including nulls and empty arrays. For example, `context.request([[{"type":"deviceInfo"}]])` returns device information. Failed commands retain `code`, `message`, and any `permissionRequest`. Set `autoRequestPermissions` on the command to request the same on-device access review as a network client.

Live shell streaming requires WebSocket, MCP or HTTP. HTML and Lua command calls have no stream delivery channel.

Enabling a script grants owner command access, including app-accessible files and shell commands through these functions. Android permissions and root approval still apply. The policy's returned-action list applies to typed actions returned by `on_event`; it does not restrict `context.request`. Native command execution is excluded from Lua CPU and allocation accounting, while aggregate command response bytes remain bounded by the Lua memory allowance.

Lua has no Android-object or dynamic-load access. Its supported globals are `assert`, `error`, `ipairs`, `next`, `pairs`, `pcall`, `select`, `tonumber`, `tostring`, `type`, and `xpcall`, plus `math`, `string`, `table`, and `bit32`. `io`, `os`, `package`, `require`, `load`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `debug`, and `print` are unavailable.

title: Dikciz scripting tutorial: Trigger work and diagnose failures
text:
## Trigger work and diagnose failures

There are four normal ways to start a workflow:

1. Run a script from the dashboard. It produces a `manual` event.
2. Dispatch an action from an HTML button.
3. Emit a custom event from HTML, Lua, WebSocket, or MCP.
4. Subscribe to an Android source such as time, location, notification, sensor, or Accessibility.

When a result surprises you, check the script's status and logs first. Common outcomes are:

| Outcome | Meaning and next step |
| --- | --- |
| `capability_denied` | Add the event capability or action to the enabled policy. |
| `rate_limited` | The event arrived inside the subscription's `minimumIntervalMilliseconds` and was dropped. Dikciz records this at `debug` log level. |
| `android_permission_denied` | Open **Settings**, then **Automation**, then grant the Android access. |
| `device_admin_inactive` | Enable Dikciz Device Administration before `lockDevice`. |
| `accessibility_not_enabled` | Enable Dikciz cross-app automation in Android Accessibility settings. |
| `root_unavailable` | The device did not grant `su`. Root-only work did not run as the app user. |
| `target_not_rendered` | `patchDom` targeted a widget that is not currently rendered. Use saved state or select the page first. |
| `invalid_lua` | Open the script log. Its diagnostic names the source line when LuaJ provides it. |

Finish every workflow by checking all three layers:

1. The visible widget result or Android effect.
2. The script dashboard status and logs.
3. The saved files under `/sdcard/Dikciz/` when your flow persists state.

That gives you a stable loop: subscribe, inspect `event`, return typed actions, observe their exact outcome, and keep visible HTML state separate from background Lua logic.

JSON state patches preserve null as a stored value, including nested objects and arrays. Null does not remove a key. This matches the saved widget/script JSON format.

title: Offline search
text:
# Offline search

Dikciz has one persistent SQLite search service shared by HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML, Lua and embedded chat. It runs on the phone without embeddings, a network connection, API keys or model downloads.
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Collections
text:
## Collections

| Collection | Content | Update behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs` | Packaged operating guides and recipes plus sections from the public manuals | Rebuilt from the serving APK when its corpus fingerprint changes |
| `tools` | Installed tool descriptions, complete input schemas and related authored aliases | Rebuilt when installed contracts or documentation change |
| Owner name | Explicitly submitted text and aliases | Upsert, remove or clear through the shared command API |

The documentation corpus omits the generated command reference, which is represented by live tool schemas, and the changelog. Screenshot gallery markup is omitted. Large sections are split into bounded parts; a part can contain a fragment of a long code example, so fetch adjacent results or the original manual before treating it as a complete script. Short operating recipes remain complete resources.

Collections are separate search scopes. Content is not automatically copied from contacts, messages, chat history or device files. Index data lives in the app's private `local-search.db`, separately from public launcher configuration. Activity recreation and APK updates preserve custom collections; clearing app data or uninstalling removes them. Release and debug packages have separate databases.
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Search and read
text:
## Search and read

HTTP and WebSocket accept an ordinary command:

```json
{"type":"searchQuery","collection":"docs","query":"custom event lua widget","limit":5,"offset":0}
```

MCP uses `dikciz_search_query` with the same arguments except `type`. HTML uses `await dikciz.command("searchQuery", arguments)`; Lua uses `context.requestJson` with the command JSON. All bindings share validation, procedure, results and errors.

The result contains `items`, `collection`, `limit`, `offset`, `total`, `hasMore`, `corrections` and `engine:"sqlite-fts4-bm25"`. Every hit has `id`, `title`, `uri`, `score` and a bounded `excerpt`. Tool hits additionally carry the exact installed `tool` descriptor and `inputSchema`. Scores order one query's results; they are not probabilities or comparable across unrelated queries.

Read full text with `searchRead` / `dikciz_search_read`:

```json
{"collection":"docs","id":"recipes/event-setup"}
```

The response includes the full `text` and `aliases`. MCP can also read an exact documentation URI returned by search through `resources/read`. The browsable resource catalog remains a short guide list; search reaches the additional manual sections without enumerating that catalog.

Queries accept 1 to 16 terms, at most 512 characters overall and 80 per term. They are plain text, not SQL or FTS expressions. Limits are 1 to 20, default 5; offsets are 0 to 10000. Empty or punctuation-only queries fail validation. An unknown query or collection returns an empty page. An unknown document ID returns `search_not_found`.
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Ranking and spelling
text:
## Ranking and spelling

SQLite FTS4 retrieves matching documents. Weighted BM25 favors identifiers/titles over aliases and body text. Term coverage and exact identifier/title matches add ranking boosts. Ranking statistics come only from the selected collection and permitted documents. Unrelated collections and hidden tools cannot change its scores. Equal scores use document ID order for stable pagination.

Normalization folds case and accents, and splits camelCase and punctuation-separated identifiers. Prefixes apply to terms of at least three characters. Authored aliases cover domain terminology and alternative task descriptions. Common English filler words do not affect retrieval unless they are the entire query.

With `fuzzy:true`, the default, a missing term of at least four characters can expand to at most three nearby vocabulary terms. Edit distance is at most one, or two for words of at least eight characters. Corrections are limited to the selected collection and permitted documents, and are returned in `corrections`. Set `fuzzy:false` to disable that expansion. Prefixes are not arbitrary substring search, and spelling correction is not semantic understanding. There is no stemming or automatic translation.
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Reuse with owner data
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Assistant and access
text:
## Assistant and access

Embedded chat exposes `phone_search` directly. Its required `query` and optional `collection`, `limit` and `offset` are strings. `phone_tools` also uses ranked retrieval; an empty tool query still browses schemas. A returned schema can be used directly with `phone_call`. Agents should search once for the relevant procedure, read the needed section and reuse contracts while the supplied toolCatalogueRevision fingerprint and access context remain current.

Trusted turn access filters writable tool documents before searching or reading them. Returned read-only schemas omit permission-prompt parameters. Forced index writes and permission prompts fail with `read_only_violation`; request arguments cannot relax that access. Read-only search may build its derived local cache, just as chat persists its transcript, but it does not mutate owner collections. External owner clients retain their own access. Documentation can describe write procedures without granting execution rights.
aliases: search engine documentation retrieval BM25 aliases fuzzy spelling correction full text offline SQLite collections

title: Offline search: Source and verification
text:
## Source and verification

The generic `search/LocalSearchIndex.kt` owns SQLite persistence, collection isolation, FTS retrieval, ranking and corrections. `DikcizSearch.kt` adapts it to the shared commands, protected datasets and trusted access. The engine has no documentation, MCP, chat or provider dependency.

Aliases are reviewed text in `app/src/dikciz/assets/search/aliases.json`. `make dikciz-search-docs` deterministically generates the bundled corpus from the current Markdown. Run it after changing documentation or aliases. `make dikciz-search-docs-check` rejects stale assets; normal lint and tooling CI include that check. `make dikciz-search-docs-test` checks generation. Live Android verification uses `make dikciz-test-existing-apk DIKCIZ_TEST_SELECTOR=test_local_search`.

See [MCP resources](mcp-resources.md), [shared control](automation-control.md), [embedded chat](embedded-chat.md) and the generated [command reference](command-reference.md).
