title: Shell sessions for every binding
text:
# Shell sessions for every binding

Shell sessions expose incremental output through ordinary HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua commands. They reuse the same process-group runner as shellStream. They continue across client disconnects and launcher recreation within the same process. App process death ends the session and its retained history.

title: Shell sessions for every binding: Start
text:
## Start

```json
{"type":"shellSessionStart","command":"printf first; sleep 1; printf second","root":false}
```

Root defaults to true, matching shell commands. Select root:false for the app sandbox. Android privileges and owner approval still apply. Start returns a streamId and current metadata; acceptance is not successful command execution. Read the terminal event for the actual outcome.

| Option | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| timeoutMilliseconds | 30000 | 0 through 2147483647; zero explicitly runs until stopped or process exit. |
| chunkBytes | 4096 | 1 through 65536. |
| bufferBytes | 1048576 | 65536 through 8388608; must fit twice chunkBytes plus 1024 metadata bytes. |
| maximumEvents | 1024 | 1 through 4096 retained events. |
| retentionMinutes | 60 | 1 through 1440 after completion. |

At most four sessions run concurrently. At most sixteen active/terminal records remain in the process, with a total reserved buffer budget of 32 MiB. Forget terminal records or wait for retention expiry to free capacity. Expired records are pruned when another session command runs.

title: Shell sessions for every binding: Read and reconnect
text:
## Read and reconnect

shellSessionRead requires streamId. Start cursor at zero. Optional limit is 1 through 200, default 50. Optional waitMilliseconds is 0 through 30000, default zero; it waits for another event or completion when caught up. Follow nextCursor until active is false and hasMore is false. Pages also respect the shared response-byte budget, so fewer than limit events can be returned.

Events preserve sequence, event kind and binary outputBase64. Decode each output event and concatenate its bytes in order. Do not concatenate independently decoded UTF-8 strings when a character can span chunks. Started, heartbeat and complete events are not output bytes.

Completed metadata and the complete event report state, exitCode and total outputBytes. A nonzero command exit remains a normal exited session with that exit code. Failed startup can include a specific code such as root unavailability. Inspect it rather than treating a successful read as successful execution.

The ring retains the newest bounded history. historyGap and lostEvents explicitly report a cursor older than retained data; firstSequence identifies the earliest available event. Never claim complete output after a gap. Increase start-time buffer/event limits or consume sooner. A cursor ahead of produced events is invalid. Retained reads are repeatable and do not consume history.

title: Shell sessions for every binding: Stop, inspect and release
text:
## Stop, inspect and release

shellSessionStop requests cancellation by streamId. Keep reading until active is false. Cancellation kills the owned process group using the existing runner and does not undo prior effects.

shellSessionsList pages metadata newest first with offset/limit, total and hasMore. It exposes no output contents. This can recover IDs after a transport reconnect.

shellSessionForget removes a terminal session and its retained output. It refuses an active session; stop and observe completion first. Unknown, expired or forgotten IDs return shell_session_not_found. IDs and data do not survive process death.

MCP names: dikciz_shell_session_start, dikciz_shell_session_read, dikciz_shell_sessions_list, dikciz_shell_session_stop and dikciz_shell_session_forget. HTML uses dikciz.command and Lua uses its ordinary command bridge. Existing connection-owned shellStream/SSE streaming remains available to network clients. See [shell and files](files-and-apks.md) and [durable jobs](command-jobs.md).

title: Recognition languages and models
text:
# Recognition languages and models

These operations inspect or prepare the installed Android recognition provider. They do not capture microphone audio. HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua use the same command target. Language support depends on the selected provider and recognition request.

title: Recognition languages and models: Language inventory
text:
## Language inventory

`speechLanguages` / `dikciz_speech_languages` requires Android 13 or later. Optional mode defaults to onDevice, with no system-provider fallback. Explicit system selects the installed system recognizer. Optional language is a BCP-47 tag, defaulting to device language.

The paginated result contains language and availability: installedOnDevice, pendingOnDevice, supportedOnDevice or online. The same language can occur in several categories. Limit defaults to 50, maximum 200; offset defaults to zero, maximum 1000000. Follow hasMore using the returned item count. Each page queries the provider again, so membership can change after model downloads or provider updates.

Timeout defaults to 30000 ms, range 1 through 120000. Unsupported provider queries and provider errors fail explicitly. No empty inventory is invented to hide a failed query.

title: Recognition languages and models: Model request
text:
## Model request

`speechModelDownload` / `dikciz_speech_model_download` requires Android 14 or later and a language. It uses the same mode and timeout options. This is an explicit request that may consume network data and cause Android/provider confirmation. It does not grant consent itself.

| Result state | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| available | The provider reported the model available. It may already have been installed. |
| scheduled | The provider scheduled work and ended observation. The model is not confirmed available. |
| failed | Startup or the provider failed. Inspect error. |
| unknown | Observation timed out or was interrupted. Provider work may continue. |

The command waits for a terminal callback or the selected deadline. Its response includes the process-owned sessionId, language, mode and provider progress when supplied. Use a durable job when the client cannot hold the request open.

title: Recognition languages and models: Observe progress
text:
## Observe progress

Call `speechModelStatus` / `dikciz_speech_model_status` from another connection while a model request is running. Without a sessionId it returns the latest request, including its ID. An optional sessionId refuses a different current request. States requested and downloading describe active observation; progressPercent is null until the provider reports progress.

A single support/model request owns the provider slot. A concurrent language query or model request returns hardware_busy. Cleanup releases that slot. The status is process-local and retains only the latest model request. It does not resume observation after a timeout, scheduled callback or process restart. Query speechLanguages again to verify later availability.

Android provides no cancellation guarantee for a provider model download. Closing the recognizer or cancelling a surrounding job ends Dikciz observation; it does not roll back network work. Never retry blindly after an unknown result.

Errors include speech_support_timeout, speech_model_timeout, speech_support_error_<Android code> and speech_model_error_<Android code>. A provider's insufficient-permissions callback uses the common permission-review flow. Platform version, installed provider and language support still apply.

See [recognition](speech-recognition.md), [durable jobs](command-jobs.md) and [command schemas](command-reference.md).

title: Speech recognition
text:
# Speech recognition

Speech recognition is microphone input converted to text. `speechSpeak` is separate text-to-speech output; `microphoneRecord` saves an audio file without transcribing it.

title: Speech recognition: Commands
text:
## Commands

| Command | MCP tool | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speechRecognitionStatus` | `dikciz_speech_recognition_status` | None. |
| `speechRecognize` | `dikciz_speech_recognize` | Optional `mode`, `language`, `timeoutMilliseconds`. |
| `speechRecognitionStop` | `dikciz_speech_recognition_stop` | None. |

All ordinary HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua calls share validation, Android access and results. The supplied Python client extends its response wait to cover the recognition deadline. Other clients must configure their own tool timeout accordingly.

title: Speech recognition: Availability and privacy
text:
## Availability and privacy

Check `recognitionAvailable` and `onDeviceAvailable` in status before starting. They report the installed Android recognition services, not a built-in Dikciz model. `listening` describes an active Dikciz recognition request. A language model may still be unavailable even when its service exists.

`mode` defaults to `onDevice`. This strictly uses Android's on-device recognition service and never falls back to the system network recognizer. It fails with `speech_on_device_unavailable` if unsupported. `mode: system` explicitly selects the installed default recognition service, which may send audio to its provider. Provider availability, connectivity and installed language models determine its behavior.

Open Dikciz before starting. Android microphone permission and foreground eligibility are required. Missing permission uses `native_permission_cameraAndMicrophone` and the common `permissionRequest`; use `autoRequestPermissions: true` for owner review, then explicitly retry. Recognition does not grant access or click Android consent automatically.

title: Speech recognition: Request and result
text:
## Request and result

`language` is an optional BCP-47 tag such as `en-US`; otherwise Android's current device language is used. `timeoutMilliseconds` defaults to 30000 and accepts 1 through 120000. A second concurrent request returns `hardware_busy`.

```json
{"type":"speechRecognize","mode":"onDevice","language":"en-US","timeoutMilliseconds":30000}
```

Successful completion returns `state: recognized`, `text`, `alternatives`, `confidence` and the requested `mode`. At most five alternatives are returned, each limited to 8192 characters. Confidence entries are numbers between zero and one when supplied by Android, otherwise null. Text is returned as data and is not executed or logged as a command.

Recognition is one utterance, not an always-listening assistant. This command does not transcribe an existing file or publish partial results. Use `speechRecognitionStop` from another connection to cancel. It returns `cancelled` after recognizer cleanup, or `idle` if nothing is active. The original recognition call returns `speech_cancelled`. Completion, errors and deadlines destroy the Android recognizer.

title: Speech recognition: Speech output controls
text:
## Speech output controls

`speechVoices` / `dikciz_speech_voices` lists the installed TTS engine's voices. Use `limit` and `offset`, follow `hasMore`, and inspect `total`. Each item has `name`, BCP-47 `language`, `networkRequired`, `quality` and `latency`. `defaultVoice` names the engine's current choice when available. Listing voices does not download a model or play audio.

`speechSpeak` accepts optional `voiceName`, `language`, `ratePercent` and `pitchPercent` alongside text and timeout. Defaults preserve the engine's voice selection with rate and pitch at 100 percent. Rate and pitch accept 25 through 400. An explicit voice takes precedence over language; choose a returned name. Network-required voices may send text to the engine provider. Unsupported language, missing voice and rejected configuration return distinct errors.

`speechStop` / `dikciz_speech_stop` stops active Dikciz output. It returns `cancelled`, or `idle` when no pending utterance exists; the original speak call returns `speech_cancelled`. A cancelled request may still be releasing its engine briefly, so wait for its result before starting another. Output completion is the Android engine callback, not acoustic proof that the speaker was audible.

title: Speech recognition: Saved speech audio
text:
## Saved speech audio

`speechSynthesize` / `dikciz_speech_synthesize` uses the same text, voice, language, rate, pitch and timeout fields as speechSpeak. It synthesizes a WAV without playing it and returns state=synthesized, path, sizeBytes and mimeType. Read the actual file through fileRead/download. speechStop also cancels synthesis. Incomplete files are removed after cancellation/failure; successful files remain until explicitly removed. Synthesis and spoken output share one active TTS owner.

title: Speech recognition: Errors
text:
## Errors

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `speech_on_device_unavailable`, `speech_service_unavailable` | No matching installed recognition service. |
| `speech_language_unsupported`, `speech_language_unavailable` | Language unsupported or model unavailable. |
| `speech_no_input`, `speech_no_match` | No speech or no recognized match. |
| `speech_audio_error`, `speech_client_error`, `speech_server_error`, `speech_server_disconnected`, `speech_too_many_requests` | Android recognizer failure. |
| `speech_network_error`, `speech_network_timeout` | System provider could not complete its network work. |
| `speech_timeout`, `speech_cancelled` | Dikciz deadline or explicit cancellation. |
| `speech_service_timeout`, `speech_cleanup_timeout` | Main-thread discovery or cleanup did not finish within five seconds. |
| `speech_start_failed`, `native_access_denied` | Android rejected startup. |
| `speech_android_error_<number>` | Additional Android provider error. |

Do not report recognized speech when the operation failed. A timed-out client connection is not proof the Android operation has stopped; inspect status or explicitly cancel it.

title: Speech recognition: Examples
text:
## Examples

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_speech_recognition_status --host phone.example --port 19002
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_speech_recognize --host phone.example --port 19002 --arguments '{"mode":"onDevice","language":"en-US"}'
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http speechRecognitionStop --host phone.example --port 19002
```

HTML uses `await dikciz.command("speechRecognize", {mode:"onDevice"})` after `dikciz-ready`. Lua uses `context.requestJson({type="speechRecognize",mode="onDevice"})` and reads the returned command envelope. Android access applies equally to both.

Reference: [Android SpeechRecognizer](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/SpeechRecognizer).

title: Speech recognition: Languages and recognition models
text:
## Languages and recognition models

Use speechLanguages for provider language inventory, speechModelDownload for an explicit download request and speechModelStatus for current progress. Android version and provider support apply. See [language and model management](speech-models.md) for pagination, consent, scheduled/available states and timeout behavior.

title: Speech recognition: Partial results and existing recordings
text:
## Partial results and existing recordings

Use speechStreamStart/Read/Stop for provider partial callbacks, or speechTranscribeFile for an explicit recording upload to a saved OpenAI-compatible transcription provider. See [the guide](visual-streams.md).

title: Starter home
text:
# Starter home

Fresh installations and **Reset Dikciz home** use four pages: Home, Tools, Device and Goblin. Customized homes survive APK updates; a still-pristine starter may refresh to the bundled layout. Reset replaces pages, restores matching bundled utility scripts and the 8-column, 6-row grid, and preserves unrelated saved scripts and policies.

Every HTML widget owns its complete HTML, CSS, JavaScript, state and files. Long press its content or handle to edit, resize, move, change appearance or delete it. Removing one widget preserves its neighbors and removes its own files beneath `/sdcard/Dikciz/pages/<page-id>/widgets/<widget-id>/`. Library templates create independent copies.
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Home
text:
## Home

**Time and weather** occupies two rows. It shows local time, date, city and temperature. Expand **Weather details and city** for feels-like temperature, wind, rain probability, low/high, European AQI and city controls. It tries already-permitted phone location when no city is saved. Missing access stays inline until you tap **Use my location**. Grant access, then tap again. A manual city takes precedence. Device locations are checked again after five minutes while visible.

City search sends the name to Open-Meteo; weather and air-quality requests send coordinates. The services load independently, retain dated successful readings on failure and refresh missing or fifteen-minute-old readings when opened. Requests time out after fifteen seconds and accept at most 64 KiB each. There is no hidden-page polling. Calendar, recordings and device metrics are not sent.

Attribution: [Open-Meteo weather](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs), [geocoding](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/geocoding-api), and [CAMS ENSEMBLE air quality through Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/air-quality-api). Public endpoints are for personal, non-commercial use under the provider terms.

**Most used apps** occupies three rows and shows up to eight installed apps with Android icons. Optional Android Usage access lets it rank foreground time over seven days. Without access or recent history, it shows **Your apps**. Tap **Use app history**, allow access in Android and return. Usage ranking refreshes once a minute while visible and immediately on return to the widget. The document subscribes to Android package changes and removes an uninstalled app immediately, including during an in-flight icon request. Updated complete template copies establish their own packageChanged subscription without replacing other subscriptions. App icons use the same checked launch action as other entrypoints.

The final row contains native Phone, Camera and Android Settings shortcuts, then Obtainium, F-Droid or Play Store in that preference order. Dikciz resolves installed launchable activities and their real icons. Missing handlers leave their slot empty. These are ordinary movable and editable shortcuts on Home. Hold a native app or group still for one second, then drag to move it. Releasing after the hold opens its edit controls. Moving before that deadline cancels the hold and cannot group icons.

**Flash attack** requests eight brief torch pulses. Tap again to stop. Each on request has a native 250-millisecond off timer independent of JavaScript; leaving the page also requests off. Camera access is requested only after a tap. Missing flash hardware produces an explicit error. **Dikciz time** speaks its demonstration line through Android text-to-speech at the current speaker volume. Neither action starts automatically. Speech is not a cellular call.
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Tools
text:
## Tools

**Agenda** occupies three rows. It shows the next Android alarm and up to three upcoming calendar occurrences in the current seven-day window. Android expands recurring events. All-day dates retain their calendar date. Calendar data stays on the phone. Tap **Allow calendar access**, return from Android and tap **Refresh agenda**. The document refreshes once a minute while visible and when reopened. Its bounded preview scans up to ten pages of fifty occurrences and directs you to Calendar when more remain. **Open calendar** and **Open alarms** request Android activities. Missing handlers produce an explicit error. The widget never changes events or alarms.

**Voice notes** occupies three rows. Recording starts only when you tap **Record voice note**. If access is missing, review it and tap Record again. Tap **Stop and save** to finalize an AAC M4A. Recording has a five-minute maximum and stops when the page becomes hidden. This is foreground microphone capture. Android interruptions report failure rather than claiming a saved recording.

Completed audio moves into this widget's directory with generated filenames. The five most recent recordings have playback buttons; earlier files and metadata remain. **Stop playback** releases playback. A failed move or metadata save leaves **Retry saving** available. Saved notes survive reopening; removing the widget deletes them. Copy recordings elsewhere before removing the widget to keep them. Active recorder sessions do not survive process death.
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Device
text:
## Device

**Device status** fills its page with a battery ring, temperature and voltage, network state, RAM/storage meters, bounded CPU history and individual core tiles. It refreshes every five seconds while visible or when you tap refresh. Storage describes the filesystem holding Dikciz app data. Network presence does not guarantee working internet. It starts no sensor listeners and requests no root access.

The chart measures this Dikciz process as a percentage of available processor capacity. It excludes other apps and separate WebView renderer processes. Android can protect whole-phone CPU counters and clock files; a runtime permission cannot unlock them. Protected values stay unknown. Where exposed, core tiles show measured utilization or a clock frequency labeled in MHz or GHz. Clock speed is not a guessed utilization percentage.
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Goblin
text:
## Goblin

**Goblin control** is a complete editable WebView. **Say the thing** speaks "Peen goes in vageen." The three preview voices demonstrate the London, heat and speed announcements without enabling their scripts. **Alien transmission** synthesizes a quiet, finite 2.4-second sound locally through Web Audio; it downloads no audio. **Flash attack** submits eight 250-millisecond torch pulses with native off timers. All effects start on a tap and use the current media volume. Leaving the page requests sound/light cleanup. **Stop this widget** stops its effects, cancels its weather request and disables its weather watch. Independently enabled Lua scripts must be disabled in Settings, Scripts.

**Check outside** requests permitted phone location and sends coordinates to [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs) for outdoor air temperature in Celsius. Battery temperature is never used. A checked weather-watch box repeats this at most every fifteen minutes while the widget is visible. No background weather fetch runs after leaving the page. Requests time out after fifteen seconds, accept at most 64 KiB and reject readings older than one hour. Successful readings retain their check time and emit `goblin.weather`; the heat script reacts only when separately enabled. Multiple copies have independent saved weather/watch state.

London and speed run from native location events when their scripts and precise Android location access are enabled, including while the widget is hidden. Their units and accuracy come from [Android Location](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/location/Location). They do not bypass Android background-location or service restrictions. The London rule is a radius around 51.5074, -0.1278, not an administrative city boundary. Edit the Lua constants and phrases to customize triggers. Stored latches and timestamps suppress repeats across restarts. Speech failures remain visible in script status and are not marked spoken.
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Optional complete templates
text:
## Optional complete templates

Previously placed documents and existing public library packages keep their saved source during APK updates. Reset the bundled home or update a document with the new package source to adopt widget-script fixes.

The picker includes all six starter documents with fresh independent state. The combined **Home dashboard**, app search, notes, detailed **System dashboard**, **Live sensors**, and **BTC and economic news** remain optional. Adding a template copies its entire document. **Save to library** makes a customized document reusable. Library edits never silently change placed widgets. Reduced-motion settings and visibility control optional visual effects.

The sensor template samples real hardware while visible. Markets and news fetch on explicit Refresh, retain dated successful data and report provider failures. See [HTML editing](user-guide.md#edit-an-html-widget), [configuration](dikciz-configuration.md) and [API coverage](capability-coverage.md).
aliases: default home starter templates reusable widgets voice notes agenda weather device goblin

title: Starter home: Optional Lua utilities
text:
## Optional Lua utilities

Six examples start disabled. Review them in **Settings**, **Scripts** before enabling them. Policies and subscriptions are prepared. The heat example consumes the Goblin widget's weather events; the GPS examples use native location events.

| Script | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `low-battery` | One notification at 20 percent or lower while discharging. Charging or reaching 30 percent resets it. |
| `charge-ready` | One notification at 80 percent or higher while charging. Unplugging or dropping below 75 percent resets it. |
| `screen-lock` | Explicit manual lock with owner-enabled Device Administration. Granting access never triggers it. |
| `goblin-london` | With a precise GPS fix accurate to 500 metres, entering 20 km of central London says "God save the Queen! The goblin has arrived in London." Leaving 25 km rearms it; a six-hour cooldown prevents rapid reentry chatter. |
| `goblin-heat` | Fresh `goblin.weather` readings above 35 Celsius say "It's hotter than Satan's armpit. The goblin is being slow cooked!" Below 32 Celsius rearms it; the cooldown is 30 minutes. |
| `goblin-speed` | Precise GPS speed above 80 km/h, with accuracy within 100 metres, says "Slow down! Your shit is about to come out of your arse!" Below 65 km/h rearms it; the cooldown is 15 minutes. |

Notification reminders need Android notification permission. Add a native script dashboard from the picker when wanted. See [Lua scripting](scripting-tutorial.md).

title: Starter home: Complete bundled widget catalog
text:
## Complete bundled widget catalog

Choose these by name in the Dikciz widget picker. Each library insertion copies the entire HTML, CSS and JavaScript document with independent saved state; editing one copy does not change the others. The first six documents are placed on the bundled pages. Native app shortcuts, Android provider widgets and the Lua script dashboard remain separate picker choices.

| **Time and weather** (`time-weather`) | Clock, location or manual-city weather, air quality and saved readings. Home. |

| **Agenda** (`agenda`) | Read-only calendar preview, next Android alarm and calendar/alarm shortcuts. Tools. |
| **Voice notes** (`voice-notes`) | Tap to record, stop/save and replay widget-owned voice notes. Tools. |
| **Device status** (`device-status`) | Live battery, memory, storage and process/per-core CPU display where Android permits it. Device. |
| **Goblin control** (`goblin-console`) | Manual speech, local alien sound, timed torch pulses, weather checks and optional weather watch. Goblin. |
| **Home dashboard** (`home-dashboard`) | Full-page clock, app search with Android icons and saved note. |
| **System dashboard** (`system-dashboard`) | Detailed full-page battery, memory, storage and CPU data with explicit restricted counters. |
| **Live sensors** (`sensors-dashboard`) | Visible-page readings from accessible hardware sensors, with accuracy and unavailable states. |

| **Find an app** (`quick-apps`) | Search installed apps and launch a selected result. |
| **Quick note** (`quick-note`) | Save a short editable note on this widget. |

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS
text:
# Build a todo app that reacts to GPS

Build one complete Dikciz app with a checklist, a JavaScript backend and saved state. Its **Go to New York** item checks itself when an accurate location fix enters an example destination circle. The backend keeps listening after you close its interface.

The working reference ships as **Dikciz > Apps > Travel todo**. Its [five source files](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/) are also in this repository. It starts with location monitoring off. No API key, model, messages or calendar writes are involved.


The captures come from the current development build on a private Android emulator. Its location was moved from London to New York through the emulator location fixture. The real Android location callback, native geofence, shared event bus, app backend and persisted state handled the change. This is not a physical trip or a synthetic geofence event.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    GPS[Android location] --> Fence[Native geofence]
    Fence --> Event[geofence.enter]
    Event --> Backend[main.js]
    Button[UI action] --> Request[customAppEvent]
    Request --> Backend
    Backend --> State[state.json]
    State --> UI[ui.js redraw]
```

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 1. Open the reference
text:
## 1. Open the reference

Open **Dikciz > Apps > Travel todo**. Check a task manually or scroll down to add your own. The initial list has **Go to New York**, **Pack my bag** and **Charge my phone**. You can use the list with location access denied.

To inspect the source, choose **Apps**, then **Edit bundle** beside Travel todo. The editor exposes the manifest, HTML, CSS, UI JavaScript and backend source together. Stop an active location watch before editing. Saving preserves whether the app is running or stopped. Open it directly, or choose **Start app** to resume a stopped backend.

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 2. Understand the five files
text:
## 2. Understand the five files

| Source | Job |
| --- | --- |
| [app.json](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/app.json) | Identity, command declarations and event subscriptions. |
| [ui.html](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/ui.html) | Checklist, destination card, task input and explicit location controls. |
| [ui.css](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/ui.css) | The complete document's layout and appearance. |
| [ui.js](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/ui.js) | DOM listeners, bridge requests and redraws when state changes. |
| [main.js](../app/src/dikciz/assets/apps/travel-todo/main.js) | Headless task operations, geofence setup, event matching and cleanup. |

Dikciz installs editable copies at `/sdcard/Dikciz/apps/travel-todo/`. It writes `state.json` there and reserves `files/` for app-owned data. App state is independent of home pages and widgets. Globals reset for each backend call, so keep durable values in state.

The manifest subscribes to two inputs:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "id": "travel-todo",
  "title": "Travel todo",
  "description": "A checklist that reacts to GPS and custom events.",
  "language": "javascript",
  "commands": ["geofenceSave", "geofenceDelete", "requestDeviceAccess"],
  "events": ["geofence.enter", "example.todo.complete"]
}
```

The example uses `geofenceSave`, `geofenceDelete` and `requestDeviceAccess`. Its legacy `commands` metadata does not restrict access. All apps share Dikciz's Android grants; the host supplies app-local state/event bindings. Android must grant location to Dikciz before it can monitor a destination.

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 3. Send UI actions to the backend
Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 4. Set up the GPS rule
text:
## 4. Set up the GPS rule

Choose **Review location access**, grant precise foreground location in Android and enable the device's location setting. Allow Dikciz notifications in Android so background monitoring has a visible notification. Return to the app and press **Watch New York**. Starting the rule is an explicit action, separate from opening or enabling the app.

The backend calls `geofenceSave` with these values:

```json
{
  "id": "travel-todo-nyc",
  "title": "Travel todo: New York",
  "latitude": 40.7128,
  "longitude": -74.0060,
  "radiusMeters": 20000,
  "enabled": true
}
```

The 20 km circle around Lower Manhattan is an example destination, not the legal boundary of New York City. Change the coordinates and radius in `NEW_YORK` inside `main.js` for another destination. The fence ID derives from `context.scriptId`, so independent copies use independent fences.

Android supplies location callbacks to the native geofence host. Dikciz rejects stale or inaccurate fixes and uses crossing hysteresis. A fresh inside fix, including the first accepted fix when you are already inside, produces `geofence.enter` with `payload.id`, `payload.title` and `payload.location`.

The backend ignores unrelated fence IDs and inactive watches. On a match, it deletes its fence, sets the `new-york` task's `done` value to `true` and saves the list. Other tasks stay unchanged. Repeated events do not rearm the watch. Close the app, arrive, then reopen it to see the persisted result. Android can delay callbacks or stop background work; this is an automation example, not guaranteed arrival detection.

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 5. Trigger another task with a custom event
Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: 6. Copy, stop and extend it
text:
## 6. Copy, stop and extend it

Press **Stop watching** to delete this app's fence. Arrival stops it automatically. Disabling or removing the app invokes its `app.stopped` backend cleanup; that also deletes its own fence while leaving unrelated fences alone. Stop monitoring before editing or replacing its source. Native geofences are separate persisted records, so inspect **Safety, journeys and devices > Places** if you edited away the cleanup code.

Choose **Export reusable bundle** to share the five source files. Exports exclude private state and recordings. To make an independent copy, install the source with a new `app.json` ID, then open it. The new ID gets separate state and an independent fence. Existing bundled copies preserve user edits during APK updates; a home reset does not restore edited app source. Current encrypted home/chat backups exclude custom apps.

To use Lua for background logic, change the manifest language to `lua`, provide `main.lua` with `on_event(event)` and keep the same interface files. For standalone background scripts without an app UI, read [background JavaScript](background-javascript.md) and the [Lua/event tutorial](scripting-tutorial.md). The [custom-app guide](custom-apps.md) owns host permissions, timers, alerts, archives and recovery.

title: Build a todo app that reacts to GPS: Verify the example in development
text:
## Verify the example in development

From the repository root, use the pinned Android Lab image through Make:

```bash
make build
make dikciz-test-existing-apk DIKCIZ_TEST_SELECTOR=test_travel_todo
make dikciz-test-stop
```

The focused cases exercise all three transports, invalid tasks, custom-event delivery, real emulator GPS with the UI closed, saved state and geofence cleanup. Captures remain under `.android-lab/shared/artifacts/travel-todo-guide/`. The test uses the private emulator, not a connected physical phone.

title: Dikciz tutorial
text:
# Dikciz tutorial

Build a home you can edit, connect an AI that can use the phone, and make HTML widgets, Lua or headless JavaScript scripts and complete custom apps react to events. This walkthrough starts with the signed APK and ends with direct Android SDK discovery. Follow it in order for a new installation, or jump to the part you need.

The examples inspect state and use a local custom-event pipeline. Messaging, calls, recordings and device changes have separate opt-in exercises. Exact accepted fields belong to the installed tool schemas and the [command reference](command-reference.md).

Screenshots use a private Android emulator. The starter, native walkthrough and custom-app captures are refreshed from the current development build; older command-result and provider captures illustrate their unchanged contracts. The populated starter uses a configured London location, live weather, sample calendar entries and an emulator recording. Chat replies and model lists use a local demonstration API with example model names; the native chat, database and phone tools are real. Provider forms also show the built-in OpenAI and Anthropic host templates. Command-result screens use a temporary HTML inspector to display actual API responses. Click an image for the full capture.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 1. Install and grant access
text:
## 1. Install and grant access

Download the signed APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher/releases/latest). For ongoing updates, add `https://github.com/psyb0t/dikciz-launcher` to [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium). Open Dikciz, choose it as the Android Home app, tap **Grant file access**, allow the requested shared-storage access and return.

Dikciz creates `/sdcard/Dikciz/`. The public home is editable files: root configuration, pages, widget documents and state, scripts, automation policies, libraries, themes and logs. Chat history and provider keys live separately in private app storage.

Open **Settings**, **Automation**, **Set up full device access**. This is a screen you can return to after Android opens another settings screen. Grant the capabilities you intend to use. For cross-app reading and control, enable **Dikciz cross-app automation** in Android Accessibility settings. For most-used app ranking, allow usage access. Location, contacts, notifications, camera and microphone have their own grants.

A permission is not the same as a role, special access or hardware support. Dikciz does not need to become your default SMS app. The [Android access guide](android-access.md) maps each feature to its actual requirements.

**Check:** press Home. Dikciz opens and the starter pages render. Return from an Android permission screen and continue setup without starting the sequence again.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 2. Explore the starter home
text:
## 2. Explore the starter home

The bundled home has four pages. Some data needs a grant or an explicit refresh; missing values stay unknown instead of being invented.

| Page | Try this | What it demonstrates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | Read the clock/weather, open an app icon and try a quick action | Time and weather, usage-ranked app icons and a native dock for Phone, Camera, Settings and an installed app store when available |
| Tools | Inspect the agenda and deliberately record a short voice note | Calendar access and a saved recording with its own widget state |
| Device | Read the battery ring, RAM/storage meters and CPU history | Live Android measurements with explicit limits for protected system counters |
| Goblin | Tap speech, alien sound or finite torch pulses, then stop them | JavaScript driving native tools and local audio from an editable document |

Weather can use permitted phone location when no city is set. Check the age and error state of fetched data. Whole-phone CPU counters may be protected even when ordinary permissions are granted; CPU frequency is not CPU utilization.

The library includes nineteen complete HTML templates, including Live sensors, BTC and economic news, app search, notes and combined dashboards. Six Lua examples start disabled: low-battery and charging reminders, lock-on-demand, and the London, heat and speed rules. The [starter catalog](starter-home.md) describes every template, trigger, data source and cleanup behavior.

**Check:** visit all four pages. Try one manual Goblin effect and stop it. Do not enable background rules until you have reviewed their source and triggers.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 3. Build and customize a page
text:
## 3. Build and customize a page

Tap the Dikciz mark beside the page rail to reach page controls, the app drawer, widgets and Settings. Pages occupy a two-axis map and have stable IDs as well as readable addresses such as `1H1V`. Use the page search control to find one by name or address.

Create a spare page for experiments. Open **Add to this page**. The **Dikciz** category lists complete HTML templates with descriptions. Add **Quick note**, edit it, then add a second copy. Change each note independently.

A template copies the whole HTML, CSS and JavaScript document. Each placed copy keeps independent state. **Save to library** makes the customized source reusable; it does not copy live widget state, and later library changes do not silently overwrite placed copies. An **Empty HTML widget** starts a document from scratch.

Long press the move handle, HTML content or background for the same whole-widget controls. **Edit** exposes the complete HTML, CSS, JavaScript and JSON state. Change an inner section by editing its markup and code. **Delete** removes the entire WebView and its scoped state, never just the DOM section under your finger. See the [HTML editing walkthrough](user-guide.md#edit-an-html-widget).

In **Appearance**, open **Border**, **Widths**, and set **All sides** to 0 to remove the native outline. Set individual edges to 0 too if the widget or theme overrides them. A border drawn by your own HTML must be removed in its CSS. WebViews hide native and CSS scrollbars while preserving scrolling; your document controls overflow and layout.

Saved widget files belong to the exact page/widget instance, so two copies can keep different notes or settings across workspaces. Removing a widget removes its scoped state. Save reusable source or export wanted data before removing an instance. Use stable widget IDs and `selfWidget` in code instead of screen pixels.

Add native app shortcuts or Android provider widgets through the same page controls. Hold an app icon for at least one second to arm dragging; an earlier swipe does not move it. Changing the global grid can shrink full-width widgets and reflow others. Read `evictedWidgets` when changing it programmatically: items that cannot fit are removed from the layout, with their scoped state. Evicting an app shortcut does not uninstall the app.

**Check:** your two notes differ after leaving and returning to the page. Edit one document and confirm the other stays unchanged. See [configuration](dikciz-configuration.md) for the file layout, grid, locks, themes, wallpaper and validation.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 4. Connect the on-device assistant
text:
## 4. Connect the on-device assistant

Tap the cheese beside the launcher controls. The chat opens as a half-screen panel; expand it when you need more room.

1. Open the header gear and **Add provider**.
2. Choose **OpenAI**, **Anthropic** or **Custom**. The first two fill the standard host and protocol. Custom accepts your own compatible base URL.
3. Enter the API key and save. Keys are stored separately with Android Keystore encryption and omitted from reads.
4. Create a conversation using that provider. Choose **Chat model** from the API-backed list; refresh it when needed. If discovery cannot list a private model, enter its exact ID under **Tune**.
5. Review the context size, maximum output, reasoning and access setting for this conversation. Several conversations can share one provider connection while using different models and budgets.

The current OpenAI-compatible protocol is streaming Chat Completions; Anthropic-compatible uses streaming Messages. A provider template does not make every model or API feature compatible. Read [provider settings](embedded-chat.md#connect-a-provider) before choosing an endpoint that only supports another protocol.

Known model metadata can fill token limits. Unknown models need manual values. Maximum output is both the provider response cap and a reserve subtracted from total context alongside the safety margin. Choose `drop-oldest` to omit older complete exchanges from outgoing requests, or `summarize` to replace an older prefix with a saved summary. Both keep the full local transcript.

Start with **Read-only phone access** enabled in model settings. Ask the assistant to inspect battery state and explain the result. Read-only mode hides write tools and independently blocks direct write calls in the executor. A model cannot bypass it with an argument. Permission prompts, app launches, shell commands and messaging are writes, so arrange needed grants yourself before this exercise.

For a separate writable exercise, disable read-only while idle and use **Make me a widget** on the spare page. Describe a small note or status widget. Inspect the resulting document and tool results; generation can fail or leave a partial result. **Explain this screen** hides chat, captures the display and accessibility tree, and sends them to an image-capable model. That turn is read-only even in a writable conversation, without changing its saved access setting.

Chat streams Markdown. Scroll up to inspect earlier messages; use **Latest** to resume following output. Hidden work appears in a progress notification. Tap it to return to the exact conversation, or use **Stop** to cancel active and queued work. Completed phone actions remain completed. The quiet **Open chat** notification opens the panel over another app when Android access and notification settings permit it.

An event rule can wake a conversation while chat is closed. Configure one only after testing its trigger and instructions. It can make paid API requests. Stopping a turn does not disable its event rules; clear those separately.

**Check:** send a follow-up question that depends on the previous reply. Confirm continuity, inspect a tool result, then test Stop during a new turn. The [chat guide](embedded-chat.md) covers failures, context recovery, conversations and event rules.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 5. Connect without USB
text:
## 5. Connect without USB

Use a reachable private network or Tailscale connection between the controlling computer and phone. Run the client on that computer. Its `127.0.0.1` refers to itself, not the phone.

On the phone:

1. Open **Settings**, **Automation**, **Configure remote bearer authentication**. Set and enable a password.
2. Open **Configure control ports**. Set **Listen address** to `0.0.0.0` for direct IPv4 access and save. The default `127.0.0.1` accepts only phone-local or forwarded connections.
3. Allow computer-to-phone TCP traffic on the chosen ports. Defaults are WebSocket `19001` and MCP/HTTP `19002`.

Listener configuration lives in `control/ports.json` under the public home. Valid address/port changes restart the listeners automatically, including while another app is foreground. `0.0.0.0` is a bind address; clients connect to the actual phone hostname or IP. The listeners supply no TLS themselves, so use a trusted private network or encrypted VPN. Tailscale ping alone does not prove the application ports are reachable.

From a checkout on the controlling computer, load the password into `DIKCIZ_REMOTE_BEARER_TOKEN` through your secret environment. Keep it outside tracked files and command arguments. Replace `phone.example` below with the reachable phone address.

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py websocket controlStatus --host phone.example --port 19001 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http deviceInfo --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp-tools --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py mcp dikciz_snapshot --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty
```

| Entrypoint | Address | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP | `http://phone.example:19002/mcp` | Tool discovery, typed calls and short documentation resources for agents |
| HTTP | `http://phone.example:19002/v1/automation` | Individual JSON commands and ordinary client integrations |
| WebSocket | `ws://phone.example:19001/v1/automation` | Persistent commands and live events |
| HTML, Lua and JavaScript | Local native bridge | Visible widgets and background event scripts |

These bindings share validation, execution, Android access and outcome semantics. Transport envelopes differ. Discover current names and required arguments instead of guessing their spelling. Search a task with `dikciz_search_query` in collection `docs`, then read the relevant result URI. Collection `tools` returns installed input schemas. The embedded agent exposes `phone_search` directly and uses the same ranked engine for tool discovery. `searchIndex` can also index explicitly supplied owner text in separate persistent collections. See [offline search](search.md) for aliases, spelling correction, pagination and read-only behavior. MCP browsing still starts at `dikciz://docs/index`.

A writable call can opt into owner review with `autoRequestPermissions: true`. For a direct review request, discover `requestDeviceAccess` or MCP `dikciz_request_device_access` and choose the required capability. Read the returned status, review-delivery result and instructions. The user still approves in Android; a review request is not a grant or completed action. Read-only conversations cannot request these prompts.

**Check:** inspect the serving package and version through `deviceInfo`, then read a snapshot over MCP. Both must describe the intended installed instance. Continue with [connection troubleshooting](automation-control.md#connect-without-usb) or [agent setup](agent-integrations.md) if discovery fails.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 6. Build an event pipeline
text:
## 6. Build an event pipeline

Start with [Build a todo app that reacts to GPS](todo-app-tutorial.md) for the shortest complete app example. **Dikciz > Apps > Travel todo** contains all five editable source files. Its explicit **Watch New York** action creates a native geofence, and its background JavaScript checks off the destination after the matching event. The same list accepts a custom event for another task. The walkthrough covers permissions, source editing, independent copies and stopping monitoring.


For separate widgets and background scripts, continue with the Lua example below. [Headless JavaScript](background-javascript.md) is a second standalone script backend with the same policies, events and command access.

Use the complete [custom-event exercise](scripting-tutorial.md#build-a-complete-custom-event-workflow) to connect your spare HTML widget to a Lua script:

```text
HTML button -> example.pipeline.request -> Lua -> saved widget state
                                              -> example.pipeline.done -> visible HTML update
```

That exercise supplies the HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Lua, policy and subscription documents. Replace its sample target address with your actual widget address. Enable the script, its policy and its subscription, then press the button. Inspect the script log for both the state update and emitted result event.

The widget waits for `dikciz-ready` before using the bridge. It reads `selfWidget.state`, updates saved state through the bridge, and listens for `dikciz-state` without reloading the document. Custom events use the same bus as native sources. External clients can publish them too; discover the installed event-publishing command and its schema before calling it.

HTML receives subscribed events while its page is selected and its WebView exists. Lua and headless JavaScript handle enabled subscriptions in the background. Put work that must survive page changes in a background script or app backend, and visible rendering in JavaScript. Add interval limits and filters for noisy sources such as sensors, location or notifications.

After the custom pipeline works, inspect one of the disabled bundled Lua examples. Start with the low-battery rule before adapting a location or heat rule. Policies authorize script actions, but never grant Android permissions. Trusted script command access includes powerful file and shell operations; review the source before enabling it.

**Check:** publish a request, see the result in the widget and inspect the final script status. Leave and return to the page to verify saved state. Disable the test script/subscription when finished. The [event replay guide](event-replay.md) covers cursors, gaps and reconnecting clients.





The two-input screenshots use the [packaged event recipe](mcp-resources.md), which extends the one-button exercise above with separate start/stop inputs.
aliases: walkthrough getting started installation permissions chat automation scripting widgets

title: Dikciz tutorial: 7. Use Android data and hardware
text:
## 7. Use Android data and hardware

Discover the installed tools for the task, grant its access, call the read operation first and inspect the result. Prefer dedicated commands over screen tapping when a data API exists. For cross-app UI, use a fresh accessibility snapshot and its semantic node IDs; after navigation, read a fresh snapshot rather than reusing stale IDs.

| Task | Exercise and guide |
| --- | --- |
| Contacts and SIMs | Search contacts directly and inspect `simList`. Own numbers can remain unavailable even with the read-number grant. [Native data](native-device-control.md) |
| SMS and calls | For an intentional test, choose an owner-approved recipient and SIM, use tracked SMS with an idempotency key, then inspect sent/delivery status. Calls, call logs and carrier USSD have separate requirements. [Native data](native-device-control.md), [USSD](ussd-control.md) |
| Calendar and alarms | Read occurrences and the next alarm first. Contact/calendar mutations are separate explicit actions. [Native data](native-device-control.md#calendar-occurrences-and-next-alarm) |
| Notifications and media | Inspect active notifications or media sessions. Replying, dismissing, snoozing and playback changes are writes. [Notification management](notification-management.md), [native data](native-device-control.md) |
| Location and sensors | Get a fix with age/accuracy, enumerate actual sensors and subscribe only to needed samples. Stop streams after testing. [Location](location-services.md), [native hardware](native-device-control.md#sensors-camera-microphone-and-speech) |
| Camera | Deliberately capture one JPEG, inspect actual frame metadata and view the output. Bounded video has a separate lifecycle. [Camera](camera-control.md), [native hardware](native-device-control.md) |
| Microphone and sound | Record a short note, stop it, then play it. Live PCM is a managed stream with replay and an owner stop control. [Microphone streams](microphone-streams.md), [audio playback](audio-playback.md) |
| Speech | Speak a short test or recognize microphone speech. Check available recognition languages/models before assuming offline support. [Recognition](speech-recognition.md), [speech models](speech-models.md) |
| Torch, vibration and settings | Use one bounded effect and stop it. Settings changes need their corresponding access. [Hardware controls](hardware-controls.md) |
| Bluetooth | Enumerate, scan and inspect a chosen peer before pairing or starting RFCOMM/GATT work. Close connections afterward. [Bluetooth](bluetooth-control.md) |
| NFC | Present a tag and inspect discovery before a deliberate NDEF write or raw transaction. A bank card is not an unrestricted tag. [NFC](nfc-control.md) |
| USB and Wi-Fi | Request access to the intended peripheral or scan, inspect freshness/status and close transfers/sessions. [USB](usb-control.md), [Wi-Fi](wifi-control.md) |
| Other platform services | Consult declared coverage for Health Connect, inventories, administration and restricted paths. [Coverage](capability-coverage.md) |

**Check:** each result describes the source, freshness and actual outcome. A permission grant cannot create absent hardware or privileged Android access. Ordinary app access does not provide unrestricted cellular-call audio interception/injection, other apps private data or fastboot control.

title: Dikciz tutorial: 8. Manage files, installs and long-running work
text:
## 8. Manage files, installs and long-running work

Use file discovery to browse paths Android permits, then read or download a chosen file. Upload a small test document to a new path before trying an APK. Transfers expose explicit offsets and completion state; finish or cancel a session deliberately. The authentication hash and private credentials are protected from ordinary remote file access.

For APK updates, upload the standalone APK and request installation. Android owns install permission and confirmation. An accepted install request is not a completed update: inspect final installation status and the serving package/version after reconnecting. Release and debug packages are distinct apps; use the documented handoff procedure rather than uninstalling your active controller and assuming access will survive.

Shell commands default to a 30-second timeout with per-request options. Root is requested by default; set `root: false` for the app sandbox. Android shell is not a desktop Linux environment and app permissions still apply. Read stdout, stderr, exit status and any explicit output-limit marker. A truncated preview is not the full output. Use incremental shell sessions, command jobs or streaming where appropriate instead of raising every response limit.

For work that outlives one request, use a durable command job and retain its identity/idempotency key. Poll the recorded result or cancel the job. After interruption, inspect the outcome before retrying a side effect. Stream logs or shell output with cursors; stop and forget sessions when done. Logcat visibility follows Android privilege limits.

**Check:** download the test file and compare its contents. For an intentional command test, inspect the exit status, not just transport success. See [files, APKs and shell](files-and-apks.md), [shell sessions](shell-sessions.md), [jobs](command-jobs.md) and [update recovery](remote-device-control.md#recover-after-an-apk-update).
aliases: walkthrough getting started installation permissions chat automation scripting widgets

title: Dikciz tutorial: 9. Discover public Android SDK calls
text:
## 9. Discover public Android SDK calls

The generic SDK bridge covers exact public classes and signatures from a pinned API catalogue. Discovery is broader than permission to invoke a method. Prefer a dedicated native tool when it already expresses your task.

After the network checks, discover a battery overload and read it:

```bash
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http androidApiDiscover --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty \
  --arguments '{"className":"android.os.BatteryManager","query":"getIntProperty"}'
python3 scripts/dikciz-control.py http androidApiRead --host phone.example --port 19002 --pretty \
  --arguments '{"className":"android.os.BatteryManager","member":"getIntProperty(int)","target":"service:batterymanager","arguments":[4]}'
```

Property `4` is Android `BATTERY_PROPERTY_CAPACITY`. Compare its returned value with the dedicated battery state. For another method, inspect `bridgePermitted`, `runtimeAvailable`, exact positional types, permission annotations and pagination before calling. Supply `arguments`, including `[]` for a no-argument member; the bridge does not guess overloads.

`androidApiRead` permits only explicitly approved reads, even for writable callers. Writable invocation uses `androidApiInvoke` and requires an idempotency key. Object results use process-scoped handles. Page their contents with `androidApiObjects`; unregister/stop SDK sessions before releasing handles. Callbacks record events and can publish `android_api_callback` on the shared bus. A timeout can mean unknown completion, not cancellation.

**Check:** distinguish a method returning from a downstream Android operation completing. Catalogue presence proves neither hardware availability nor platform privilege. Read the [SDK guide](android-sdk.md) before constructors, callbacks, mutable methods or handle cleanup.
aliases: walkthrough getting started installation permissions chat automation scripting widgets

title: Dikciz tutorial: 10. Check results and recover
text:
## 10. Check results and recover

Read the response at the layer that owns the effect. These are different outcomes:

| Reply | What to verify next |
| --- | --- |
| App launch accepted | Observed foreground package or a fresh screenshot/tree |
| SMS submitted | Tracked sent/delivery status, including unsupported delivery evidence |
| APK install requested | Android confirmation, terminal install status and installed version |
| Permission review shown | Actual Android grant, then a deliberate retry |
| Agent turn queued | Conversation state, tool outcomes and final reply |
| SDK method returned | Any separate callback, session or external completion |

Daily UTC JSON Lines logs live under `/sdcard/Dikciz/logs/`. **Settings**, **Configure logging** selects DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR and retention. Defaults are INFO and seven days. Use DEBUG for investigation, inspect script/tool failures and keep sensitive phone data out of shared bug reports.

Valid home/configuration and asset edits reload automatically. Invalid input reports an error rather than making a working configuration proof of a valid new edit. If a widget breaks, edit that document or restore its saved source before resetting the home. APK updates preserve placed custom documents; a new bundled template does not overwrite an old placed copy automatically.

When updating, Dikciz reopens if it is default Home or has overlay access. If Android prevents it, tap **Dikciz updated** or open the app. Recheck device identity and listeners afterward. A home reset and chat-history deletion are separate operations; back up wanted public files and exports before any reset.

Finish an experiment by disabling its scripts and chat event rules, stopping recordings/streams/jobs/effects, unregistering SDK callbacks and restoring settings you changed. Closing a chat panel or leaving a page is not a universal undo.

For a specific failure, use the [documentation index](index.md), [command schemas](command-reference.md) and [capability coverage](capability-coverage.md). Report the installed version, operation, exact structured error and relevant redacted log lines.

title: Typed automation actions
text:
# Typed automation actions

Typed actions are separate from ordinary commands. HTML uses `dikciz.dispatch({actions})`; HTTP/WebSocket use `automationDispatch`; MCP uses `dikciz_automation_dispatch`. Network dispatch requires an existing HTML `sourceWidgetAddress`. Lua returns `{status="...",actions={...}}` from `on_event`. An enabled Lua policy must allow the event capability and each returned action's policy name.

A dispatch contains 1 through 8 actions. Lua may also return one action, an action array, status without actions, or nil. Unknown fields and unsupported values fail validation. Actions execute in order, but the array is not a transaction: inspect every outcome and retry only work that did not complete. An Android permission prompt never grants access or retries work.

title: Typed automation actions: Every action and its fields
text:
## Every action and its fields

Every record has `type`. Fields below are required unless marked optional. Most policy names match `type`; the volume exception is explicit.

| Type | Fields beyond type | Lua policy action | Effect and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selectPage` | `pageId` | `selectPage` | Select an existing stable page ID. |
| `patchWidget` | `widgetAddress`, `values` | `patchWidget` | Persist supported fields in another widget. See field limits below. |
| `patchState` | `values` object | `patchState` | Replace current script state in Lua; replace the source HTML widget's state in HTML/network dispatch. |
| `patchDom` | `widgetAddress`, `selector`, `values` | `patchDom` | Change rendered HTML without saving source. Selector is at most 512 characters. |
| `launchApp` | `component` | `launchApp` | Launch a flattened Android component. Inspect foreground verification separately from acceptance. |
| `appAction` | `component`, `action` | `appAction` | `launch`, `appInfo`, `uninstall` or `forceStop`; no `addShortcut` in typed actions. Force stop requires approved root. |
| `postNotification` | `title`, `text` | `postNotification` | Post a Dikciz notification subject to Android posting access. |
| `sendSms` | `recipient`, `body` | `sendSms` | Legacy submission-only SMS. Prefer the ordinary `smsSend` command for SIM choice, idempotency and receipts. |
| `explicitIntent` | `intentType`, `component`; optional `action` | `explicitIntent` | Explicit `activity` or `broadcast`. For data URIs and ordinary intent fields, use the `intent` command. |
| `emitEvent` | `event`, `payload` object; optional `coalescingKey` | `emitEvent` | Publish a valid custom event. Publication is not consumer completion. |
| `mediaControl` | `packageName`, `command`; conditional `positionMilliseconds` | `mediaControl` | Existing media session: `play`, `pause`, `playPause`, `skipNext`, `skipPrevious` or `seekTo`. Only `seekTo` requires and accepts integer position 0..86400000. Notification-listener access is required. |
| `setMediaVolume` | integer `levelPercent`, 0..100 | `mediaVolume` | Set Android's media stream volume, mapping the percentage to its discrete minimum/maximum indices. |
| `notificationControl` | `actionToken` | `notificationControl` | Invoke an unexpired plain action from `notificationsList`. Use `notificationManage` for inline reply, dismissal or snooze. |
| `lockDevice` | None | `lockDevice` | Lock with owner-enabled Device Administration. |
| `accessibilityAction` | `snapshotId`, `nodeId`, `action`; optional `text` | `accessibilityAction` | Act on a fresh Android Accessibility node; `setText` needs text. See the Accessibility guide for supported actions and freshness. |
| `accessibilityGesture` | `snapshotId`, `gesture`, `durationMilliseconds`; coordinates below | `accessibilityGesture` | `tap` needs `x`, `y`; `swipe` needs `startX`, `startY`, `endX`, `endY`. Coordinates are integer 0..10000; duration is integer 1..10000 ms. |
| `accessibilityGlobalAction` | `action` | `accessibilityGlobalAction` | `back`, `home`, `recents`, `notifications`, `quickSettings`, `lockScreen` or `takeScreenshot`. Android version and service access apply. |

title: Typed automation actions: Volume example
text:
## Volume example

The request's action type is `setMediaVolume`. The policy capability is `mediaVolume`, and result/log records can use that capability name. Do not use `mediaVolume` as an action type.

```json
{"sourceWidgetAddress":"1H1V-example-widget","actions":[{"type":"setMediaVolume","levelPercent":35}]}
```

Replace the address with an actual HTML widget. Pass these arguments to MCP dispatch, add `type: "automationDispatch"` for HTTP/WebSocket, or pass just the actions to the HTML dispatcher.

The corresponding Lua policy includes `"actions":["mediaVolume"]`, and its handler returns:

```lua
return {status="Volume requested",actions={{type="setMediaVolume",levelPercent=35}}}
```

Read `deviceState.mediaVolume` and `mediaVolumeMaximum` before and after changes. The percentage is rounded to a device volume step, not a measured sound level. Fixed-volume devices or a rejected read-back return an explicit refusal. Per-player `audioPlayback.volumePercent` is a separate gain control and does not replace the media-stream setting.

title: Typed automation actions: Widget fields and state
text:
## Widget fields and state

For an HTML target, JSON `patchWidget.values` supports `title`, `html`, `css`, `javascript`, `state`, `itemStates` and `eventSubscriptions`. The JSON parser also accepts `text` for compatible text targets. A single JSON patch accepts at most 6 fields. Target-specific validation, editing locks, configured text/document limits and state limits still apply. Layout is not a widget-patch field. `eventSubscriptions` replaces the complete array, accepts at most 128 entries, and uses the same subscription validation as saved configuration. Read the current list with `widgetGet` before preserving or extending it.

The Lua returned-action parser accepts at most 5 fields per `patchWidget` and does not accept `itemStates` or `eventSubscriptions`. It supports `title`, `text`, `html`, `css`, `javascript` and object `state` subject to the target. To use the JSON action contract from Lua, call ordinary `automationDispatch` through `context.request` with an actual HTML source address, or edit the saved widget record. These command calls have owner authority independently of the returned-action policy.

State patches replace the object rather than merge individual keys. Preserve existing keys when needed. JSON null is a saved value, not key deletion. Lua nil omits fields; use a JSON string through the command bridge when explicit null is needed. `patchDom.values` permits `text`, `html`, `value`, `className` and string-valued `attributes` (at most 16). A hidden/missing target or invalid selector is an explicit outcome. DOM changes disappear on rendering recreation; source or saved state changes persist.

Source edits can recreate the calling WebView. Wait for `dikciz-ready` before further bridge calls. Whole-widget native Delete removes owned files; DOM sections do not have independent native Delete menus.

title: Typed automation actions: Validation bounds
text:
## Validation bounds

The saved configuration supplies the text, title, component and identifier limits. Bundled defaults are 65536 text characters, 120 title characters, 512 component characters and 80 identifier characters; inspect configGet for the current values. Widget addresses use the configured identifier budget plus page-address overhead.

State/payload validation permits at most eight nesting levels and 128 entries in each object or array. Numbers must be finite. State keys use the identifier grammar: a letter followed by letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens. JSON string fields cannot contain NUL. DOM attribute names start with a letter and contain at most 64 ASCII letters, digits, colons, underscores or hyphens. Event names have their own 1..128-character grammar in the scripting tutorial.

Explicit intent action strings are at most 256 characters; media package names 255, media commands 32, notification tokens 36, and Accessibility snapshot/node IDs 128. The Accessibility runtime additionally enforces its 8192-character setText ceiling. Device support and target identity are checked separately from syntactic bounds.

title: Typed automation actions: Authority and verification
text:
## Authority and verification

Lua returned actions are policy-gated. Enabled Lua `context.request` and HTML command calls have owner command authority subject to Android access; the Lua action allowlist is not a sandbox for those calls. Network calls additionally enforce authentication and Origin policy.

Android acceptance, observed foreground launch, carrier delivery and audible/physical effects are different outcomes. Read `actions` results, script run status and the relevant operation's read-back. A queued trigger or an executed `emitEvent` proves neither the Lua handler nor its widget receiver completed. Use [event replay](event-replay.md) or persisted acknowledgements when reconnecting.

See [scripting](scripting-tutorial.md), [Android access](android-access.md), [Accessibility](automation-control.md#cross-app-android-ui) and the [ordinary command schemas](command-reference.md).

title: USB host control
text:
# USB host control

USB commands operate on peripherals attached to the Android phone acting as a USB host. They do not control the phone through its computer-facing ADB connection.

Use usbDevices to discover deviceId, permissionGranted and interface descriptors. Each interface reports its array index, ID, alternate setting, class/subclass and endpoints. Endpoint descriptors include address, direction, transfer type, maximum packet size and interval. Device IDs can change after reconnection.

title: USB host control: Owner access
text:
## Owner access

usbRequestAccess, MCP dikciz_usb_request_access, takes deviceId. It requests Android approval for that attached device and returns user_action_required, or granted if access already exists. Check the phone, review the dialog, then query usbDevices.permissionGranted and explicitly retry. Access expires on disconnect. Android may additionally require camera permission for a video-class USB device.

usbTransfer with missing access returns permission_required and permissionRequest identifying usbDevice and deviceId. autoRequestPermissions=true starts the same owner-review flow. It never silently grants access or retries a transaction.

title: USB host control: Transfer fields
text:
## Transfer fields

usbTransfer, MCP dikciz_usb_transfer, always requires deviceId and kind.

| Kind | Required fields |
| --- | --- |
| control | requestType (0..255), request (0..255), value (0..65535), index (0..65535). |
| bulk | interfaceIndex (0..255) and endpointAddress (0..255), from the discovered bulk endpoint. |

The requestType direction bit selects control input/output. The endpoint address selects bulk direction. Input requires length from 0 to 65536 and refuses dataBase64. Output requires dataBase64 with at most 65536 decoded bytes and refuses length. Unknown or action-inappropriate fields fail validation before USB work.

timeoutMilliseconds defaults to 30000 and accepts 1..120000. Successful completion returns bytesTransferred, deviceId, state=completed and Base64 input data, or null data for output. Zero transferred bytes is valid. A negative Android return becomes usb_transfer_failed; Android does not distinguish every timeout/detach failure here.

A bulk transfer claims its interface without forcing another driver to release it. A busy interface returns usb_interface_busy. Every opened connection is closed and a claimed interface is released on success or failure. Connections are scoped to one command; use a device-specific protocol appropriate to independent transfers.

Missing/detached identities return native_record_not_found. Missing host service returns native_unavailable. Failed writes can have partial external effects even when no successful byte count was returned. Inspect the peripheral before deciding whether a retry is safe. Android does not expose every USB host operation to ordinary applications, including arbitrary gadget/bootloader control.

These operations share schemas, execution and permission procedures across HTTP, WebSocket, MCP, HTML and Lua. See the [command reference](command-reference.md), [hardware inventory](hardware-controls.md) and [coverage](capability-coverage.md).

title: Dikciz user guide
text:
# Dikciz user guide

This guide starts after you have downloaded and installed a Dikciz APK on your Android phone. It covers using the launcher on the phone. Each screenshot follows the step beside it.

For a complete editable app, follow [Travel todo](todo-app-tutorial.md). For events, HTML widgets, Lua/JavaScript scripts, and typed actions, start with the [scripting tutorial](scripting-tutorial.md). Read [Dikciz configuration](dikciz-configuration.md) for the editable-file layout and [automation control](automation-control.md) for WebSocket, MCP, and remote-control commands.

Tap the cheese beside the launcher controls to open the [on-device assistant](embedded-chat.md). Configure its provider in chat Settings, create conversations, expand the panel or hide it while the agent works.

title: Dikciz user guide: Install Dikciz and make it your home screen
text:
## Install Dikciz and make it your home screen

1. Open the Dikciz APK from your browser, file manager, or Downloads app.
2. If Android asks, allow that app to install unknown apps, then accept Android's installation screen.
3. Open Dikciz. If Android asks which Home app to use, choose **Dikciz** and make it the default. If it does not ask, press the Home button and choose Dikciz there.
4. On a cold start, Dikciz shows its mark and five joke lines for five seconds. The bottom of this screen shows the running version and build type, such as release or debug. Tap anywhere to skip it.
5. The first Dikciz screen asks for shared-storage access. Tap **Grant file access**, enable access for Dikciz in the Android panel, then return to Dikciz.

That access lets Dikciz create and watch `/sdcard/Dikciz/`. It contains your pages, widgets, themes, scripts, packages, and logs. Dikciz cannot load or save your home until Android grants it.

The bundled home opens on `Home (1H1V)`. Its native bottom and right rails show the current horizontal and vertical page coordinates. Every page is a fixed grid. A full page rejects another native widget instead of making items overlap or extending the page below the screen.

![Bundled home](images/user-guide/01-first-launch.png)

If release and debug builds are installed together, Android lists them as **Dikciz** and **Dikciz (debug)**. Choose **Dikciz** as Home when using Obtainium releases. Updates replace only the matching package; updating release does not replace or restart the debug app.

After an APK update, Dikciz reopens automatically when it is the default Home app or has overlay access. If it stays closed, tap **Dikciz updated** in notifications or open the app. [Update recovery](remote-device-control.md#recover-after-an-apk-update) explains the required access and reconnecting remote clients.

title: Dikciz user guide: Move around the home
text:
## Move around the home

Apps opened from the drawer or a native shortcut run in their own Android task. Press Home to return to Dikciz, then use Android Recent apps to resume the app.
